[1423] The TECHNICAL-INDUSTRIAL AREA reform The aforementioned law of 28 December 1995, n. 549 established to "proceed with the restructuring of the Arsenals, Factories and Technical Centres, rationalizing their relative tasks through the optimization and concentration of production processes, including through mergers

[1424] The aforementioned precept was implemented with Legislative Decree No. 459 of 28 November 1997, which divided the Defence industrial area into two parts

[1425] the first included the bodies that were to be placed under the control of the FA Inspectorates, while the second included those that were under the control of the General Secretary

[1426] A subsequent Ministerial Decree dated 20 January 1998 identified the bodies reporting to the Army Logistics Inspectorate, the Navy Naval Support Inspectorate and the Secretary General

[1427] Essentially, the differences between the bodies under the control of the Armed Forces Inspectorates and those under the Secretary General consisted in the fact that the former were considered functional bodies for the use of the military instrument, while the latter belonged to a category destined for closure if, within two years, it was not possible to entrust them with the performance of any activity or if, for two consecutive years after the assignment of the activity and the adoption of the measures envisaged in the restructuring plan, they had not achieved the capacity to operate according to economic management criteria. The restructuring of the Defence was based on the criteria of reduction, rationalization and optimization of production processes, the regulation of the negotiated mobility of civilian employees, and the disposal of structures and buildings no longer usable

[1428] all with the aim of adapting the organization to the needs of the modern military instrument and the available resources

[1429] In this context, the industrial area (which concerns only the Army and Navy) has undergone a profound reform, aimed primarily at addressing the Armed Forces' actual technical and logistical support needs by identifying a limited and efficient number of Maintenance Centers, also meeting operational and strategic requirements. Meanwhile, the remaining factories/arsenals have been transferred to the Secretary General's area for an analysis of their production capacity, with a view to identifying other potential production sectors, with the aim of decommissioning them in the event of a negative outcome of the aforementioned analysis

[1430] This process, sanctioned by Legislative Decree No. 459 of 28 November 1997, resulted in the subdivision of military establishments into tables "A" (5 maintenance centers for the Army), "B" (3 arsenals and 1 joint missile maintenance center for the Navy), "C" (19 Army entities and 4 Navy entities), and "D" (including the technical centers and aircraft maintenance departments of the technical-operational area), as per Ministerial Decree No. 20.1.1998, implementing the aforementioned legislative decree

[1431] The establishments in Tables "A" and "B" have been transferred to the technical-operational area in application of the specific provision of the law on the reform of the leadership (Law of 18 February 1997, no. 25), which places the maintenance of the efficiency of the military instrument entrusted to them under the direct responsibility of the Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces

[1432] Therefore, the entities in question were placed under the control of the respective FA Logistics Inspectorates and subjected to a restructuring process, still underway, with the consequent adjustment of their staffing, with the aim of achieving maximum production efficiency

[1433] The Secretary General carries out the functions overriding the establishments/arsenals of Table "C" through the General Office for the Management of Technical-Industrial Area Entities (UGGEATI), which the Minister of Defense, pursuant to Legislative Decree 459/97, established by decree dated

[1434] UGGEATI, which took charge of the aforementioned entities as of November 1, 1999, carried out a preliminary investigation of the area, also with the help of an expert from the national industry selected by the Minister, aimed at acquiring a comprehensive picture of the plants' activities and the potential possibilities for their industrial reconversion

[1435] Furthermore, it ensured the day-to-day management of the entities in question, having taken over all the powers previously exercised by the general technical directorates

[1436] The aforementioned survey made it possible to identify establishments with concrete possibilities for rationalization and/or reconversion according to economically viable management criteria, to be implemented according to the procedure dictated by Legislative Decree 459/97, which provides for the following steps for each establishment: • assignment of a new mission, in whole or in part identical to the one performed, which can guarantee a secure outlet both in the Defense sector and on the market; • restructuring, which allows for the effective performance of the new mission and economically viable management

[1437] • control of economic management for two consecutive financial years

[1438] • closure of entities for which it is not possible to identify a new mission within two years of the entry into force of the legislative decree, or of those which have not achieved economically viable management for two consecutive financial years

[1439] • possible transformation into joint-stock companies of the reconverted and economically viable entities, which are destined to become non-Armed Forces industrial areas, with the task of operating both for the benefit of the CEO and in external sectors

[1440] From this perspective, in order to ensure that these latter bodies enjoy unified private management, the Defence Industries Agency was established (Article 22 of Legislative Decree 30.7.1999, no. 300), which must operate in compliance with the objective of economic management and the principles governing competition and the market

[1464] These are entities that produce goods and services in various fields, both for public administrations and, especially in the future, for private individuals

[1465] The ultimate goal of the organizations in question is to achieve, within a certain period of time, the ability to operate according to economic management criteria through the rationalization of activities, the numerical and qualitative definition of staff, a new organizational structure, and an opening to the commercial market

[1466] The Council of Ministers' decision to appoint a person with proven entrepreneurial experience to lead the Agency clearly demonstrates its desire to enhance the value of these institutions

[1467] There may even be areas that, with appropriate redevelopment and adequate entrepreneurial capacity, could become niches of excellence

[1468] The agency has the power to transform production units into joint-stock companies, exercising shareholder rights on behalf of the Treasury

[1469] To achieve its institutional goals, it may enter into agreements and arrangements with public and private entities for the supply or acquisition of goods or services, participate in consortia, including international ones, and participate in companies authorized by the Minister of Defense

[1470] Among the most significant innovations introduced by the founding decree is the provision of an agreement regulating the relationship between the agency itself and the supervising Minister

[1471] In fact, three-year agreements will be signed between the supervising Minister and the Agency, through its Director General, to define specific objectives and ensure the Minister's verification of the expected results

[1472] The Director General is also responsible for the organization and management of the Agency and its staff

[1473] The Director General himself is responsible for the achievement of the established objectives, as well as for the quality of the production processes and administrative procedures, and adopts the acts and provisions necessary for the functioning of the Agency

[1474] Publications Centre for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ The Agency is based in Rome, has legal personality under public law with activities subject to the rules of civil law

[1475] and is equipped with administrative, organizational, financial and accounting autonomy and has access to the assets of the various units necessary for managing its activities

[1477] • SM Production of ropes of Castellammare di Stabia

[1478] • Chemical Pharmaceutical Institute of Florence

[1490] In particular, the pursuit of economical management occurs through a reduction in costs and an increase in revenues

[1493] This will allow for a percentage increase in production costs compared to support and manufacturing costs, while simultaneously reducing overall costs through increased efficiency and a redefinition of the overall workforce

[1494] The improvement in production value occurs through: * an increase in volumes, a necessary objective resulting from the increase in production capacity, guaranteed by the existing order portfolio and that to be acquired on the military and civilian markets; * development and production of new product lines such as, for example: post-2000 hand grenades in Baiano (employment 35 people); or cartridges with the Capua plant to be immediately transferred to Fontana Liri (employment 60 people); * ability to penetrate the "institutional" market (Financial Police, Coast Guard, etc.) for the Castellammare plant and the civilian market for Castellammare (merchant market and various applications) and for Florence (production of health cosmetics and medicines for third parties); * interest of the Defence Administration in the Agency's current products and in new ones that can be developed

Finally, it should be emphasized that the Minister of Defense intends to transfer the Gaeta printing plant and the La Maddalena and Messina arsenals to the Agency's management by merging the latter two into a single operational unit

[1497] National industrial apparatus The defense industry represents one of the primary instruments through which each nation expresses its needs for security, sovereignty and technological and industrial independence

[1498] A nation's defensive and security potential, in fact, is measured on the basis of the operational capacity of its Armed Forces but also depends, to a significant extent, on the credibility and degree of autonomy and self-sufficiency of the corresponding industry

[1499] The defense industry is one of the three pillars on which security policy is based, together with foreign policy and military policy

[1500] has a positive impact on the trade balance of states

[1501] contributes to the creation and development of a high-level industrial, technological and employment network

[1502] To maintain these values, in recent years, following the changing global geostrategic balance, Italy has undertaken a profound restructuring, rationalization, and concentration of resources in areas of excellence, thus allowing the country to play an equal role with other European companies

[1503] Currently, the Italian defense industry includes private companies such as FIAT (vehicles, space, propulsion and electronics), MARCONI (electronics and communications), ELETTRONICA (electronic warfare), MACCHI (trainer aircraft), BERETTA (small and medium caliber weapons), INTERMARINE (shipbuilding) and state-owned companies such as FINMECCANICA (aerospace, helicopters, defense electronics, energy and transport) and FINCANTIERI (shipbuilding

[1504] It employs a total of 30,000 people, generates a turnover of €4.5 billion, 35% of which comes from exports, and meets approximately 80% of the country's defense needs

[1505] These companies have already completed their financial restructuring and industrial relaunch plans, concentrating all the sector's key expertise in-house (industrial hubs specializing in specific product lines) and streamlining and optimizing their corporate structures

[1506] The Public Administration, and therefore also the Ministry of Defense, encourages and supports this rationalization process to help protect those sectors of excellence possessed by the national industry, eliminating overlaps and duplications to the benefit of cost containment, clarity in the relationship with users and, ultimately, increased competitiveness in the market

[1507] A typical intervention tool is Law No. 237 of 19 July 1993, "Urgent interventions to support the economy," which allocates funding aimed at promoting the rationalization, restructuring, and reconversion of companies operating in the defense materials production sector

[1508] Other similar measures include Law No. 808 of December 24, 1985, "Measures for the Development and Increase of the Competitiveness of Industries Operating in the Aeronautics Sector," Law No. 644 of November 22, 1994, "Urgent Measures to Support the Economy," and Law No. 421 of August 8, 1996, "Urgent Provisions for Production Activities" for the technological development of the aeronautics sector; Law No. 266 of August 7, 1997, "Urgent Measures to Support the Economy" - which guarantees national participation in aeronautical programs related to air defense needs and implemented within the EU; and Law No. 140 of May 11, 1999, "Regulations on Production Activities," which promotes the development of the national high-tech industry

[1509] Having completed the internal industrial reorganization process, the national industry continues to take an active part in the European one, which is constantly evolving and is leading to the implementation of mergers and acquisitions aimed at creating transnational production hubs for each production sector, of a size and technological level such as to ensure their presence on the world arms market

[1510] Italy is fully engaged in this process following the agreements signed in April 2001 between Finmeccanica, EADS, and BAE Systems in the missile sector and those signed in June 2000 between Finmeccanica and EADS in the aeronautics sector. These agreements were preceded by the already operational agreements between Alenia and Marconi Systems in defense electronics and between Agusta and GKN in the helicopter sector. These alliances were also supported by broad government collaboration, and the Ministry of Defense, in particular, has established cooperation agreements aimed at achieving the synergies essential for strengthening the defense industry

[1511] This is an optimization process that involves, alongside industries, various ministries and sectors of the Public Administration in a coordinated effort to direct activities towards common objectives

[1512] This is an action carried out by the "Inter-Ministerial Committee for Research, Development and Production Activities Relating to Defense," established in 1984 by Interministerial Decree

[1513] Within the Committee, chaired by the Minister of Defense, representatives of the Public Administration (DEFENSE—ECONOMY and FINANCE - MAE - MAP - UCPMA - EDUCATION, UNIVERSITY and RESEARCH) meet with those of industry represented by the Association of Industries for Aerospace, Systems and Defense (AIAD), which brings together approximately 80 advanced-technology industries with approximately 50,000 employees

[1514] The Committee defines the guidelines for defense industrial policy, compares various needs with the country's actual capabilities, promotes export support, updates contractual procedures, and coordinates activities for national industries' participation in international tenders

[1515] In practice, government support for the defense industry is taking shape

[1516] International Co-production in the International Industrial Landscape The Italian Ministry of Defence is involved in numerous international cooperation activities, both multilateral and bilateral, with particular attention to Europe and North America

[1517] BILATERAL COOPERATION In the European multilateral context, the European Union's (EU) desire to create a European Security and Defence Identity has required collaboration to create a technological and industrial base aimed at enabling the creation of an integrated and interdependent industrial system at the European level, without which the greater operational autonomy sought would lose its concreteness and become unrealistic

[1518] On this basis, efforts have long been underway to promote the creation of a truly European defense industry, reducing protectionist barriers within EU countries and encouraging sectoral mergers between industries, in order to concentrate various national capabilities in high-quality production hubs

[1519] The initiatives aimed at creating a European armaments market are mainly the WEAG (Western European Armament Group), the OCCAR (Organisme Conjoint de Cooperation en matière d'Armament) and the LoI (Letter of Intent). WEAG (Western European Armaments Group) The WEAG was created in 1993 from the transfer of the functions of the IEPG (European Independent Programme Group) to the Western European Union (WEU

[1520] It consists of 19 member countries and operates as an informal consultation group in the field of armaments cooperation at the level of Defence Ministers

[1521] Its aim is to enable a more effective use of funds for research, development and procurement of military materials, increase the standardization and interoperability of armaments among member countries and strengthen Europe's political and industrial weight within NATO

[1522] The WEAG's decision-making activity takes place on a unanimous basis and consequently, given the large number of participating countries and the many different national interests to be considered, it has not led to concrete results, except for those - rather limited - in the sector of Research and Technology

[1523] The downsizing of the WEU and the absorption of its functions by the EU seem to mark the Group's life, but the need to have a political forum in Europe, led by the Defence Ministers, in which there is the possibility of discussing together and developing cooperative activities makes it essential, at least for the short/medium-term, to keep the Group active

[1524] The research organization that reports to Panel II of the WEAG currently constitutes the most efficient and consolidated instrument of intervention, at European level, in the sector of research of specific military interest

[1525] Panel II, of which Italy held the presidency until 31/12/2000, in Italy, France, Germany, Great Britain, Spain, Sweden, Finland, Austria, Greece, Belgium, the Netherlands, Portugal, Luxembourg, Denmark, Poland, Hungary, Rep

[1526] Czech Republic, Türkiye and Norway

[1527] NATO Board is the organization's oversight body that promotes, selects, and approves individual research projects

[1528] WEAG has a structure, the Research Cell, based in Brussels, specifically dedicated to the technical-administrative management of contracts that are awarded mainly to defense industries

[1529] WEAG research is essentially conducted in an industrial context, has an annual budget (which each country individually and differently allocates from its own budget) and provides for a financial participation from industry of around 50%

[1530] Projects are identified using a "top-down" (EUCLID MOU) or "bottom-up" procedure through the Eurofinder procedure, which requires the free and spontaneous submission of individual projects by industries and/or research institutions interested in conducting (and co-financing) them

[1531] Italy is currently participating in approximately 59 projects for a total financial commitment of around €90.6 million/year, of which €72.8 billion has already been financed

[1532] Some of the management rigidities inherent in the EUCLID MOU and the Eurofinder procedure, which required the WEAG countries to be completely open to each other regarding participation in each programme, have recently been overcome with the signing of the Europe MOU

[1533] This makes WEAG procedures extremely flexible and available for the technical-administrative management of any type of program that may be implemented under any institutional framework involving European countries. OCCAR (Joint Organization for Armament Collaboration) OCCAR (FR, GE, IT, UK) was established with the aim of rationalizing "demand" through a common policy on armaments procurement, in order to ensure interoperability between the respective Armed Forces and achieve economies of scale in the sector

[1534] From this perspective, the Organization's task is to coordinate, control and implement the armaments programmes assigned to it by its member states, thereby improving the effectiveness of the management of cooperative projects in terms of cost, time and performance

[1535] Having legal personality, which gives the Organization its own negotiating power (drafting contracts, hiring personnel, and conducting general negotiating activities), allows OCCAR to manage these programs completely independently, without having to resort to applying national procurement policy procedures

[1536] It therefore appears essential for Italy to carefully monitor and monitor OCCAR's activities, as do other member countries, which also involve the entire national defense industry

[1537] LoI (Letter of Intent

[1538] The same objective of seeking a common will to operate concretely is set in the Framework Agreement of the LoI (FR, GE, IT, SP, SE and UK), signed on 27 July 2000, aimed at rationalising the "offer" of European industry

[1539] The Agreement represents a fundamental step not only towards the creation of a European industrial base, but also towards the first concrete steps towards the creation of a common European arms market, the harmonization of military requirements, the definition of common export rules, and coordinated research and development

[1540] Technological research also plays a central role in the recently signed treaty between the six major European countries producing military equipment, which resulted from the signing of the LoI

[1541] To take this into account, the Group of Publication Managers of the Peace Studies Centre www.studiperlapace.it LoI Research was recently established, which is on its way to becoming an important point of reference for a unitary and coordinated management of research policy at least among the aforementioned countries which, due to the importance of their respective production capacities, aspire to become a privileged forum for direction and decision-making at a European level

[1542] No concrete plans have yet been defined, but the aspirations described will lead to the development of initiatives capable of directing the axis of military research activities in Europe and therefore promise to require significant financial commitment

[1543] Considerations However, despite the affirmation of these "enhanced cooperation" initiatives, i.e. those referring to a limited number of countries, a broad and mature European solidarity is still lacking

[1544] In fact, the mutual defense pact contained in Article V of the amended Brussels Treaty has not been incorporated into the Community framework, and the EU is also slow to take significant decisions regarding the armaments sector

[1545] One reason for the reluctance to take a leading role in this area lies in the constraints arising from Article 296 of the Amsterdam Treaty, through which EU member states have sought to reserve decision-making power in the armaments sector for themselves, effectively imposing a barrier to the Commission's work and Parliament's oversight, even though some bodies within the European Commission are closely monitoring the actions to be taken

[1546] Reference is made to the initiative launched in 1997 by the Commission regarding the "Implementation of a European Union Strategy for Defence-Related Industries", through an "Action Plan", structured into 14 points

[1547] A plan which, however, has not yet had any concrete development

[1548] In the near future, it will therefore be necessary to proceed with the harmonization and, subsequently, the integration into a single system of European bodies that will ultimately flow into the institutional structures of the European Union

[1549] To achieve maximum results in terms of quality and cost-effectiveness, it is also necessary to refine the way in which operational needs are planned today

[1550] At the national level, it is necessary to concentrate as much as possible the process of evaluating operational requirements, and therefore programs, in a fundamentally joint manner

[1551] As established by Law 25 of February 18, 1997, and Presidential Decree 556 of October 25, 1999, military planning begins with the directives of the Minister of Defense, is developed by the Chief of Staff of Defense, who submits it to the Political Authority, and concludes with the approval of the Minister of Defense. By leveraging an overall vision of the military instrument, the programs, and the priorities to which available resources should be allocated, the most appropriate and effective choices can be made for the instrument as a whole

[1552] Investment planning that focuses on individual components, then adds them together and adjusts them in some way, is no longer cost-effective or responsive to needs

[1553] The second element that must be taken into account is that military planning, just as it is no longer "single service", it is no longer "single nation" either

[1554] This requires strengthening our knowledge of how other countries operate, and coordinating defense plans ever more closely, right from the design stage, so that they become increasingly homogeneous and coherent

[1555] It is increasingly less true, in fact, that Italy has its own requirement, different from the German or French one

[1556] In reality, the defence plans of the British, French, Italian and German forces – to name a few – are much more uniform than one might think

[1557] If we look at the end of the process, we can in fact see that the capacities pursued are 80 or 90% similar, even if at the moment each country is still thinking about and planning them on its own

[1558] Pushing harder for a European "joint moment" for military planning and defining operational requirements—fully consistent and transparent with the Alliance's Defense Planning—by involving at least those countries with greater homogeneity and a more active role in the vision of a European defense policy, can help, among other things, increase opportunities for cooperation and, therefore, create that critical mass on programs that will in turn enable real savings in terms of cost-effectiveness, both in development and acquisition, and, above all, in the management of the life cycle of materials

[1559] The Atlantic Alliance remains a pillar of Italian and European security

[1560] The CNAD (Conference of National Armaments Directors) is one of the main committees of the North Atlantic Council and is responsible for all issues relating to defense equipment

[1561] It plays a senior management role (Board of Directors) with respect to the employees of the multinational Working Groups responsible for carrying out cooperation activities in the armaments sector

[1562] Publications Centre for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ STRUCTURE OF THE CNAD Some difficulties encountered by the CNAD in responding to the needs of member countries, towards the mid-1980s, induced the National Armaments Directors of France, Germany, Great Britain and the United States of America, to establish the so-called "Four Power NADs", which became, since April 2000, with the entry of Italy, the "Five Power NADs

[1563] This is an informal partnership intended to coordinate the positions of the major nations and to define common strategies regarding major international cooperation programmes

[1564] In this context, the participating nations have also established the "International Cooperative Opportunities Group (ICOG)", which aims to strengthen transatlantic cooperation in the field of defense systems, with the objective of identifying opportunities for cooperation and developing the most concrete ones

[1565] Within international relations for cooperation in the armaments sector, bilateral government agreements, based on specific MoUs, are particularly important. The formalization of these agreements responds to strategic needs and, at the same time, offers industries better opportunities for intervention in areas of interest

[1566] The forms of collaboration generally envisaged in this type of agreement range from the purchase/sale of products and/or production licenses, to joint research, development and production

[1567] At a bilateral level, the Italian Ministry of Defence has so far signed 48 agreements (14 already ratified) and 12 are under negotiation

[1568] Among these, those relating to the countries of Eastern Europe (particularly Russia), North Africa (Egypt and Algeria), the Far East (India, China, South Korea, Singapore and Malaysia) and South America (Chile) are of great interest

[1569] The ratification and implementation of these agreements will, in short, prevent the long delays usually required for the approval process from being perceived abroad as indifference to the problems of cooperation

[1570] The changes that have occurred in the international geostrategic landscape over the last decade have been addressed by Western countries not only on a political level but also on an industrial one

[1571] Faced with a market characterized by redundant production, strong competition, and reduced demand, a review process was initiated that led the industries to undertake a courageous and challenging restructuring, rationalization, and concentration of resources in areas of excellence, allowing them to ensure an adequate presence and competitiveness in the armaments market

[1572] The US defense industry was the first to react to this new and unexpected framework

[1573] In fact, the USA, aided by the unitary legislative context and the advantage of operating in a single internal market and with a single customer, has been able to express uniqueness and coherence in its defense and foreign policy strategies, with the consequent possibility of operating on the global market with great competitiveness and effectiveness

[1574] They have therefore quickly created alliances and mergers between the large national industrial complexes, among which it is worth mentioning Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman for the aerospace, missile and defense electronics sectors, Boeing for aerospace and Raytheon for the missile sector

[1575] Even the major industrialized countries of Europe, albeit with some difficulty, have subsequently implemented specific rationalizations on a national basis and have also attempted to form alliances and mergers between their own defense companies

[1576] The most evident manifestation of this desire dates back to early 1998 with the launch of a study aimed at establishing a European Aerospace and Defence Company (EADC), through the integration of the main European defence companies

[1577] The ambitious project proved difficult to implement and in its place, sectoral production hubs were established through transnational structural agreements

[1578] In particular, national vertical integration operations have been carried out, such as the mergers between the French companies Aerospatiale and Matra Hautes Technologies and between the British companies BAe and GEC (Marconi Electronic Systems), transnational sectoral acquisitions, such as the case of the German company DASA of the Spanish company CASA, and mergers of companies of different nationalities (Aerospatiale Matra with DASA/CASA) which gave rise to the European Aeronautic Defence and Space Company (EADS), the leading European aerospace group

[1579] In parallel with this process, the path of international cooperation was pursued by establishing numerous collaborations, through consortia, companies and joint ventures, relating to specific programmes

[1580] This process of industrial reorganization is constantly evolving and is leading, as mentioned, to the implementation of mergers and consolidations aimed at establishing transnational production hubs for each production sector, with sufficient size and technological level to ensure a presence on the armaments market. These include ASTRIUM (EADS, BAe Systems) in the space sector, Eurocopter (EADS) and Agusta Westland in the helicopter sector, MBDA (BAe Systems, Aerospatiale Matra and Alenia Difesa) in the missile sector, Alenia Marconi Systems (BAe Systems and Alenia Difesa) in defense electronics. An agreement is currently being finalized between Finmeccanica and EADS to establish a 50-50 joint venture that will control the activities of Alenia, the German company DASA, and the Spanish company CASA

[1581] The avionics, land and naval armaments, and motor sectors do not yet show any particular concentrations of activity

[1582] The European defense industry must now continue along the path of concentration and rationalization in order to reduce the technological gap with the United States and increase its ability to penetrate the international arms market

[1583] The Ministry of Defence is therefore involved in numerous international programmes, both multilateral and bilateral, with particular attention to Europe and North America. FIGURE 2 4.7 Procurement Policy (broken down by Force) 4.7.1 Programme Development and Implementation The procedures for implementing a procurement policy, even if the evolutionary process of the problem is characterised by continuity and unity of development, are currently conducted separately within the technical-operational area and within the technical-administrative area

[1584] The technical-operational area is responsible for technical planning and programming, which is implemented by defining the objectives for strengthening and modernizing the instrument and is essentially developed through the following fundamental phases

[1585] identification of needs; definition of the technical-operational characteristics of the means and materials and evaluation of the needs and related financial costs

[1586] • official attribution of the mandate to the competent DG

[1587] • general indication, by the DG, of the technical-financial-industrial parameters relating to the acquisition

[1588] This final phase marks the end of the program's preliminary process, which is primarily technical and operational in nature

[1589] Pursuant to Law No. 436 of October 4, 1988 (regulations for the simplification and control of procedures established for central Defense procurement), the main programs concerning Defense (renewal and modernization of weapons systems, works, vehicles, and goods directly intended for national defense) are subject to approval by: • law, if they require extraordinary funding; • decree of the Minister of Defense, when the programs are financed through ordinary budget allocations

[1590] In this case, and provided that the programmes do not refer to the maintenance of supplies or the replenishment of stocks, the opinion of the competent Parliamentary Commissions must be obtained before the ministerial decree is issued

[1591] The Minister of Defense reports annually to the competent Parliamentary Committees on the aforementioned programs and the resulting contractual activity

[1592] The technical-administrative area (relevant General Directorates) is involved in the acquisition of supplies through procurement orders for goods and/or services by the General Staffs

[1593] These procurement orders are consequently embodied in contractual relationships between the AD and the private contracting parties in accordance with the national and community procedures in force

[1594] Once activated, the General Directorate identifies the purchasing methods by determining the scope of the contractor search (national, Community, WTO, WEAG, or between countries signatory to specific international agreements) and the type of procedure to be adopted (tender, private negotiation, competitive tender, etc

[1595] Subsequently, the draft contract, the technical specifications, and other related documents are prepared, which, where possible, depending on the nature of the contractual document, are conformed to standardized models

[1596] Private negotiation Among the methods for selecting a contractor, "private negotiation" plays a particularly important role in the context of defense procurement

[1597] This is due to the frequency, particularly in the field of WAR-LIKE materials, of the purchase of goods whose production is guaranteed by industrial patents, due to the nature of which it is not possible to promote public tenders, which only one company can supply with the technical requirements and degree of perfection required

[1598] While with the adoption of “restricted procedures” (private tender and competitive tender), the supply is based on the price previously identified by the Administration following the definition of specific “technical conditions” and the market situation, with “negotiated” procedures there is a need to subject the price offered by the company chosen for the negotiation to a specific form of control called “technical-economic adequacy analysis”

[1599] This review is carried out by a commission specifically appointed by the contracting authority. In making its assessments, it draws on the findings of previous audits conducted by another commission at the company in question. These audits are designed to determine the impact of all company costs on the running of the business, in order to determine the hourly labor rate, which will be one of the factors in determining the price of the goods to be purchased

[1600] To this end, the General Secretariat of Defense has prepared a specific "Methodology for determining company hourly costs for services or supplies," which indicates the "guidelines" and procedures to be followed to avoid, as noted by the Court of Auditors itself, the burden of the so-called "costs of inefficiency" of the industrial system on the Defense Administration

[1601] Furthermore, privately negotiated contracts include a "safeguard clause" as a further means of monitoring and adjusting prices to a principle of fairness. This clause requires the company to provide assurance that the price offered is not higher than the price it has charged for similar services to its best customer, including internationally. Violation of this clause will result in the contract terms being reduced by the aforementioned limit

[1602] Advisory Committee In order to streamline the procedural process for Defense contracts, the recent Legislative Decree no. 496 of December 28, 1998, established a "Consultative Committee," chaired by the Secretary General of Defense, with the task of expressing "opinions" on draft contracts resulting from international cooperation agreements in the armaments sector and on those implementing programs approved by law or by decree of the Minister of Defense pursuant to the aforementioned Law

[1603] The Committee's jurisdiction covers programmes exceeding €5 million

[1604] These opinions concern the technical, administrative and economic aspects as well as the appropriateness and suitability of the estimated prices to be used as the basis for the tenders (restricted procedures), or agreed with the contracting companies (negotiated procedure

[1605] Pursuant to the legislative decree that established the Committee, this advisory body - composed of the Deputy Chief of Staff of Defence, a Director General of the Ministry, a Magistrate of the Court of Auditors and two experts with specific expertise in cost analysis and industrial accounting - replaced, with a view to simplifying and streamlining procedures within the joint force, various advisory bodies, including those of the FA, provided for by numerous pre-existing laws, the activation of which often caused considerable delays in the start of contractual activity due to the recurring overlapping of the relevant responsibilities

[1606] Peculiarities related to the arms market

[1607] The arms market is a highly specialized market where companies operate that adopt solutions with extremely high technological content

[1608] Therefore, the areas of origin of weapon systems and their components and spare parts are very limited

[1609] It is therefore inevitable for Italy to turn to foreign markets, particularly the United States, for its supplies

[1610] Given the complexity of the materials being procured, the supply is typically carried out a long time after the order is issued, and as a result, the company finds itself financially exposed for the activities involved in preparing the project and procuring the raw materials, as well as paying its workers

[1611] In current international commercial practice, it is customary to pay the supplier an advance on the supply price upon signing the contract

[1612] This practice is not compatible with the general accounting rules of the State according to which it is legitimate to pay the price exclusively upon completion of the supply (art. 12 LCGS, art. 5, paragraph 1 Legislative Decree

[1613] March 1977, n. 79 converted, with amendments, by law 28 May 1997, n

[1614] In fact, national legislation does not take into account the financial reality of the sector's international markets, limiting the possibility of trading and acquiring materials produced abroad

[1615] In this context, and after consulting the Council of State on the matter, a draft provision has been proposed for inclusion in the 2002 Finance Act. This provision contemplates the possibility, in the cases described above, of granting advances on part of the contract price, subject to the provision of an appropriate guarantee, even in derogation of the current provisions prohibiting this

[1616] Computerization of Contract Procedures and "e-Procurement" Despite the inherent difficulties in operating within the timeframes often required by operational needs, the Defence Administration's negotiating activities are guided by the principles established in Legislative Decree no. 29 of 3 February 1993, as amended by Legislative Decree no. 80/98, of cost-effectiveness, effectiveness, and efficiency, with the aim of ensuring maximum transparency in the implementation of procedures

[1617] In this context, it should be noted that Law 340/2000, which establishes rules on administrative simplification, in order to implement the aforementioned transparency requirement, requires all public administrations to publish tender notices and tender offers on one or more websites, identified by Prime Ministerial Decree

[1618] These forms of communication do not, however, replace the other advertising obligations provided for by Community legislation, including publication obligations in daily or periodical newspapers

[1619] The aforementioned provision, however, has not yet found widespread application as the expected Prime Ministerial Decree has not yet been issued

[1620] Despite this regulatory shortcoming, and even before the aforementioned simplified regulation was issued, since December 1998 the General Directorate of the Commissioner's Office and General Services has posted on a dedicated website not only all tender notices and calls for tenders relating to its activities, but also the related specifications and directives that precisely and precisely regulate the procedures and criteria to which the Administration itself is required to comply in its activities

[1621] Worth mentioning in this regard are the directives regarding the "verification of the appropriateness of abnormally low offers," the "contractual execution," and the "materials testing procedures" of the commissioner's office, which, again for the purpose of widespread dissemination, have also been published in the Official Journal of the Italian Republic

[1622] Particular attention was also paid to strengthening the Public Relations Office, which, through an intranet system connected to all internal offices and divisions, ensures real-time provision of information requested by various users

[1623] These achievements undoubtedly constitute an example that other General Directorates can follow when the implementing decree is issued for the widespread adoption of advertising on dedicated websites, in order to ensure maximum transparency in the business activities carried out

[1624] With regard to the specific aspect of “e-procurement”, the aforementioned law also provides for the possibility of carrying out “economic tenders” through the use of IT systems

[1625] These online procedures, which will also be regulated by specific regulations, will certainly speed up the process of selecting the contractor while guaranteeing the necessary “equal opportunities” as well as confidentiality, where required, and transparency of all tender procedures

[1626] The need to rationalise and optimise state spending on goods and services that are common to all administrations has led to the establishment of a special company within the Ministry of Economy and Finance (CONSIP S.p.A

[1627] which, following specific "economic tenders", proceeds to stipulate specific agreements for goods and services, which each administration is obliged to adhere to in order to satisfy its own needs

[1628] This, in addition to achieving economies of scale, leads to a streamlining of procurement procedures by individual administrations, with consequent advantages also in terms of reduced use of human resources

[1632] The procedures in force for issuing authorizations for the export of military equipment and the transfer of related documentation are currently regulated by Law 185/90 and its implementing regulation, Prime Ministerial Decree no. 448 of 25 September

[1633] The regulations and controls provided for by this law are among the most restrictive currently in force in other Western countries

[1634] In summary, the bureaucratic process involves requesting authorization for commercial negotiations and, upon conclusion of a contract, a subsequent request for export

[1635] After an initial investigation, conducted by the SMD or the MAE depending on the type of negotiation, the authorization request is usually brought to the attention of an Advisory Committee composed of representatives of the MAE (President), the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of the Interior, Productive Activities, the Ministry of the Environment, and the Customs Agency, which expresses a non-binding opinion

[1636] In the case of classified material, during the investigation phase, ANS/UCSI is asked for its opinion and, if necessary, authorization to disclose classified information

[1637] Furthermore, the Defence General Staff, after having requested information on the material under examination from the Armed Forces General Staffs and the General Secretariat of Defence/DNA, expresses a binding opinion regarding the security and military-technical aspects

[1638] As regards DUAL-USE material, export is regulated by Legislative Decree 89/97 and takes into account European Community Regulation

[1639] The entire investigation is carried out by the Ministry of Productive Activities, which grants the export authorization after presentation to another Advisory Committee composed of representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (President), the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of the Interior, Productive Activities, the Treasury, Health, Education and Research, and the Customs Agency

[1640] More than ten years after this law came into force, however, several points have emerged that require modification, in order to streamline procedures without eliminating controls

[1641] In particular, its inadequacy in managing the complex phenomenon of European industrial concentration has been noted, with the formation of new companies in the form of Transnational Defence Corporations (TDCs), which presupposes the possibility of rationalizing and specializing production units according to a logic of industrial efficiency, through the circulation of manufactured parts between different plants located in different countries

[1642] The opportunity of the ratification of the Framework Agreement, signed by the Defence Ministers of Italy, France, England, Germany, Spain and Sweden in Farnborough on 27 July 2000, was therefore taken to make some necessary adjustments

[1643] Further operational adjustments to the authorization procedures remain to be examined to allow the national industry to best present itself in the process of structural integration of the European arms industry and participate, on an equal basis, in co-production programs

Technological Research In the field of technological research, the Ministry of Defense has undertaken a series of initiatives aimed at strengthening research by acting according to three main criteria: - giving the military research sector greater autonomy with respect to specific weapons development programs, in the belief that technology has "neutral" characteristics with respect to its applications

[1756] It is therefore essential to seek maximum synergy between the needs of studies that, while arising from needs related to different systems or applications, involve identical technological bases; - to focus on using all the intellectual and organizational resources available in the country, involving universities, industries, and public and private research institutions without limits or distinctions

[1757] significantly increase the financial resources allocated to research, with the ultimate goal of aligning national spending with that of the European countries with which Italy aspires to compete

[1758] In parallel with the legislative attribution (law on Military Summits) to the Secretary General and DGA of responsibility for the sector's development, ongoing activities have been strengthened and new ones have been launched at the national and international levels

[1759] At the national level, the launch of the first National Military Research Programme was promoted, which led to the collection of over 228 new research projects relating to the sectors and priorities identified by the Defence General Staff (Directive SMD

[1760] Of these projects, which cover almost all technological sectors and whose development is considered essential to ensure a qualified national presence in future armament programs, 30 have already been selected, with an estimated total cost of around €4.5 billion, funded in the 2001 financial year or the following one

[1761] Furthermore, the Ministry of Defence actively participated in the study conducted by the Ministry in preparation of the National Research Plan (PNR) which, starting from the observation of the existence of a "gap" between the Italian, European and, even more so, the US and Japanese situations, envisaged a series of strategic actions (in particular

[1762] a structural action for the strategic repositioning of the national scientific system, a short-medium term action to recover the efficiency and effectiveness of intervention tools and a cross-cutting action for the monitoring and evaluation of interventions) and identified the financial resources deemed necessary

[1763] The technological priorities identified by the PNR, however, referring to all scientific disciplines, only marginally involve, and always on a "dual" basis, the interests of the Ministry of Defence, which will therefore have to continue to develop and finance research of military interest on its own

[1764] At the international level, the activity and commitment of the Ministry of Defence have been manifested even more sensitively due to the dense network of relationships that characterizes the sector at European and global level

[1765] Traditional areas (WEAG, NATO) have been dynamically joined by new ones (Loi, ETAP, etc.), contributing to the creation of a rapidly evolving and extremely competitive framework

[1766] NATO RTO (Research & Technology Organisation) The NATO RTO promotes and coordinates scientific and technological research activities of military interest within the Atlantic Alliance

[1767] The supervisory body of this Organization, of which Italy is an active member, is the "NATO Research & Technology Board" (RT Board), which remains dually dependent on the Military Committee and the CNAD

[1768] The RT Board, for the management of research activities, uses an Agency (Research & Technology Agency - RTA) based in Paris

[1769] The RTA's study and research activities are implemented through "Panels" which, by technological sector, promote the initiation and management of the work of Working Groups in which national experts participate

[1770] Italy provides its experts to over 60 working groups, funding their participation

[1771] However, the study activities do not require specific funding but are conducted on a voluntary and free basis by experts made available by the Alliance countries who selectively decide which studies to participate in and contribute to

[1772] The driving force and value of this commitment must therefore be sought in the exchange of information that the network of government and academic experts from the Alliance countries who report to the RTO is able to ensure, since there are no funds dedicated to awarding contracts

[1773] The Organization's “product”—study reports, scientific publications, symposiums, etc.—is of the highest quality and continues to constitute a point of reference for the entire scientific and technological community of NATO countries

[1774] ETAP (European Technology Acquisition Program) Following a Franco-British initiative, ETAP was launched with the aim of jointly identifying and conducting those technological research programs that will ensure the availability of the technologies that the two countries, individually, deem necessary to support their specific future aeronautical programs

[1775] The initial nucleus of France and Great Britain was later joined by Germany, Sweden, Portugal and Italy (reconstituting the same group of Loi countries within ETAP

[1776] These research programs, primarily oriented towards the aeronautical sector and currently being defined, will involve significant human and financial resources, currently estimated at around 20 billion/year (10.33 million euros) per country for the next 4 years and will be framed within a technological perspective that optimizes participation and maximizes their impact. The current overabundant availability of government testing centers specialized in military materials (ranges, technical centers, specialized laboratories) has led to a critical review of their geographical distribution and technological destination with the now unavoidable aim of seeking their rationalization on a European scale

[1777] Two initiatives are therefore active, conducted within WEAG and on a smaller scale within a group made up of France, Germany, England and Italy

[1778] The pursuit of greater savings must be mediated in light of the safeguarding of testing capacity, which remains the basis of the ability to independently conduct research activities

[1779] The prospect of significant future savings could, on the contrary, require an initial additional investment, not yet estimable, necessary for the establishment of common structures (European Test Centres) that ensure effective and transparent joint maintenance of these capabilities

[1780] The resources needed to achieve the outlined results appear to be far superior to those actually available, the former having been estimated to be in the order of 500 billion / year (258. 23 million euros), compared to the latter which, currently, have been estimated to be equal to approximately 40 billion / year (20. 65 million euros) of which 20 (10. 33 million euros) are ensured annually for WEAG activities

[1781] This situation requires a “flexible” commitment which, despite the awareness of an optimal reference level, is content to finalize programs to the extent possible and consequently accepts a partial and limited achievement of the objectives

[1782] Research Funds Despite the progress made in the 2001 Defense budget, Italian spending on research and development remains marginal both in relation to absolute needs and in comparison with the amount invested in the sector by Italy's main European partners

[1783] Since a serious R&D policy is a preliminary condition for closing the technological gap that separates Italy from its major allies, to achieve an adequate increase in resources it is necessary to move in two directions

[1784] one internal to Defence as such, and one external, referring to the "country system

[1785] The sector currently has a volume of resources in the order of 250 billion per year (129.12 million euros), compared to the previous 100-120 billion per year (51.64-61.97 million euros

[1786] This is indicative of a significant positive trend reversal

[1787] However, more can be done, first of all on the internal front, by finding resources that can be allocated to modernization

[1788] billion (103.29 million euros) less on an acquisition program worth 10000 billion (5,165 million euros) certainly has a smaller impact than what going from 250 to 400-500 billion euros per year (from 129.12 to 206.59/258.23 million euros) could mean for research and development

[1789] The second possible approach consists in valorizing the R&D that comes from the "country system", that is, that produced by the MURST national R&D plan and by the funds of the Ministry of Industry, through the laws it uses to promote high technologies, including dual-use technologies

[1790] By using the resources made available by the various laws regulating this sector with a more in-depth approach, oriented towards R&D rather than procurement in the strict sense (as has sometimes been done in emergencies), it would be possible to achieve significant additional volumes for technological research, in the order of €1,000 billion per year (€516.46 million), while at the same time using the funds in a way that is even more in line with the spirit of the laws supporting the national technological base

[1791] Dual-use technologies There are many sectors of civilian research that allow for strong spill-overs to the military and vice versa

[1792] It is necessary to use the fruits of that research and those commercial technologies, without exaggerating the requirements of what were once military specifications

[1793] A sort of "philosophical revision" of MILSPEC is already underway by military planners

[1794] the tendency is to focus attention on the truly essential aspects, making greater use of both technologies and (in certain cases) COTS (commercial off the shelf) products

[1795] After all, many of these technologies are "managed" by the same industries that work in both the civilian and military sectors, and therefore lend themselves well to generating internal spin-offs

[1796] From this perspective, Italian defense industries must also embark on a "cultural modernization" journey, abandoning the imposition of solely self-developed technologies in certain production sectors and instead adopting them where they already exist and are perhaps more cost-effective. 4.10 CONCLUSIONS/CONSIDERATIONS Publications Center for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ Italy, along with other European countries, is pursuing a defense materials policy along a political-operational and industrial path of extensive international co-production

[1797] Pragmatically and gradually, with inevitable setbacks, the member countries of the Union have succeeded in "communitarizing" large sectors of activity that were once typically national, starting with those of an economic and then monetary nature

[1798] There have thus been significant concessions of sovereignty in various aspects of free movement and, ultimately, of currency

[1799] The emerging European security and defense dimension requires the pursuit of ever-increasing effectiveness in military spending, with a view to effectively planning and standardizing European operational requirements and capabilities, including through the reorganization of the European defense industry

[1800] From all this arose the need for an armaments policy that was as unified and coordinated as possible to provide the European Security and Defence Policy (ESDP) with concreteness and effective tools

[1801] At the same time, however, it seems appropriate and convenient, given the realities of the resources that Europeans dedicate to the defense sector, to seek a healthy and mutually beneficial cooperative relationship with the US defense industry

[1802] Europe's defense sector cannot and must not systematically pay a toll, in order to have the modern operational systems it needs, to any logic and sirens of production autarky, isolating itself from healthy competitive pressure, in this case predominantly American, and from the positive effects this competition—in terms of prices and quality—has on European products

[1803] It should also not be overlooked that, in certain specific sectors, the United States has highly sophisticated knowhow that Europe cannot ignore

[1804] It is also necessary to invest more in research and development, thus promoting the reduction of the technological and operational "gap" of European military instruments compared to those across the Atlantic

[1805] The various European bodies, currently coexisting, will therefore need to be harmonized, starting from the WEAG (Western European Armament Group) up to the OCCAR (Organism for Joint Cooperation on Armaments) or the structure resulting from the signing of the LOI (Letter of Intent), in order to finally arrive at the appropriate changes to the EU institutional framework called upon to manage this matter

[1806] This effort to reorganize and modernize our military, with a European and Atlantic focus, raises the question of the resources to be allocated to the sector

[1807] To increase European and national strategic capabilities, it will be necessary to give greater impetus to industrial investments, strengthen the defense-industry link, and place greater emphasis on the joint efforts of institutions and the manufacturing sector

[1808] On the personnel front, the available human resources, both military and civilian, do not allow for adequately addressing organizational structures and require joint rationalization and a more effective allocation of responsibilities, which currently in some areas present some redundancy and a not always clear division of responsibilities

[1809] In the area of civilian personnel, however, professional development must be pursued, facilitating a significant shift in mentality, both at the military and civilian levels, to enhance the civilian personnel component of the Defense, which constitutes a very important resource for the military instrument as a whole. Publications Peace Studies Centre www.studiperlapace.it ____________ PART V MILITARY PERSONNEL 5.1 MILITARY CONDITION 5.1.1 The fact-finding survey on the military condition 5.2 RECRUITMENT 5.2.1 The recruitment of enlisted men 5.2.2 The recruitment of non-commissioned officers 5.2.3 The recruitment of officers in special 5.2.4 The recruitment of auxiliary officers 5.2.5 The supplementary forces 5.2.6 Recalls to service from the auxiliary 5.2.7 The Carabinieri 5.2.8 Women's military service 5.2.9 Military chaplains in Italy 5.2.10 Conscientious objection 5.2.11 The balanced force of 2001 5.3 CAREER PROCESS (selection, evaluation and criteria) 5.3.1 Officers 5.3.2 Non-commissioned officers 5.3.3 Troops 5.3.4 Resignations (excluding Carabinieri) 5.4 SALARY 5.4.1 Periodic adjustment of remuneration 5.4.2 Retirement benefits 5.4.3 Future developments 5.4.4 Treatment of military personnel engaged in peacekeeping and humanitarian operations 5.4.5 The difference in the economic treatment of the Italian armed forces compared to NATO Allies 5.5 THE ACCOMMODATION PROBLEM 5.6 MILITARY REPRESENTATION 5.7 PERSONNEL WELFARE 5.8 THE PHENOMENON OF HAZING 5.1 Military status The Constitutional Court, in expressing its opinion on “military status”, has repeatedly reiterated the peculiarity of the situation of the citizen (military) included in the Armed Forces compared to that of other citizens

[1810] This is because the position of the military citizen is characterised, among other things, by his strict submission to the hierarchical relationship and military discipline

[1811] elements that form the basis of the functioning of the Armed Forces themselves

[1812] hierarchical and disciplinary relationships that materialize in precise limits on fundamental rights (such as, for example, the right to strike, freedom of expression, and association), subjection to special legislation (the military penal code), and specific disciplinary regulations

[1813] This results in atypical recruitment (normalized, i.e., constant inflows of recruits) also linked to constant physical fitness, the loss of which leads to the termination of the employment relationship (unsuitability for military service), targeted and ongoing training and education, continuous monitoring of the results achieved and the soldier's behavior during service (which takes shape in the preparation of specific documentation), a peculiar and often risky employment starting from the training phase, which also entails a mobility in the career path without parallel in the public sector

[1814] In this regard, it should be noted that the movement of military personnel from one location to another falls within the category of military order and therefore does not require any justification, as it is intrinsic to a matter in which the specific public interest of respect for discipline and service directly and immediately prevails over any other

[1815] As an example of the difference with the general nature of public employment, it is reported that the failure by a military officer to execute a movement from one location to another takes on criminal relevance from a military perspective, as it falls within the violation of the obligation to immediately execute the order (article 173 of the CMPM

[1816] Last but not least, it should not be overlooked that military personnel of all ranks who serve in the Armed Forces, voluntarily or in fulfillment of the obligations established by the law on conscription, solemnly pledge by their oath to perform the institutional duties of the Armed Forces with absolute loyalty to the institutions of the Republic, with discipline and honor, with a sense of responsibility and conscious participation, sparing no physical, moral, or intellectual energy, even facing, if necessary, the risk of sacrificing their lives (Presidential Decree 545/1986, art. 9). More specifically, this set of duties ordinarily entails, for career military personnel

[1817] disciplinary, administrative and criminal responsibilities related to the command of units and the management of sophisticated and expensive weapons systems

[1818] • continuous technical and professional updating and requalification

[1819] extreme mobility of work and location, with a high frequency of transfers

[1820] It should also be noted that such mobility has repercussions not only on the soldier, but also on his family unit, who is often faced with the choice between continually moving from one station to another or due to the distance of the head of the family; • limitation and slowness of the career path depending on the pyramidal structure of the military hierarchy

[1821] • greater psychological and physical wear and tear compared to civilian careers and professions and greater risk of physical injury and illness due to service

[1822] Military personnel on conscription duty face different but equally significant burdens: • psychological difficulties in integrating into the social context of the places where they serve and into the military environment itself, due to its atypicality compared to the civilian environment; • economic difficulties, which the very modest pay does not allow them to face

[1823] • possible under-utilization in unrewarding or inferior roles to the cultural and technical-professional qualifications possessed

[1824] • possible separation from places of residence and from social and emotional interests

[1825] While the above-mentioned burdens are in themselves unavoidable because they arise from the nature of military service (with the exception of those relating to military service, which will be suspended by 2004), it is nevertheless possible to reduce or compensate for the resulting inconvenience with appropriate measures

[1826] Solutions to the problems may include adjustments to pay, housing standards, and the general well-being of personnel, as well as those related to the functioning of military representative bodies

[1827] Even within a fully professional model, pride in one's role and in military values remains essential, and these remain the true source of institutional affection for those who have chosen a military career

[1828] However, it is beyond doubt that such subjective factors cannot be preserved by the interventions of military institutions alone, precisely because the military citizen and his family are in any case an integral part of society

[1829] The public's lack of appreciation for the service generally performed, or even opposition, for example, to training activities (which can always be carried out elsewhere or cancelled as unnecessary) and social protection systems, the latter seen as privileges of the profession rather than measures designed to temper the unique nature of military service, can certainly influence personnel's attachment to the institution and thus make the burden of military service unsustainable

[1830] One measure by which this psychological attitude among permanent service personnel can be assessed is the rate of resignations from service among officers in the ranks from captain to lieutenant colonel, where departures have increased over the last three years to almost 100% of annual recruitments in certain roles (pilots, doctors) and are also significantly elevated in other officer specializations

[1831] In this regard, it should be noted that these are personnel with professional skills that the Administration requires years of training and significant financial resources to develop

[1832] This must necessarily be taken into account regardless of the defense model to be pursued

[1833] The fact-finding investigation into the military situation It is necessary at this point to also take into consideration the conclusions reached by the Defence Committee of the Chamber of Deputies at the end of the fact-finding investigation into the military situation

[1834] Unfortunately, the investigation was launched at the end of 2000, when all the legislative provisions regarding the restructuring of the Armed Forces had already been approved

[1835] “The conduct of the fact-finding investigation allowed the Commission to deepen its understanding of the main issues that define the contours and specificity of the condition of military personnel

[1836] In general, what emerged from the various hearings was the need to focus attention on the profound and widespread state of distress among military personnel, which has repercussions on their very motivations, with inevitable consequences in terms of functionality and operational effectiveness

[1837] Publications Center for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ This situation is particularly jarring with the impressive restructuring process of the Armed Forces, begun in this legislature, with the approval of reforms, which have also seen the Commission as a protagonist in the legislative activity

[1838] These reforms, defined by many as “epochal”, culminated in the approval of Law 331 of 14 November 2000, which established professional military service

[1839] They are therefore aimed at the profound transformation of our military instrument, which has proven indispensable for the presence and influence of Italy's role within the context of the European Union and the Atlantic Alliance

[1840] It is therefore clear that the major innovations underway reinforce the need to focus attention on issues relating to the condition of military personnel, that is, on the human factor, as a fundamental and decisive factor in any reform. As emerged during the fact-finding investigation, there are numerous significant avenues for potential interventions

[1841] As has emerged from the examination of the individual aspects touched upon by the investigation

[1842] They can form the basis for regulatory interventions to be implemented in the current legislature or to be developed starting from the next one

[1843] In any case, the issues raised must be addressed with the same incisiveness with which the structural reforms of the Armed Forces were addressed, in order to ensure that the military has the functionality necessary to achieve its assigned goals, also within the framework of Italy's obligations arising from its membership in the European Union and NATO

[1844] The Constitutional Court's considerations and the conclusions of the Chamber of Deputies' fact-finding investigation fully represent the ethical and moral situation of the Armed Forces, which during the five years of the legislature have been subjected to "epochal reforms," endured and endured with extreme discipline, but with equally significant hardships that have led to demoralization and demotivation. These elements must be kept in mind as the restructuring process is completed, including through the remediation of certain measures that have proven to be of questionable effectiveness

[1845] Recruitment Since the late 1990s, the “defense sector” has been affected by a transformation process which for the Armed Forces

[1846] as a first step, led to the quantitative reduction of the instrument through a significant reduction in personnel (from 350,000 to approximately 250,000) by introducing a form of nutrition for the troops as an alternative to conscription and based on professional criteria (mixed model), balanced and calibrated on a minority professional component and, subsequently, with the suspension of conscription, to a model of professional soldiers for a total of 190,000 units
