[2060] Military Chaplains in Italy Spiritual Assistance in the Italian Armed Forces is entrusted to approximately 200 Catholic Chaplains under the guidance of the Military Ordinary Archbishop

[2061] In recent years, the service has undergone several transformations to adequately meet the new needs arising from changes in the Armed Forces

[2062] In the same ecclesial context, facts and documents have made it possible to deepen the meaning and value of this service

[2063] It is enough to mention: - the publication of the Apostolic Constitution "Spiritualis Militum Curae" on 21 April 1986; - the preparation and celebration of the First Synod of the Military Ordinariate Church in Italy in the years 1997-1999; - the celebration of the Jubilee of the Military on 20 November 2000, to indicate the attention that the Church pays to the military world

[2064] The military chaplain is a Catholic priest suitable to carry out this service, appointed by Decree of the President of the Republic upon designation by the Military Ordinary and proposal by the Minister of Defence

[2065] art. 78, 80 First Synod of the Church Military Ordinariate

[2066] The service of the military chaplain cannot ignore complete integration with the realities of the Armed Forces

[2067] In fact, it is practiced “among” soldiers called upon to perform an increasingly advanced and complex professional role and destined to operate in national and international contexts

[2068] The Chaplain follows his soldiers, adapts to their conditions, participates in their missions

[2069] Its presence indicates the possibility of faithfully living the deepest ideals of the human person

[2070] Honesty, consistency, discipline, fortitude, altruism, and the ability to serve are just some of the characteristics that accompany the life and professionalism of men and women in arms

[2071] For believers, more specifically, it becomes an eloquent sign and authoritative aid for living Christianity coherently even in the world of the barracks

[2072] The Chaplain's attention is not only for the soldier but also for his family

[2073] It follows her from her birth with marriage training courses and accompanies her throughout her subsequent development

[2074] Family issues related to the effectiveness of military personnel's duties in Italy and on missions abroad are highlighted in the Pastoral Letter that the Military Ordinary published this year

[2075] With this in mind, a special commission was established with a specific pastoral office for the family

[2076] International events in recent years have required the use of military personnel, and consequently of chaplains, for peacekeeping missions

[2077] This presence proved particularly useful and indispensable for both the military and the local population

[2078] A man of communion, the Chaplain actively contributes to maintaining a serene and supportive climate among the military

[2079] It shares hardships, celebrates anniversaries, fosters moments of brotherhood and communion, and coordinates solidarity efforts for those most in need

[2080] As pastor of a community, he leads it on a path of purification and renewed impetus in faith, and as a spiritual guide he knows how to find the right word, discreet yet eloquent, for each believer who entrusts himself to him, proposing a path of personal progression

[2081] In his meeting with ministers of other religious confessions, he expressed the supreme good of peace and the primacy of human dignity, which comes before any form of belief or religion

[2082] Attention to the training of Chaplains has recently materialized in the establishment of a School for Chaplain Students, located in the Military City of Cecchignola

[2083] This year, twenty-five young men began their studies to become military chaplains under the guidance of a team of priests who take care of their human, spiritual, and physical formation

[2084] A fundamental step in the preparation of the future Chaplain is represented by the acquisition of knowledge relating to the organizational structure of the Armed Forces, both from a theoretical and practical point of view

[2085] This objective is also achieved through visits that aspiring chaplains make to military settings such as barracks, bases and naval units

[2086] Conscientious objection Conscientious objection, which originated as a refusal of military service and has now become a citizen's right, has had clear repercussions on military organization given the identical pool of recipients, the parity of civil service for the purposes of fulfilling military service obligations, and the constraints associated with the different conditions for fulfilling the two services (in essence, in the absence of solid moral and religious convictions, personnel subject to conscription, all other conditions being equal, choose the less onerous service

[2087] This has caused an exponential expansion of the phenomenon of conscientious objection from a few thousand individuals in the early 1980s and a few tens of thousands in the early 1990s (effects due to jurisprudential interventions that led to the equating of the duration of civil service to that of military service), to over 70,000 applications in 1998, to approximately 108,000 applications in 1999 and to 62,524 in 2000. With the law on conscientious objection (L. n. 230/98), the regulation of conscientious objection was radically modified

[2088] The most significant innovations were

[2089] the recognition of conscientious objection as a "subjective right" of the citizen and the transfer of management to the National Office for Civil Service (UNSC), within the Presidency of the Council of Ministers

[2090] Furthermore, the deadline for this transition was extended to 31 December 2001, due to the difficulties encountered by the UNSC in implementing the management of the entire sector of conscientious objectors

[2091] Subsequently, the legislator intervened (Law no. 64/2001) to establish the national civil service, which was managed by the UNSC itself pending the establishment of the Civil Service Agency. This provision provides for the admission to the civil service of men and women on an equal basis, whose financial treatment is related to that reserved for Volunteers on Annual Service (VFA) and within the limits of the financial availability of the National Fund for the Civil Service

[2092] Among the main innovations introduced, it is foreseen that: in the transitional period (until the suspension of compulsory military service), conscientious objectors and citizens fit for military service who opt for such service are subject to the obligation to perform civil service, provided that they are not necessary to satisfy the needs of the Armed Forces

[2093] Furthermore, Italian citizens who request it and are at least 26 years of age are eligible to perform this service on a voluntary basis, as are citizens who have been discharged due to unfitness for military service or who are on temporary indefinite leave, if they are under 26 years of age; • during the current period (after the suspension of compulsory military service), the matter will be regulated by specific legislative decrees, aimed at identifying those eligible to voluntarily perform civil service, defining the methods of access to the service and its duration, as well as the related legal and financial benefits

[2094] The inspiring criteria of the aforementioned decrees are, in summary

[2095] admission to civil service for men and women, on a completely equal basis

[2096] determining the economic and legal treatment of civil service volunteers, taking into account the treatment reserved for VFA (Volunteers on Annual Service) and within the limits of the financial availability of the National Fund for Civil Service

[2097] the analogous condition between civil and military service, in relation to the vocational choice, the area in which they perform their service, the hours of service and free time

[2098] Therefore, the measure resulting from the institutionalization of the civil service presents itself as an alternative to the recruitment of professional military forces, which will need to rely on a large pool of applicants to acquire committed and well-selected personnel, both physically and mentally

[2099] At the moment, the number of applications is barely sufficient to ensure the minimum annual revenue planned for the recruitment of ShortTerm Volunteers (VFB

[2100] It is therefore necessary that the aforementioned structures - to avoid harmful competition - be able to interact for the institutional purposes for which they are intended

[2101] Furthermore, when drafting the legislative decrees resulting from Law No. 64 of March 6, 2001, we hope for concrete recognition of the uniqueness/particularity of voluntary military service, compared to civilian service, without detracting from this highly esteemed form of social commitment

[2102] Furthermore, it should be noted that the introduction of professional military service has led to a halving of applications for conscientious objection, while applications for civilian service in 2001 are not yet known. [2112] Career path (selection, evaluation and criteria) 5.3.1 Officers The Legislative Decree

[2113] and subsequent amendments has reorganised the roles of Officers in a reductive manner (around 8000 fewer units), grouping them into four types (operational, intermediate, technical and logistical), each of which is divided into a normal role (coming from the Academies or recruited from young graduates in possession of specific professional skills, such as doctors, psychologists, engineers, etc.) and a special role (coming from the roles of Non-Commissioned Officers or Reserve Officers

[2114] The same measure significantly modified the advancement process, previously based on evaluation rates defined as a percentage of staff presence in the role. This was to prevent, as in the past, irregular staff recruitment or departures from causing career accelerations or slowdowns

[2115] In particular, the new system establishes minimum tenures at each rank in order to access promotion rates, thus allowing the Administration to better plan the deployment of Officers and simultaneously provide those interested with adequate certainty in terms of career expectations

[2116] In essence, the so-called normalized promotion system (i.e., a fixed number of annual promotions) has been strengthened, while at the same time reiterating the use of "forced departures" by management in order not to exceed the maximum number of personnel allowed for each grade

[2117] Expectancy for Reduction of Staff (ARS

[2118] This also takes into account that in the Armed Forces, career progression cannot be tied to mere "natural" vacancy in the higher rank, but must include a preestablished number of annual promotions, resulting from a precise combination of training periods, command obligations, employment situations, tenure at the rank, and planned recruitment

[2119] For the similar roles listed above (operational, intermediate, logistical, and technical), similar career profiles have been established, i.e., identical advancement rates, while keeping in mind that the career profiles of non-similar roles generally differ less than the pre-existing situation

[2120] This made it possible to remediate previous anomalous conditions, whereby the careers of Officers with the same function differed significantly depending on the Armed Force to which they belonged

[2121] On the other hand, this interforce homogenization, while mediating positions, has also led to significant career slowdowns, particularly in accessing management

[2122] This also takes into account that, as a consequence of the reorganization of the military personnel's social security system, implemented by Legislative Decree No. 165 of 30 April 1997 - which raised the retirement age - it has become necessary to appropriately extend the duration of service at certain ranks of each role

[2123] The changed organizational structure of the Armed Forces has also made it necessary to update the rules governing the composition of the Advancement Commissions, and to introduce specific control procedures dictated by the most recent case law on the matter

[2124] In particular, in accordance with the law reorganizing the "Military Higher Ranks", the Chief of Defense - who has been awarded the rank of General or Admiral - assumes the Presidency of the "Top Commission", established within each Armed Force to evaluate division generals

[2125] This Commission coincides with the superior advancement commission of each Armed Force and the respective Chief of Staff assumes the Vice-Presidency

[2126] The composition of the Ordinary Commission and the Higher Commission for Publications of the Peace Studies Centre www.studiperlapace.it ____________ of Advancement has also been changed both in relation to the new organizational structure of the Armed Forces and for functional and employment reasons

[2127] Furthermore, in compliance with the delegation, a Control Commission (5 members, including one official appointed by Ministerial Decree) has been established to oversee the work of the Advancement Commissions. This Commission is responsible for verifying the procedures for advancement decisions that have been annulled ex officio or following the acceptance of a judicial appeal or an extraordinary appeal to the President of the Republic

[2128] In the event of annulled advancement decisions, the Minister of Defense may convene the Commission to verify the regularity of the Advancement Commissions' activities and assessments, as well as the consistency, when rehearsing, of the Advancement Commissions' activities and assessments with the decisions accepting the appeals

[2129] To at least partially compensate for the slowdown in certain career profiles and safeguard economic aspects, rules have also been introduced that, similarly to the Police Forces, allow the attribution of the economic treatment of Colonel and General upon promotion to Major/Lieutenant Colonel respectively, provided they have 15/25 years of seniority of service from the rank of Lieutenant

[2130] In this way, an administrative career has been effectively established that compensates for the slowdown in the hierarchical career

[2152] The Implementation Regulation of the Law on Leadership Reform has assigned to the Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces, among other things, the responsibility for selecting volunteer personnel. This has led, with regard to the procedures for recruiting volunteers, to the implementation of a series of changes and initiatives aimed at selecting personnel suitable for operating within the individual Armed Forces

[2153] Above all, new selection criteria were established, adhering to a concept that goes beyond the simple principle of choice/exclusion and projects a vision of the soldier not only as a current, present, but also a potential, future resource, in which to invest in terms of training and education and consequently in employment, as volunteer personnel are, in any case, destined to remain in service for an extended period

[2154] Consequently, the responsibilities for selecting personnel, including volunteers, have been transferred from the General Directorate of Conscription to the Armed Forces General Staffs, who exercise them through the Armed Forces Inspectorates and the various selection centers under their control, or the selection centers of the Police Forces, both civil and military, or of other Administrations, to which the military may be admitted

[2170] Economic treatment The remuneration of military personnel is made up of the following components: fundamental, accessory and eventual: • Fundamental component or Salary

[2171] remunerates the work performance connected with the employment relationship with the State

[2172] In particular, non-managerial staff (up to the rank of lieutenant colonel) are classified in different "salary levels" in relation to the rank they hold, like other public employees

[2173] Furthermore, he is the recipient of the Individual Seniority Remuneration (IRA) linked to seniority of service

[2174] Managerial staff receive a salary that is linked to their rank and beyond

[2175] or Special supplementary allowance

[2176] intended to adjust the level of salaries to changes in the cost of living (inflation

[2177] Since November 1991, this allowance has not been increased

[2178] Currently, its value is on average around 1,100,000 lire per month

[2179] or Additional pensionable emolument

[2180] diversified in relation to the salary level and supported by fixed and continuous contractual resources

[2181] • Accessory component | Operational employment allowance

[2182] specific allowance for FA personnel that compensates for the risks, inconveniences, and responsibilities associated with the specific activities performed in various employment situations

[2183] Operating allowances are divided into

[2184] fundamental and supplementary

[2185] Basic allowances are paid in relation to rank, length of service and the type of operational activity performed

[2186] In practice, these allowances are linked to the status or professionalism of the personnel and cannot be combined with each other (campaign, boarding, air navigation, airspace control

[2187] Supplementary allowances are granted in addition to the basic ones in relation to the actual performance of specific activities or to particular conditions of operational employment (marching allowance, out-of-office allowance, air emergency response, etc

[2188] Among the supplementary allowances is the command allowance, awarded to personnel who carry out command roles at various levels that involve high levels of responsibility

[2189] Optional or Extraordinary Component

[2190] compensates for service performances exceeding the normal weekly working hours

[2191] Hourly compensation is linked to salary and therefore to rank

[2192] Within each grade, it varies depending on whether the excess work was performed during the weekday daytime period, weekday nighttime period, holiday daytime service, or holiday nighttime service

[2193] assigned to staff based on family responsibilities and overall income

[2194] o Emoluments for transfers and missions

[2195] awarded to compensate for the inconveniences suffered during transfers between locations and to reimburse expenses incurred during isolated services provided outside the ordinary place of employment

[2196] Periodic adjustment of remuneration The economic contents of the employment relationship of military personnel, initially modifiable only by legislation for all personnel, are now adjusted differently depending on whether they are managerial or non-managerial personnel

[2197] For non-managerial personnel (up to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel), and within a framework of homogeneity between the Armed Forces and the Police Forces, delegated "contractual" procedures are envisaged to be carried out at the Civil Service Department and with the participation of the Personnel Representative Bodies

[2198] These procedures lead to the implementation by presidential decree of the contents of the “concertation” procedures, which refer every four years to regulatory aspects (service hours, leaves, leave of absence, travel and transfer payments, etc.) and every two years to economic aspects (salaries, allowances

[2199] Senior military personnel (Colonels and Generals), as well as police force managers, are not contracted

[2200] The remuneration is adjusted annually on a percentage basis to the average of the contractual improvements in public employment in the previous year

[2201] Finally, for military management, any changes to the regulatory framework and the establishment of new salary items (as well as financial adjustments other than the automatic annual ones) can only be pursued through legislation

[2202] The need to ensure adequate recognition of the specificities of the military's status, which acknowledges the quantity and quality of the work performed and is able to compensate for the inconveniences, is strongly felt

[2203] In this context, the following are included: Publications of the Peace Studies Center - the authorization granted to the Government to reintroduce salary parameters based on rank/qualification rather than salary levels for non-managerial personnel in the Security Sector, also with the aim of concretely differentiating the military pay structure from that of public employment; - the allowance in lieu of overtime for personnel in specific employment positions (the so-called "operational window"), which will allow operational and training activities to be carried out nationwide beyond normal working hours without burdensome administrative and bureaucratic formalities

[2204] Furthermore, the upcoming suspension of compulsory military service will certainly require the implementation of financial instruments to ensure a sufficient flow of volunteers, including both recruitment incentives and additional job market opportunities

[2207] treatment attributed to the employee who leaves service early due to resignation; • Disability (Privileged): pension treatment proportional to the percentage of permanent infirmities or impairments recognised as being due to service-related causes or a 10% increase in the ordinary pension

[2241] a basic public pension system (mandatory and “managed” by the State), a collective supplementary pension system (defined through employment contracts or concerted action), a “private” pension system (optional and linked to individual savings opportunities

[2249] Treatment of military personnel engaged in peacekeeping and humanitarian operations The participation of Italian military units in international peacekeeping and humanitarian missions outside the national territory is formally authorized by decree law, aimed at following up on commitments undertaken at the international level, regulating the methods of carrying out the missions and determining the financial coverage of the related costs

[2250] The mission authorization decree, and any subsequent extension decrees, establish the duration of the operation and the size of the military contingent deployed, and define the legal and financial status of the personnel, making reference to other regulatory provisions regarding legal, insurance, and social security aspects

[2251] With regard to economic treatment, the "1996 Finance Law" (Article 1, paragraph 63, of Law No. 549 of 28 December 1995) established some general principles for military interventions abroad

[2252] In particular, it was established that personnel belonging to "contingents" will be paid the daily allowance for missions abroad, provided for in the destination country, at a reduced percentage rate

[2253] As of January 1, 2000, this percentage has been set at 90% of the entire treatment by the legislative decrees that authorize the specific interventions

[2254] Furthermore, with regards to financing the operations, recourse is foreseen to the "fund for unexpected expenses" included in the Treasury Ministry's budget estimates

[2255] Of particular importance is the need to define a uniform regulatory framework for regulating the legal, insurance, salary, and social security aspects of personnel engaged in each mission, avoiding multiple, interconnected regulatory references that impair the readability of the texts

[2256] Furthermore, it is clear that it will be necessary to overcome the adjustment to the dollar in the future, given the upcoming introduction of the euro

[2281] The Military Representation (RM) was established with the “Rules of principle on military discipline” (Law no. 382/78) which, in summary, established the fundamental legislative principles relating to the rights/duties of military citizens and introduced Representative bodies into the military system for the first time

Publications of the Peace Studies Center Regarding the need for support for the families of military personnel engaged in out-of-area operations, one of the objectives has been to ensure the essential protection of the personnel employed in these delicate activities and, consequently, of their families, who undoubtedly experience psychological and material hardship comparable to that of most citizens

[2310] Supporting the families of personnel deployed on operations, considered a duty not only from a moral but also a functional perspective, is obviously affected by the limitations resulting from strict regulations that, even administratively, create limitations that are difficult to overcome

[2348] The Phenomenon of Hazing Publications Center for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ In 2000, the Defense Committee of the Chamber, for the first time for an institutional body of this level, addressed the problem of hazing in a thorough and systematic manner, ordering an investigative survey on the phenomenon

[2349] This particular attention, added to that of the leaders of the Armed Forces

[2350] forcefully affirmed the clear will of the institutions to address and resolve the problem of violence within military structures

[2351] It is not considered useful, in this context, to dwell on the sociological interpretation of hazing

[2352] Indeed, distinguished scholars have already expressed their views on this topic in the past through sociological analyses of the reasons for the deviant phenomenon, its nature, its dangers, and its connections with other forms of youth deviance that are widespread in schools, universities, sports, and the workplace

[2353] A common element in all these cases is the desire to bully and marginalize those who are weaker or considered "different" for the most disparate reasons

[2354] what matters is that there is a pretext, no matter what, to unleash the aggression

[2355] The Armed Forces, since they are closely connected to civil society – of which they represent a cross-section – are not immune to such degenerations which, indeed, in the world of military youth, combine and integrate, favored in this by greater promiscuity

[2358] under these conditions, the commitment of the Defense to counter violence within its own ranks, a commitment that is renewed every month with each new intake of recruits

[2360] This decisive awareness and stance, beyond any other consideration, represents an important step forward in the fight against hazing

[2361] an important struggle for the reaffirmation and re-establishment of legality, where violated, and to put an end to the serious damage that this phenomenon has caused, and still causes, to the image and credibility of the Armed Forces, which the military has progressively built at the cost of heavy sacrifices

[2362] This awareness, perhaps unique, was all the more important as it occurred at a time when the Armed Forces were, as they still are, engaged in a profound transformation that will lead them, in a short time, to a leaner configuration with markedly professional characteristics

[2363] Much remains to be done, however, to achieve the goal that everyone, both military and political authorities, have set themselves: the quality of life within the military, the serenity of young people, and attention to their problems, hardships, uncertainties, and needs during military service

[2364] Political authorities and military leaders are aware that the military of the future, based on entirely professional forces with a female component, will certainly benefit from more adequate measures to protect personnel, especially enlisted personnel

[2365] By doing so, young people will be assured of a peaceful environment, free from archaic forms of bullying, and one that will encourage them to pursue an interesting professional opportunity

[2366] This is the operation that the Armed Forces are carrying out, responding positively to requests from within and outside the military, initiating actions aimed at improving the overall image of the military world and the level of knowledge of it that young people normally derive from summary, and often preconceived, information

[2385] In this context, it was deemed essential to proceed with even greater vigor in achieving continuous training aimed at employment

[2386] This is in order to pursue the modern goal of abandoning the traditional, notional-based school model and replacing it with a "job-oriented" qualification, in order to have personnel with concrete know-how

[2387] The search for this type of training has led to the definition of an objective based training system which, inspired by criteria of pragmatism and realism, and continuously subjected to quality control, has at the same time guaranteed "civilian" recognition of the studies carried out at military institutes

[2406] Defense needs in the training sector

[2407] inter-force The key needs of the Defence in the field of inter-force training have been identified as

[2408] basic training and qualification/specialization, higher education, professionalization, continuing education, European training

[2409] Basic training and qualification/specialization The complexity of the materials and equipment supplied to the units requires the availability of specialized personnel capable of satisfying the multiple needs of use and efficiency

[2410] Each Armed Forces, which is responsible for preparing its own forces, therefore identifies the most suitable training courses to enable its personnel – in relatively short training times and in any case compatible with the correct training/operational activity ratio – to acquire the "skills" necessary for practical and operational use in the main contexts in which the Armed Forces find themselves operating

[2411] Referring to all military personnel, basic training and qualification/specialization provides for the preparation of the individual combatant, the Commander at the lower levels and the specialists

[2412] Higher education Higher education is part of the general education system, having as its basis the “basic education”, specific to FA

[2413] It represents the set of general cultural and technical-professional preparation activities, carried out within the framework of the Armed Forces and inter-force educational institutes, aimed at providing the Armed Forces Officers

[2414] the skills and competences necessary to hold positions of responsibility at various hierarchical levels within the General Staff and Armed Forces, joint and international commands, as well as to be able to carry out medium and high level command roles

[2415] Furthermore, higher education pursues the potential goal of acquiring the specific professional skills necessary to fill specific technical, managerial, or operational roles

[2416] In particular, it can be considered divided into: FA Specification

[2417] it is mainly expressed in the attendance of the SM/Normal Courses at the respective War Schools/Higher Institute of Maritime Studies; • Interforce and international

[2418] It is expressed through the attendance - by a quota of Officers, selected by their respective Armed Forces and designated by the Chief of Defense - of the Istituto Superiore di Stato Maggiore Interforze (ISSMI) and the Istituto Alti Studi per la Difesa (IASD

[2419] In this context, to acquire specific skills/competencies or for refresher courses, higher education can be integrated by attending "targeted" courses at the NATO School in Oberammergau, military schools in foreign countries, national universities, or private institutes

[2420] Professionalization The common trend among all modern complex organizations is to train their managers in an increasingly pragmatic and concrete manner

[2421] For the military commander - given the variety of possible fields of employment and the extreme indeterminacy of the problems, especially operational ones, that he may find himself facing - it is necessary to provide training that is more focused on the acquisition of problem-solving methods, with particular attention to the variability of the characterizing parameters

[2422] In the military profession, in fact, it is not always possible to apply managerial concepts and, at times, it is very difficult to align the choices made with cost-benefit criteria, given that, in the operational field, there exists a will openly opposed to the achievement of the pre-established objectives

[2423] It is therefore necessary to seek a compromise between specialized training and broad-spectrum preparation aimed at acquiring general skills and increasing analytical, synthesis, and conceptualization abilities

[2424] The pursuit of "know-how" therefore becomes the driving force behind the higher education design system, the effectiveness of which can be tangibly measured through the level of professional competence acquired

[2425] Publications Center for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ Making specific reference to the ISSMI course, a graduate cannot therefore limit himself to being just a bureaucrat trained to "do" and "apply" standardized procedures, but must also be able, once inserted into a SM, to understand its "function" and "rules" adapting them, with intelligence and a sense of responsibility, to the various situations

[2426] The modern concept of "continuing education" for managers assigns the institution the role of constantly and uninterruptedly updating the knowledge and skills of its managers through every possible teaching method (short courses, internships, lectures, conferences, involvement in training activities, distance learning, correspondence refresher courses, itinerant teaching positions, email, etc.), as well as the creation of new professional skills as they become necessary following doctrinal or employment developments

[2427] This project, currently being defined, will allow for the creation of a close bond between educational institutions and their students

[2428] European training Recently, the problems involving the Armed Forces

[2429] Italian operations are developing in a strategic and geographical context outside NATO's area of direct interest but of pre-eminent European and/or Mediterranean significance

[2430] The goal of creating an integrated military instrument at a European level must, therefore, be considered a high priority and, consequently, it appears necessary to make every effort to achieve it as soon as possible

[2431] The current political military reality, new strategies, and modern applied technologies constitute the parameters with which every military force will have to deal in order to achieve the necessary compatibility of employment with the peer structures of other countries

[2432] Such interoperability must be sought, first and foremost, in the areas of standardization of doctrines, procedures of use and means/materials but, above all, in the field of military culture, to be built through training of military leaders that is as common as possible, within a European context, at all levels

[2433] To this end, several measures are being studied to achieve this objective

[2434] In particular: • increase, at all levels, bilateral exchanges of students between basic training institutes in Europe

[2435] • develop joint activities with European and Mediterranean military training institutes, verifying the application of doctrine and increasing the use of standardized procedures and operational simulation

[2436] make attendance of courses held abroad by Italian students equal to those of the same level held in Italy

[2437] Verify the possibility of making this concept valid also for basic courses (Academies, Non-Commissioned Officer Schools, etc

[2438] • provide for the establishment of a higher education institution (modeled after the NATO Defense College in Rome) open to students from all European and Mediterranean countries. This institution, aimed at training military leadership, should achieve the following goals

[2439] pursue the amalgamation between future European military leaders, to be achieved also through direct knowledge of the personnel

[2440] • contribute in the long term to effective cohesion between European military units employed in “combined” missions under a different aegis than NATO

[2441] • develop and conduct courses at strategic and political-military levels, aimed at training, in the various fields of interest, officers (and possibly civilian managers) selected to fill relevant roles within the national military organisation and in the foreseeable future European defence organisation

[2442] European training also has significant implications for the military, and the Ministry of Defense is focusing particular attention on this topic, particularly with regard to the preparation and employment of volunteers upon completion of their military service. [2477] In particular, Article 17, paragraph 3 of the aforementioned Legislative Decree clearly outlines the actions to be implemented regarding vocational training and job placement for young armed forces members

[2478] The SMD is responsible for coordinating the activities that will be promoted, within the Technical Operations Area, for the creation of a synergistic device, between the SMD and the FA SMs, to be interfaced with the Office for the placement of discharged volunteer soldiers in LEVADIFE. The current training process for permanent service officers of the Normal Role (various Armed Forces, TRAMAT Armed Forces, Administration and Commissariat Corps, Engineer Corps and Medical Corps), develops through the following phases: • training; • qualification; • specialization; • professionalization

[2479] Training The training process for RN Officers, which aims to prepare young Officers from an ethical, cultural and technical perspective, providing them with all the necessary references to build a solid professional base, lasts approximately 5 years and includes, in succession, attendance at: • two years at the Military Academy of Modena, at the end of which the students obtain the appointment as Second Lieutenant (the training objective is to provide attendees with the ability to use the tools of individual combat, command a rifle team and operate within a patrol); • two years at the Application School of Turin (the training objective is to provide attendees with the ability to use the communication, doctrinal, procedural, methodological, logistical-administrative and technical tools to operate within the scope of the Force/Specialty/Corps to which they belong); • one year (the fifth) consisting of a Linguistic Improvement Course, a Technical Application Course at the relevant Weapons/Specialty Schools and Practical Internship at the Volunteer Training Regiments

[2480] The exception is made for Medical Corps Officers, who complete their entire university and technical-professional studies at the Military Academy of Modena

[2481] At the end of the aforementioned training process, the Officers obtain a degree

[2482] Qualification The qualification aims to enable Officers to acquire specific knowledge relating to the sector in which they are destined to operate, perfecting their military skills with reference to the Armed Forces/Specialty/Corps to which they belong

[2483] It takes place in the period from the end of the training phase to the General Staff Course (excluding) and focuses on: activities that have a common value, for the qualification of personnel approaching key employment milestones; activities diversified in content and of short duration (courses, seminars and refresher courses), aimed both at constantly keeping the knowledge base updated and at acquiring further skills related to the tasks to be carried out

[2484] Specialization The specialization phase aims to provide Officers with specific knowledge and basic skills to operate effectively at the Commands of Large National and International Units

[2485] Specialization is initially achieved through the mandatory General Staff Course lasting approximately five months at the Turin School of Application. At the end of this course, a voluntary portion of the attendees, composed of officers who have demonstrated adequate skills, aptitude, and professionalism, are admitted to the Multi-Thematic Course, lasting approximately five months, held at the University of Turin and the School of Application

[2486] The training objective of the SM Course is to prepare attendees for employment as Staff Officers at the level of a Large Elementary Unit, while the Plurithematic Course is aimed at providing the skills to operate as Staff Officers within the intermediate and top Commands of the Armed Forces

[2487] Those who have passed the General Staff Course and the Plurithematic Course obtain the Master's Degree in Strategic Sciences

[2488] After attending the General Staff Course, a number of Officers may be eligible to attend (on a voluntary basis) the Joint General Staff Advanced Course (ISSMI) at the Centro Alti Studi Difesa (Center for Advanced Defence Studies). The training objective of this course is to prepare participants to operate within the joint command structures

[2489] Another group of Officers (the largest) is instead destined for employment in specialized sectors (staff positions, military teachers, instructors, positions in Technical Directorates, etc.), after attending “ad hoc” courses, both nationally and abroad

[2490] For the ISSMI Course, interested personnel are selected through a procedure that also includes a correspondence language course, at the end of which participants are subjected to a diagnostic test to verify their learning

[2491] Those who pass the aforementioned course are admitted to an intensive phase at the Army Foreign Language School

[2492] Subsequently, as part of the selection process in question, the Officers attend a Qualification Course at the War School (lasting approximately 2 months), preceded by a “remote” phase

[2493] Professionalization completes the training process of Officers

[2494] It is aimed essentially at officers destined for employment in General Staffs, in international commands and, subsequently, in high management positions

[2495] This phase begins with attendance at the Joint General Staff Advanced Training Course (ISSMI) and continues with other training and/or refresher courses aimed at the specific tasks to be fulfilled. As can be seen from the context just outlined, the high level of basic training of military personnel and the ever-increasing complexity of the sectors in which they are called upon to operate have led the Armed Forces to establish a dense, constantly expanding network of collaborations with the university world for undergraduate and postgraduate courses for officers and warrant officers

[2496] In these collaborations, the Army does not act as a mere "user", but rather as an active participant in a fruitful cultural exchange

[2497] In fact, the courses referred to in the agreements in question - all open to interested civilian students - are also conducted using military teachers, appointed by the University Institutes on the recommendation of the Armed Forces

[2518] Non-Commissioned Officers Role of Marshals In relation to the increased cultural level of conscripts and volunteers, and the split of the category of Non-Commissioned Officers into the roles of Sergeants and Marshals, Marshals have been attributed functions and responsibilities that were previously the property of junior officers (for example, platoon command) and require greater cultural and professional skills than in the past

[2531] The training of such personnel is carried out directly at the deployment units using modular criteria and includes 3 successive "levels of preparation", coinciding with as many operational deployment profiles

[2532] In particular, the aforementioned levels of preparation are divided as follows

[2533] • 1st level of preparation (after 7-11 weeks), which confers the ability to survive on the battlefield, carry out security and self-defense tasks, as well as fulfill all the functions connected to the assigned task (or to the 2nd task for personnel already in conscription and confirmed in the previously held task

[2534] Upon completion, the VFA can be employed in general surveillance and escort services, in interventions to benefit the community in the event of public disasters, in territorial control operations in conjunction with the police forces, as well as in logisticaladministrative activities for the life and functioning of the departments

[2535] • 2nd degree of preparation (after 11-17 weeks

[2536] which ensures the VFA's ability to carry out tasks related to its employment in low-intensity peace support operations and humanitarian assistance interventions outside the national territory

[2537] • 3rd level of preparation (after 8-10 months

[2538] which integrates and perfects the operational capabilities already acquired in the previous levels of preparation, through the development of technical-tactical activities connected with the use of smaller units in combat, even in particular environments, within the scope of the relevant Force/Specialty

[2539] Depending on the awarding of the three levels of preparation, the training process is divided into three training phases divided into training modules

[2540] The first phase, relating to the 1st level of preparation, is divided into 4 modules: basic training (1-2 weeks); individual combat training (1-3 weeks); task specialization training (on average 4 weeks

[2543] For Specialization Courses lasting longer than average (4 weeks) and held at operational regiments, the related activities will continue and can be completed at the destination operational companies

[2544] Phase 1 activities must be carried out intensively and without interruption, involving the participation of all relevant personnel

[2545] The second phase, connected with the achievement of the 2nd level of preparation, is divided into 2 modules

[2546] corporals course (2 weeks

[2548] Phase 2 activities, which are mandatory for reaching the 2nd level of preparation and for subsequent deployment even "outside the area," are conducted intensively and without interruption, requiring the participation of all personnel

[2549] The third phase, in which the 3rd level of preparation is reached, is divided into several modules: - specific training for the weapon/specialty (6-8 weeks

[2550] training in specific environments (3 weeks); - improvement and training of smaller units (6-7 weeks

[2593] The preparation is divided into three closely related levels

[2594] • the first level concerns all units regardless of their typology and concerns preparation for the conduct of war operations, understood in the classical sense

[2595] • the second level is differentiated in relation to the "package" to which the units belong and refers to the activities necessary to bring the instrument to conduct the planned and foreseeable operations within the framework of the fulfillment of the other two strategic functions, "presence and surveillance" and "defense of external interests and contribution to international security

[2596] The third level finalizes the preparation for a specific operational plan and concerns exclusively the units pre-designated for intervention in a specific operation for which all the elements of interest are known

[2597] These activities are developed within an operational cycle, identifiable as a circuit that begins before the deployment of forces, continues during the mission and ends upon return from the theatre of operation for reconditioning, to then begin again in anticipation of a new commitment

[2598] Operating cycle The operating cycle of a department develops in four phases

[2599] General preparation

[2600] During this period, the unit carries out preparation activities called 1st and 2nd level, aimed at acquiring the capabilities required for the category of forces in which it is included (projection, reaction, presence and surveillance

[2601] During this phase, moreover, a unit can be temporarily placed in a “ready to deploy” condition (units which are maintained at a high state of readiness on a rotational basis

[2602] Under these conditions, the training/education activities developed by the departments are significantly affected, related to the need to be able to be projected into operations within the timeframes envisaged by the various alert states

[2603] The duration of this phase varies depending on the operational commitments in progress

[2604] Preparation for the execution of an order This is the condition in which the departments designated for a specific mission find themselves, for which all the situational elements are known, which allow for specific preparation (3rd level preparation) aimed at fulfilling the assigned task

[2605] With regard to "out-of-area" operations, this phase includes the implementation of coordination and mission-specific training activities, preparatory to entering the theater

[2606] The duration of this phase is in the order of 4 months

[2607] Deployment This is the “highlight” of the operational cycle, the phase in which the department must implement what has been acquired in the previous phases, conducting a real verification of its operational capabilities

[2608] Furthermore, during the deployment, activities are carried out aimed at maintaining individual training and unit training up to platoon/company level, also using the available simulation systems

[2609] Reconditioning after use

[2610] In this phase, activities aimed at restoring the unit to full operational efficiency are developed, with particular reference to: • psychological and physical recovery; • extraordinary maintenance of vehicles, materials, and equipment; • verification of operational capabilities

[2611] Command and Unit Training In the context examined so far, training plays a crucial role, capable of influencing the development of the operational cycle

[2612] To properly finalize the preparation of the units, it is necessary to conduct a series of training events which, linked together according to a sequential logic, allow the achievement of the training objectives set by NATO STANDARDS, which then translate into operational capabilities

[2613] In this situation, in addition to individual training, different types of training activities have been defined, aimed at: Command Training. This can essentially be defined as a group training of the Command's cadres who apply specific procedures, in line with the specific NATO directives

[2614] Unit Training Unit training, a phase which naturally follows individual training, is essentially identified in the conduct of exercises, both in open fire and live fire, which, with a view to progressive difficulty and complexity, are aimed at acquiring and verifying the operational capacity of a unit in relation to the type of troop personnel (VSP, VFB, VFA and conscript) with which it is supplied and, consequently, to its category of belonging

[2615] In particular, the following are distinguished

[2616] or training of units supplied with conscripts; or training of units supplied with volunteers on annual service

[2618] The organization and execution of training involves ascertaining and evaluating, throughout its various phases, the improvements achieved and the results achieved, with a view to constantly applying (at all levels) the concept of "lessons learned", for the progressive elimination of deficiencies and gaps

[2619] Therefore, widespread and continuous monitoring is essential, and must have educational rather than purely fiscal purposes

[2620] The aspects to be taken into consideration for the checks are: • "operational" efficiency of the staff

[2621] • individual knowledge of weapons

[2622] • shooting training level

[2623] • formal structure of the units

[2626] To achieve these objectives, the Armed Forces conduct various exercises abroad, particularly in Hungary, Lithuania, Romania, Poland, Bulgaria, Tunisia, Egypt, and Sweden. These exercises test, for Brigade-level units, firstly the forward deployment capability achieved, and secondly the ability to manage crisis situations

[2627] These activities abroad, in 2001, involved approximately 10,000 men including Officers, Non-Commissioned Officers and Volunteers

[2629] Navy 6.1.2.1 Officers

[2630] The training process for Officers is developed through the following fundamental steps: basic training, initial training (Qualification Courses), intermediate training (Specialization Courses), advanced training (Normal Master's Degree Course and Joint Master's Degree Advanced Course). Basic training is carried out at the Naval Academy through: five-year courses leading to a specialist degree, in agreement with the Universities of Pisa, Genoa, Trieste and Naples, for Officers of the Normal Role; applied courses lasting one academic year for Directly Appointed Officers and Officers of the Special Role, a 3-month course for Reserve Officers

[2631] The review of the Officers' training process began with the adaptation of the basic training programs, an action also affected by the profound regulatory changes in the university education sector

[2632] Having confirmed the inadequacy of the purely technical-scientific study path, abandoned in the mid-1990s, we have proceeded to integrate it into the legal, political economic and historical-social fields

[2633] Indeed, while on the one hand, a solid mathematical and scientific foundation is essential to operate consciously in a highly technological environment and utilize resources to their full potential, on the other, there is an opportunity to broaden one's cultural horizons to include law, politics, and sociology. This will enhance the understanding of the realities of the areas of intervention and enable personnel to operate even in nonbelligerent, often unplanned, situations, in a context where even individual behaviors have public and international relevance

[2634] The operations carried out in this context have ultimately influenced and intensified the relations between the Armed Forces and the country's civil society, sensitive to the need for "stability and security" in its region and to the contribution that, as members of the international community, they are able to make, ultimately requiring more solid preparation in the sector of communication and public information

[2635] At the same time, the need to direct the preparation of tomorrow's Commander and Manager towards notions of economics, logistics and administration was considered

[2636] The definition of the training requirement described above and the regulatory requirement that fulltime officers obtain a degree initially constituted two objectives that were not exactly coincident, forcing us to pursue difficult compromise solutions to be negotiated with the relevant universities

[2637] On the occasion of the recent University Reform, a dedicated degree class was finally established, called "Defense and Security Sciences

[2638] This measure has enabled the activation of "tailor-made" study courses for the Navy, significantly changing the negotiating position with universities, which nevertheless remain the sole holders of the right to issue qualifications

[2639] In particular, the 2001/02 academic year saw the inauguration of the new degree course in “Maritime and Naval Sciences”, offered in agreement with the University of Pisa for the benefit of the Officers of the General Staff Corps

[2640] The subsequent training sessions, aimed at completing the specific preparation for placement of personnel in the various Operational Departments, build on the foundations laid during the basic training period

[2641] The organization of these Departments generally provides for two levels of employment with increasing responsibility

[2642] The specialist training is therefore structured in two phases: initial training, aimed at taking on the role of Head of Naval Unit Component (and corresponding roles in other Departments

[2643] it is achieved through Qualification Courses, lasting a maximum of six months, held at the Navy Training Centres (Naval, Submarine, Air, Amphibious, Incursion and Underwater, Mining and Mine Countermeasures, Hydrographic) and attended jointly by all Officers of the Normal Role and Special Role; • intermediate training, aimed at taking on the role of Head of Naval Unit Department (and corresponding roles in other Departments

[2644] it is achieved through Specialization Courses, lasting a maximum of one year, held at the Navy Training Centres, the Naval Academy and/or Armed Forces or joint forces institutes, both national and foreign

[2645] they are attended by almost all the Officers of the Normal Role and, on a selective basis, by some Officers of the Special Role

[2646] A limited number of officers, assigned to study and planning tasks for the acquisition of new vehicles and materials, subsequently complete their specialist training with university-level courses at military and civilian institutes, both national and foreign

[2647] Front-line employment in Operational Departments involves Officers for approximately a decade, at the end of which the promotion to the rank of Senior Officer opens up the prospect of employment in staff positions, in the Armed Forces and joint forces, both national and international

[2648] The required change of pace is supported by advanced training programs, developed in two stages at the Institute of Maritime Military Studies (Standard Course of SM) and at the ISSMI (Advanced Course of SM Interforces

[2649] The Standard SM Course is held for the benefit of the Standard Role Officers of all Corps

[2650] It lasts 3 months and constitutes a fundamental moment of connection between the different paths followed, aimed at

[2651] • to the acquisition of the Staff working procedures

[2652] • to the updating and in-depth study of geostrategic and geoeconomic knowledge, with particular reference to the specific dimension of each FA; • to the application of the “method” for the planning and study of operational, logistical, ordering and organizational problems

[2653] Advanced training continues, on a selective basis, with the Joint Staff Advanced Course, aimed at assuming important roles in the Armed Forces and joint forces, both nationally and internationally

[2654] Finally, it is integrated, for the benefit of Officers designated to Command and Management roles, with specific refresher/indoctrination training modules, lasting 2-3 weeks and carried out in the form of seminars

[2655] Adopting the same principle of progressive and harmonious development envisaged for Officers, we proceeded to plan a training program aimed at professional growth, with reference to Legislative Decree 196/95 and the subsequent amendments made by Legislative Decree

[2656] The new professional figure requires a higher level of modular training than in the past, aimed at creating "high" profile specialists who, particularly in the Marshal Role, are capable of leading groups of men

[2657] Publications of the Peace Studies Centre. In the context of the topic, the innovation introduced in the basic training of the new Marshals is highlighted, consisting of a two-year course at the FA Schools for the winners of specific competitions for recruitment from the outside world, aimed at young people in possession of a secondary school diploma, with the possibility of enrolling in university courses

[2658] During this initial training phase, we provide the basic knowledge needed to successfully perform second-level roles (Coordinator and/or Controller), along with technical and professional knowledge, diversified according to the candidate's specialization

[2659] The training period is followed by various subsequent moments, such as the Practical Internship and any Qualification Courses on the specific equipment/systems of interest, in order to allow the Marshal to quickly integrate into new work contexts

[2660] This course is of paramount importance to the Air Force and represents an essential and crucial step in the career progression, characterized by strong continuity with previous personal experiences. It lays the foundation for subsequent career development. This is essential to the future success, efficiency, and effectiveness of the organization itself, as it addresses all aspects of a Marshal's career, particularly military ethics, the art of command, and physical/sporting/seafaring skills, as well as cultural and specialized knowledge

[2661] The subsequent stages of the training will be connected and will fit into what has already been acquired during the basic training process

[2662] A further determining aspect of the new professional figure emerges from the reference legislation

[2663] This refers to personnel in the top ranks of the aforementioned Marshals Role (First Marshals and Lieutenants), who must be able to be employed, in substitution of lower officers, in positions of greater responsibility and with a particularly competitive professional profile in relation to the "civilian" world

[2664] Another significant development is the planned addition of female personnel to the role of Marshals, who will be involved in training at the FA Institutes

[2665] Troops For the troops, it is necessary to continue the planning work aimed at technical-military training, differentiated according to the specialization of the individual soldier, together with the evaluation of the psychological profile and an additional training module such as "full immersion", to provide them with the knowledge that may prove useful for their possible subsequent entry into the world of work

[2666] Also for this type of personnel, starting in 2003 and for a foreseeable quota of 500 units, the opportunity for women to enter the annual competitions for Short-Term Volunteer Troops (VFB/V3) is foreseen

[2667] Training Activities To maintain the operational efficiency of the Forces, ordinary training of naval units at national level requires an average stay away from their normal deployment locations of around three months/year (to which must be added international activities – NATO, EU or multinational - actual operations, presence and surveillance activities, etc

[2668] Training also takes the form of live fire activities, where the ordinary ammunition consumption is in the order of 100 rounds/year for each embarked artillery installation, an activity which also allows for the verification of accuracy in shooting against ground targets (limited to the 127/54 calibre and carried out at the Capo Teulada range), in anti-aircraft shooting (conducted on remote controlled targets or on a sleeve towed by aircraft) and anti-ship shooting (on fast radio controlled targets or on targets towed by another naval unit

[2669] Missile launch activities by naval units are carried out at the joint experimental range in Perdasdefogu, on an annual or biennial basis depending on the type of unit and the missile used

[2670] Last but not least, as regards training in underwater warfare (submarine and anti-submarine activities), torpedo launching activities are conducted on an annual basis for naval units and every six months for submarines

[2671] For the amphibious force, in particular, training also involves the consumption of approximately 1,500–2,000 rounds per marine rifleman, divided into the various calibers (pistol, submachine gun, machine gun, etc

[2672] The unit's live fire training also involves launching an average of twenty anti-tank missiles per year

[2673] The overall efficiency of naval units and departments is monitored through the “system for continuous monitoring of force efficiency”

[2674] The data relating to this efficiency and their processing allow us to establish annual merit rankings based on the level of training achieved

[2675] For individual naval units and departments, qualitative efficiency reflects the level of training of the personnel and the efficiency of the materials, while quantitative efficiency refers to the actual presence of personnel with respect to war tables and the actual quantity of material with respect to war supplies

[2676] The score thus calculated is associated with the relative degree of readiness

[2677] • 1st grade - Unit/department unconditionally ready to carry out a war mission

[2678] • 2nd grade - Unit/department ready to carry out a war mission with some limitations

[2679] • 3rd grade - Unit/department ready to carry out a war mission with significant limitations

[2680] • 4th grade - Unit/department not ready for war mission

[2681] The overall preparedness of the Armed Forces is evaluated by considering the degree of overall efficiency, obtained by adding together the scores assigned to the overall efficiency of individual naval units and departments

[2682] Training/efficiency level control activities are implemented through the Armed Forces chain of command

[2683] Each commander is responsible for evaluating the efficiency of his own unit or department, based on appropriate directives issued by higher commands

[2684] The Taranto Navy Training Centre carries out evaluations and checks on the training of units through the TIRNAVs (Naval Internships) and the CLA (Training Level Control

[2685] TIRNAVs are carried out at the end of long-term maintenance stops, while CLAs represent an additional training phase when, following an inspection, deficiencies are found in one or more sectors

[2686] Mine countermeasures specialist units carry out checks called CBE (war effectiveness checks), carried out by the Sweeping Forces Command, to evaluate the combat readiness of the aforementioned units according to a pre-established test programme

[2687] The training methodologies used in the aforementioned centers are similar to those used at the Basic Operational Sea Training and the Joint Maritime Course of the British Navy and the Mine Warfare Operational Sea Training developed by the Belgian and Dutch Navies, centers considered leaders in NATO in their specific sectors and also used by the Italian Navy for appropriate evaluation and comparison activities

[2688] The training is also integrated through the use of specific simulators for: the conduct of naval unit maneuvers for young officers at the Naval Academy in Livorno; the use of various forms of naval air combat for the Commands of the Naval Units and their staff, at the tactical simulator of the Training Center in Taranto; the use of most of the embarked weapon systems through specific simulation programs present in the systems themselves; shooting in particular conditions of use for the riflemen of the Amphibious Force at a specific simulator in Brindisi; the management and conduct of underwater units, for the benefit of submarine personnel, at the Underwater Forces Command

[2689] The Armed Forces also use Army-owned simulators for tank combat training by amphibious force personnel, according to times and methods agreed upon between the two Armed Forces

[2690] As regards the ranges and training areas, these are sufficient, except for those connected to training for complex amphibious activities, for which only the Capo Teulada range, owned by the Army, is available, which is unable to fully satisfy the needs of the Armed Forces

[2691] Air Force Officers The training of all personnel is divided into a basic and an advanced course

[2692] This subdivision arises from the need to first provide those essential and indispensable elements of cultural, technical-professional and military knowledge, commensurate with the performance of the tasks and duties that will be assigned in the initial years of the career

[2693] Subsequently, the advanced program aims to perfect and specialize military personnel called upon to carry out tasks of greater responsibility and increasing importance that cannot be separated from more rigorous training

[2694] Training, therefore, no longer confined to a very limited period of time and no longer reduced to a set of oneoff notions, becomes an integral part of professional life, a tool for growth and deepening, and an important opportunity for that ideal osmosis that allows the exchange of information between the Air Force, the institutes, the attendees, and vice versa

[2695] The training of Officers, whose objective is cultural, moral, professional and ethical growth, must provide the necessary tools so that they can best perform the functions of their rank, to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the FA and, furthermore, be capable of anticipating and managing change

[2696] He must aspire to acquire an “open mind” aimed at solving problems

[2698] or it is differentiated by role

[2701] or is aimed at providing the necessary knowledge to carry out the assigned tasks

[2753] It should be emphasized that the current minimum quota restrictions are difficult to reconcile with the needs of the Operational Departments for advanced training

[2754] Restrictions have forced the development of activities abroad, in areas that allow the simulation of war missions, such as the flight program at Goose Bay in Canada

[2755] The search for such areas also concerns the Mediterranean, where possibilities are currently being studied that would allow for realistic training activities outside national borders, taking off from Italian bases

[2756] Thanks to the advanced technologies available, the Armed Forces of many countries are planning to transfer substantial parts of their training from aircraft to simulators, ranging from basic and advanced training, to tactical events, such as in-flight refueling and weapon release in firing ranges, to training and maintenance

[2757] Generally, the sector that can benefit most from simulation is basic training

[2758] In fact, although some of the basic procedures and operations can be performed on systems comparable to commercial personal computers with an extremely high cost-effectiveness ratio, the situation is different when it comes to advanced training

[2759] In fact, to carry out the normal procedures of an advanced training phase, systems are needed that reproduce real performances with great fidelity

[2760] Consequently, costs increase and a careful evaluation of the cost/effectiveness ratio of the simulators to be purchased compared to carrying out training operations on commercial aircraft is necessary (for example, some modern flight simulators allow the element being trained to be qualified on the machine at "zero hours", i.e. without carrying out any dedicated flights on the real airplane) even if the costs are so high (a simulator of this kind can cost as much as two new aircraft), that the purchase of the simulator is not recommended unless there is a significant number of crews to train

[2761] This statement emerges from a mere economic and operational assessment of the problem and can be modified by evaluating the environmental and noise pollution issues that could make the necessary investment worthwhile

[2762] It should not be overlooked that international experience shows that the extensive use of advanced simulation, however realistic, deprives crews of the essential personal experience of the operations carried out

[2763] Current training plans include extensive use of basic simulation capabilities and timely use of advanced simulation for combat lines

[2764] In particular, the use of advanced simulators (capable of reproducing complex situations) allows crews to be trained in the use of the machine, at the limits of performance and in threat conditions that cannot be reproduced in reality. Furthermore, in the future, it will be possible to connect the simulators of the different bases to a network so as to obtain joint training of distant departments, benefiting standardization and interoperability

[2765] A further benefit of the basic simulation is the possibility of using part of it for the purposes of disseminating the image of the Armed Forces

[2772] Non-commissioned officers The enactment of Legislative Decree no. 196/1995 and subsequent amendments made by Legislative Decree

[2773] led to a new division of the non-commissioned officer personnel of the Armed Forces

[2774] creating new roles and modifying their recruitment, status and advancement rules

[2775] The decree, among other things, has established new duties and responsibilities which, to be fulfilled effectively, require adequate professional and military training

[2776] In this context, training takes on fundamental importance, the aim of which is to provide military, cultural, moral and technical-professional education

[2777] Even for non-managerial staff, training

[2778] it focuses on multiple training “moments”

[2779] • constitutes the right balance between the set of specifically technical-professional knowledge and the set of military knowledge

[2780] The first characteristics of each individual specialty, the second are common to all; • provides the essential knowledge so that everyone is able to operate in their own sector of employment with competence and professionalism

[2781] • meets the real needs of the Armed Forces; • takes into account the cultural level of the recipient of the training event

[2782] In particular, the design of the Marshals' training role necessarily had to take into account the new responsibilities assigned to this role

[2783] No longer, therefore, a purely specialized training aimed only at the acquisition of technical knowledge, but a “higher” level training essential to be able to carry out tasks that involve the command, management and direction of small units

[2784] This is ensured through a two-year course at the Italian Air Force Non-Commissioned Officers' School in Caserta. [2785] A second year, therefore, more dedicated to the acquisition of professional knowledge, culminating in a series of internships in the maintenance and/or training departments in which the theoretical phase carried out at the Caserta institute is concretized through practical activities

[2790] The course aims to provide participants with the military, professional, and cultural preparation appropriate to their new status and to provide the know-how necessary to carry out executive roles with direct and personal responsibility in the maintenance, operational, and support sectors

[2791] The program was designed to achieve the objectives set while taking into account that the participants come from the Volunteer Role and already possess, albeit to a limited extent, certain military and professional knowledge

[2900] A NEW CONCEPT

[2901] PROSPECTS ROLE OF STAFF REPRESENTATIVES Civilian personnel The Defence structure includes within it a significant and valid civilian component

[2902] In relation to the ongoing restructuring processes, just as military personnel will be reduced from 385,880 in 1985 to 190,000 in the near future, so civilian personnel will have to reach 43,000 by 2005, from 53,000 in 1985—distributed between functional and managerial personnel

[2903] The functions of the civilian component are mainly administrative and partly technical, all aimed at supporting the military instrument as a whole

[2904] The employees in question are managed by the General Directorate for Civilian Personnel, established in 1997 with the simultaneous suppression of the pre-existing General Directorates for Employees and Workers

[2905] Civilian personnel, in relation to the significant reduction in the military component, are destined to assume an ever-increasing importance over time at all organizational levels, both central and peripheral

[2906] The civilian personnel headcount was set by Legislative Decree no. 265/1997 at 43,000 units, to be reached upon completion of the restructuring process and "in any case within eight years of the entry into force of the same Legislative Decree" (August

[2907] The first redetermination of the workforce in the above-mentioned reductionist perspective was carried out with the Prime Ministerial Decree of 26 June 1998, which established the total workforce at 45,740 units. Of this total, 40,304 employees were present as of 1 June 2001, with a shortfall of 2,696 compared to the planned workforce (43,000 units

[2913] It is clear that fully filling staffing shortages through external recruitment will require taking into account the associated costs and the financial resources required to address them

[2914] However, the aforementioned shortages could also be addressed by implementing the training programs provided for by the National Collective Bargaining Agreement (CCNL), which would allow, with the professional advancement of employees, a more rapid replenishment of staffing needs, especially among higher level professionals

[2917] This measure, while maintaining the spending constraints on civilian personnel, must take into account the new employment positions emerging from ongoing restructuring, which have identified a significant need for medium- to high-level qualifications. This arises, on the one hand, from the need to acquire new skills, especially in the technical and IT sectors, and on the other from the expected progressive replacement of military personnel with civilian personnel for logistical and administrative support functions
