[2919] TECHNICAL-ADMINISTRATIVE AND TECHNICAL-INDUSTRIAL AREA TECHNICAL-OPERATIONAL AREA 7.3.2 One aspect that deserves reflection and that will have to be addressed in order to reduce, within physiological limits, the obstacles that stand in the way of a greater use of civilian personnel within the new professional structure of the Armed Forces is certainly to be identified in the non-optimal distribution of the same across the territory

[2920] Indeed, despite areas oversized in terms of civilian personnel, there are also critically understaffed areas. On the other hand, personnel mobility, if kept within acceptable limits, generally meets with little resistance

[2921] If, on the contrary, it were to be used as a general tool to address essential needs, it would encounter insurmountable obstacles, both due to the physiological reaction of the staff, who see consolidated family, housing, relational, and income situations compromised, and due to the current inability of the Administration to reduce the inconveniences resulting from a new placement to acceptable levels

[2922] Recourse to external structures (Outsourcing) Some services that must necessarily be ensured (in particular cleaning services, canteens, etc.) for their performance require tasks that are no longer attractive to Defence employees in the current socio-cultural context

[2923] Nevertheless, organizational models require such performances

[2924] Hence the need to resort to external companies that guarantee such services

[2925] Furthermore, opening up to the outside world synergistic forms of private work contributions can also have beneficial effects on reducing the management costs of certain services

[2926] Therefore, outsourcing opportunities must be carefully evaluated, whether due to financial constraints or the objective impossibility of having the necessary human resources

[2927] But sometimes even higher professional skills, if absent from the Defense organization due to the need to meet the needs of the Administration, may have to be outsourced (computerization of technical services, design of engineering services

[2928] Therefore, in these cases, it is not so much cost containment that is important, but rather the unavoidable need to pursue and achieve institutional goals

[2929] In this context, it will be necessary to verify the existence of suitable professional figures to manage and ensure the implementation of the structure established by Article 5, paragraph 1, of Law No. 331 of 16 November 2000, which will provide employment for discharged volunteer military personnel

[2931] a new concept

[2932] Perspectives Various elements can influence the ability to ensure a Defence performance that meets internal and external expectations

[2933] But beyond the numbers, the figures, the recruitment and promotion systems, an irreplaceable and decisive element can only be identified in the subjective response that each person is called upon to give in their work activity

[2934] Until now, there has probably been a lack of a personnel policy that, in addition to management—which should not be underestimated, given the positive effects it can produce if carefully implemented in terms of timely and effective administrative action—envisions the development of human resources

[2935] The valorization of the individual, when inserted in a work context, constitutes a multiplier of performance, both in qualitative and quantitative terms

[2936] There is no doubt that the sum of the performances thus achieved optimizes the system

[2937] Particular attention must be paid above all to identifying the so-called "key resources", understood as units that are potentially called upon to play a decisive role in making the Defence function competitive

[2938] Obviously, everyone, without distinction, at every level, is required to cope with the dynamics of the organization so that it, in constant evolution, maintains the high profile of the institutional image

[2939] Hence the need, on a personal level, to set daily goals that, in a temporal sequence, can achieve the Administration's primary objectives

[2940] Even long-term goals require the achievement of short- and medium-term goals

[2941] All of this can be of great help, on the one hand, by rediscovering the awareness of belonging to an Administration that, more than ever, is called upon, both nationally and internationally, to express a calm determination in its actions; on the other, by assuming, at the highest levels of responsibility, consistent behaviors that interpret values to be strengthened and transmitted to all collaborators, in a renewed spirit of common action involving the entire working community

[2942] Role of employee representatives Employee representatives also have a significant role to play

[2943] The appreciated work of national and local trade unions has enabled us to achieve, despite at times physiological difficulties and divergent points of view, positive results in launching the reform process, whose progress has not yet been finalised. Further reflections on the topic will be conducted, which is why the Government has requested a delegation from Parliament to update an initial intuition, which must be verified and aligned with changing situations and events that push in directions that may differ from those initially envisioned

[2944] Union participation, beyond the formulas that only abstractly seem to strengthen its role, is essentially based on dialogue and discussion

[2945] It is in the dialectic of the parties, in the strength of their motivations, and in the need to achieve certain goals that we must find the resulting solutions that best balance the various interests at stake

[2946] Therefore, there is no prejudice in addressing, together with the Union, problems that affect the future of the Administration and whose repercussions also affect the staff

[2947] The path will be easier to the extent that we understand that we are proceeding side by side in the awareness of a path whose destination is common

[2949] STATISTICS

[2950] JUDICIAL PERSONNEL 8.6 NON-JUDICIAL PERSONNEL 8.7 ASSIGNMENT OF MILITARY PERSONNEL 8.8 ESTABLISHMENT OF MILITARY JUDICIAL POLICE SECTIONS 8.9 THE MILITARY PENITENTIARY ORGANIZATION (OPM – EXECUTIVE BODIES) 8.10 CONSIDERATIONS 8.11 APPLICATION OF THE MILITARY PENAL CODE IN PEACE (AND NOT WAR) DURING MILITARY MISSIONS ABROAD – PROBLEMATIC ASPECTS 8.1 General The Minister of Defense has, with respect to military magistrates and the Council of the Military Judiciary, CMM, the same powers that the Minister of Justice has with respect to the Superior Council of the Judiciary (CSM), and ordinary magistrates

[2951] Article 103 of the Constitution grants military courts jurisdiction, in peacetime, over military crimes committed by members of the Armed Forces

[2952] Law No. 180 of May 7, 1981, introduced a series of changes to the military judicial system

[2953] Council of the Military Judiciary The CMM, a self-governing body, was subsequently regulated by Presidential Decree No. 158 of March

[2954] In order to guarantee the same independence recognized to ordinary judges, the Council has, as already mentioned, the same powers as the CSM, including those concerning disciplinary proceedings against military magistrates

[2955] The CMM is, in fact, competent to deliberate on any state provision regarding military magistrates and on any other matter devolved to it by law

[2956] In particular, it decides on the hiring of members of the Military Judiciary, the assignment of offices and functions, transfers, promotions, disciplinary sanctions, and the assignment of extrajudicial duties to military magistrates

[2957] expresses opinions and can make proposals to the Minister of Defense on changes to military judicial districts and on all matters concerning the organization or functioning of services relating to military justice

[2958] gives opinions on bills concerning problems in the judicial sector

[2959] On matters within the Council's jurisdiction, the Minister of Defense may advance proposals, propose observations, and may attend Council meetings, when requested by the President or when he deems it appropriate, to make announcements or provide clarifications

[2960] The Minister, however, cannot be present at the deliberations

[2961] The Council - which holds office for 4 years - includes

[2962] the first president of the Court of Cassation, who presides over it

[2963] the military attorney general at the Court of Cassation

[2964] five members elected by military magistrates, of whom at least one is a military magistrate of the Court of Cassation

[2965] two members external to the military judiciary, chosen by agreement between the Presidents of the two Chambers from among full university professors in legal subjects and lawyers with at least fifteen years of professional practice

[2966] one of them is elected by the Council as Vice President

[2967] The current Council - which is the fourth since the founding law - took office on 31 July

[2968] Military judicial organization Military judicial offices are divided into prosecuting bodies (Military Attorney General's Office at the Supreme Court of Cassation

[2969] General Prosecutor's Office at the Military Court of Appeal and Military Prosecutors' Offices at the Military Courts) and adjudicating bodies (Military Court of Appeal, Military Courts and Military Surveillance Court

[2970] Each military court, a judicial body of the first instance, has an office for the preliminary investigation judge and an office for the preliminary hearing judge. Their organization is no different from the corresponding offices existing in ordinary courts

[2971] Pursuant to law 180/81, military tribunals judge with the intervention of the president of the military tribunal, who presides over it or, in case of impediment, of a military appeals magistrate, with the function of president

[2972] of a military magistrate of a tribunal or of appeal, with the functions of a judge

[2973] of a soldier of one of the Armed Forces

[2974] or of the Guardia di Finanza, of equal rank to that of the accused and in any case not lower than the rank of officer, drawn by lot, with judicial functions

[2975] The Military Court of Appeal, established by Article 3 of Law No. 180 of May 7, 1981, is the second-instance court. It hears appeals against decisions issued by military tribunals

[2976] The Military Court of Appeals also has the powers that Article 45 of the Military Judicial System (Royal Decree 9 September 1941, no. 1022) attributed to the Supreme Military Tribunal in special composition (military rehabilitation; reinstatement in rank, etc

[2977] The judging panel of the Military Court of Appeal is made up of the president of the Court itself or, in case of impediment, by a military magistrate of Cassation or Appeal, with the function of president

[2978] by two military magistrates of appeal, with judge-like functions

[2979] by two soldiers of one of the Armed Forces

[2980] or of the Guardia di Finanza, of equal rank to that of the accused and, in any case, not lower than lieutenant colonel, drawn by lot, with the role of judge

[2981] Then there is the Military Surveillance Tribunal - established by Legislative Decree 27.10.1986, n. 700, converted with Law 23.12.1986, n. 897, following the reorganisation of the supervisory bodies of the ordinary jurisdiction - competent to supervise the execution of sentences

[2982] The aforementioned tribunal is composed of all military supervisory magistrates and experts appointed by the CMM, within the categories indicated in Article 80, paragraph IV, of Law No. 354 of July 26, 1975 (professionals expert in psychology, social work, pedagogy, and psychiatry), as well as professors of forensic sciences

[2983] TABLE ITALY 8.4 Judicial activity

[2984] Statistics During the year 2000 - as emerges from the results of a fact-finding investigation promoted by the Council of the Military Judiciary - the first-instance military judicial offices issued 4,010 trial sentences (of which 870 were plea bargains), to which must be added 1,500 sentences issued by the preliminary hearing judges - these figures are practically constant compared to those of recent years

[2985] In the same reference year, however, the first-instance prosecution offices prosecuted approximately 4,300 cases, compared to nearly 9,000 in 1997 (a 50% decrease

[2986] Data relating to the military judicial offices of appeal, the surveillance offices, and the Military Attorney General's Office at the Supreme Court of Cassation show that judicial activity is numerically limited and, in any case, tending to decrease

[2987] This picture should not, however, lead us to believe - as the Council itself argued in a recent resolution - that the workload and needs of military judicial offices will necessarily decline with the reduction in conscripted personnel

[2988] Indeed, while it is true that statistically there has been a decrease in typical crimes committed by conscripts, known as "absence" crimes (failure to appear on the call-up list, desertion, etc.), it is equally true that so-called "character" crimes have increased, especially certain types of crimes such as property crimes against the public administration. This means that while the workload may appear to have decreased numerically, in reality, these types of "character" crimes, due to the difficulties of investigations and trials, require much greater workload than previously

[2989] Furthermore, it is necessary to take into account the workload resulting from the new Code of Criminal Procedure, which introduced the so-called "accusatory" procedure in which evidence is formed through cross-examination of the parties, as well as the new establishment of the Offices of the Judge for Preliminary Investigations (GIP) and the Judge for Preliminary Hearing (GUP

[2990] In this context, the current situation regarding the coverage of military magistrates appears to be quite satisfactory, also taking into account the fact that few retirements are expected in the immediate future

[2991] In fact, out of a staff of 103 military magistrates, there are currently 83 registered presences, to which must be added another 13 recently appointed units who are completing their period of induction, upon completion of which they will be placed in their respective roles

[2992] Publications of the Peace Studies Centre. To fill the remaining 7 positions, the competition based on qualifications is currently underway (reserved for ordinary magistrates

[2993] The Council of the Military Judiciary, however, highlighted, for the medium term, the difficulties associated with the particular procedures for commissioning military magistrates

[2994] Specifically, the competitive exam for admission to the military judiciary is divided into two phases, the first of which is reserved for ordinary magistrates, and the second for graduates

[2995] However, successful ordinary magistrates often reach their assigned positions only if they are satisfied and only if in the meantime they have been unable to satisfy their aspirations for a transfer within the judicial system of origin

[2996] This inevitably results in delays and negative impacts on office coverage. [3012] The above-mentioned problem (also extended to the unsustainable over-allocation of cars to serve the Military Judicial Offices

[3013] compared to the 37 foreseen by the DI 06.11.1990), is being examined by a special Working Group, set up by order of the Minister's Office at the Defence General Staff (SMD) and including representatives, in addition to SMD (which chairs) and the Minister's Office, also of the Armed Forces General Staffs, of the CC General Commands

[3015] Establishment of Military Judicial Police Sections The establishment of Military Judicial Police Sections at each Military Prosecutor's Office is a strongly felt need of the military judicial system

[3016] The Council of the Military Judiciary has repeatedly addressed this issue in its plenary deliberations, as has the Military Attorney General of the Republic at the Military Court of Appeal in his periodic report for the inauguration of the judicial year

[3017] On this point, it seems appropriate to establish a comprehensive set of rules that take into account the specific military situation and ensure the harmonization of the duties and responsibilities of the Corps Commanders with the proposed powers of the Sections, the establishment of which could be analyzed within the context of a broader reform of the military criminal justice system

[3018] At present, however, despite the absence of a specific legislative vehicle, the needs reported over the years by the various military prosecutors' offices have sometimes been met by assigning, on a purely operational level, the requested personnel belonging to the Carabinieri. [3043] dating back to 1941, like the peace treaty, it states that

[3044] Expeditionary forces abroad for military operations are subject to the military penal law of war, even in peacetime, from the moment in which they begin to cross the borders of the State and, in the case of overseas expeditions, from the moment in which the expeditionary force begins to embark

[3045] For the crews of military vessels or military aircraft, subjection to the military penal law of war begins from the moment in which they are notified of the destination of the shipment

[3046] The provision, establishing the application of the military criminal law of war to all Corps - land, naval and air crews - when they are sent abroad for military actions, allows both the exercise of criminal action against all those typical crimes codified in such law possibly committed by Italian soldiers, as well as the prosecution of specific crimes committed against the latter

[3087] Logistics - General Information "Logistics" has always represented the essential element for the life and activity of any complex organization and, even more so, for that of Defense

[3088] Its fundamental aim is to enable operational forces to conduct and complete the missions entrusted to them

[3089] As is well known, the strategic security framework in Europe and around the world has changed significantly in recent times

[3090] This change has led most countries, particularly those belonging to NATO, to redefine their role and tasks

[3091] In this regard, the Atlantic Alliance has developed a new strategic concept based on the concept of “Collective Defense and Security”

[3092] In line with this renewed approach, NATO has already begun a process of internal structural adaptation of its military organization to make it more responsive to new scenarios, to give due prominence, within the Alliance, to the European Security and Defence Identity (ESDI), and to acquire improved operational capabilities to respond to the new tasks and missions associated with crisis management and the risks of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction

[3093] In particular, with regard to “Logistics”, this process of structural adaptation includes: rapid, flexible and interoperable logistical support; adequate coordination with other organisations such as the EU and the United Nations; improved global logistical apparatus of the Alliance with a vision based on the principle of “collective responsibility”

[3094] It follows that, at the national level, structural choices and adjustments must be compatible and coherent with European and Atlantic ones within a framework of full integrability and interoperability with the Armed Forces of allied countries

[3095] It will therefore be necessary to substantiate the fundamental principles of military redevelopment, such as timeliness, deployment, integrability, interoperability and sustainability

[3096] All this inevitably presupposes a radical change in the logistics concepts that have dominated the sector until now, based on territoriality and a certain rigidity and cumbersomeness due to the traditional concept of materials storage with all its organizational and technical-administrative implications

[3097] In this context, it has become imperative to radically revise the organizational framework of logistics, with particular attention to Logistics Planning, which must be conducted with a unified joint vision, seeking every possible integration between the Armed Forces aimed at optimizing available resources

[3098] It is therefore necessary to seek the basis for a common approach on this matter which, while respecting the specific operational philosophy of each Armed Force, allows for efforts to converge towards the optimal achievement of objectives

[3099] On this basis, it is therefore important that the military instrument have "purpose-driven logistics," in other words, aimed at supporting the projection of forces outside the area. This logistics, through the synergistic use of information, materials, healthcare, and transportation, enables the mobility and supply of operational units in a timely, operationally optimal, and cost-effective manner

[3100] In particular, the Navy needs a support tool that can continuously maintain, at the usual levels of operational readiness, various force complexes (from single units to naval-air power projection groups, minesweeping, amphibious intervention, escort and protection, advanced covert surveillance, etc.) deployed anywhere in international waters at very short notice, with extremely high technical and logistical autonomy and without the need for theater bases

[3101] In summary, the new political-military framework in which the aforementioned functional and structural changes in Defence are taking place postulate: • increased mobility of forces not only in the tactical field, but also and above all at a strategic level and with a multimodal typology; • balanced and mobile sustainability of forces in all its components; Publications Centre for Peace Studies www.studiperlapace.it ____________ It should be noted that these initiatives concern and will concern various aspects of the technical and political activity of Defence such as

[3102] the definition of needs", "the setting of programs", "the acquisition process", "industrial cooperation" and "the participation of other countries", in short a medium/long-term "General Planning" that will require the involvement of the entire military apparatus

[3103] The results of this policy, given the resources available, will be achievable only by eliminating waste, overlapping areas and redundancies, rationalising and optimising the resources available at the Armed Forces level. • a different policy in the management of stocks that avoids the immobilisation of materials and capital, especially for those with advanced technology, pursuing uniformity of direction among the Armed Forces, starting with materials for common use; • military healthcare, to which particular emphasis must be given, through the inter-force sharing of healthcare resources; • a more advanced standardisation policy in order to improve cooperation and the cost/effectiveness ratio in the provision of logistical support to the forces, particularly in the multinational context; • review of responsibilities and competences in the field of Host Nation Support (HNS), in order to harmonise the national situation with NATO/EU regulations

[3104] • policy aimed at a fair and more effective interaction between the Armed Forces and the civilian context; • creation of a common logistics management IT platform (also including the healthcare segment) that will allow the exchange of information and coordination between national bodies and between these and/or NATO/International bodies, through the timely and precise sharing of logistics information

[3105] Current situation and future prospects The second half of the 1990s saw a more accentuated projection of the military instrument for foreign policy issues, with the assumption of increasing responsibilities in the Mediterranean area and also in extra-Mediterranean areas or those geostrategically linked to them, and with a primary political-military role in the crisis in the Balkan area

[3106] As a result, an active, efficient and long-term military participation, which caused a strong wear and tear of the materials

[3107] In this regard, the most significant comparison can only be translated into terms of a comparison between the operational capabilities provided in relation to the resources – always limited – invested and that are invested to achieve them

[3108] In practice, the succession of operations conducted by a limited part of the military instrument has not been compensated by the allocation of funds necessary for the maintenance and modernization of the materials of the entire instrument

[3109] That is, the Italian Armed Forces ultimately lack the depth to sustain even a limited effort or efforts over time in different theaters unless there is a significant increase in the budget dedicated to materials

[3110] In essence, mobility, external projection capacity and logistical sustainability – in concrete terms, the “modernization of our Armed Forces” – are still limited

[3111] The gap between us and other European countries is, more than a technological gap of quality in the strict sense, a gap of depth, that is, of the size, intensity, and sustainability over time of the operational interventions we can carry out

[3112] This gap is essentially attributable to the aforementioned undercapitalization of our military, that is, to an incorrect and unsustainable size/resources ratio

[3122] Procurement Policy Geopolitical evolution is accentuating the concept of the centrality of security and has exalted its globality in international terms

[3123] In this context, procurement policy must operate in accordance with safety-related needs, adapting to the priorities indicated by the Ministerial Directive

[3124] Indeed, the Ministry of Defense, abandoning the old policy that encouraged the purchase of domestically produced materials, resorting to foreign procurement only when absolutely necessary and economically viable, has long since focused its efforts on constant international market research

[3125] With regard to the procurement of materials relating to "Logistics", i.e. materials/services relating to the technical-logistical support of operational units, the Ministry of Defence intends to pursue a procurement policy based on the following criteria: • increased use of outsourcing on a convenience-necessity basis; • transfer of all maintenance activities - including procurement - to the Technical-Operational Area, in compliance with the principle that, since these are logistical activities dedicated to supporting operational units, these must necessarily be the responsibility of the Armed Forces; • transition from "just in case" consumption logistics, i.e. based on the analysis of "potential" needs, with consequent costly and unusable accumulations of materials to deal with every type of hypothesized emergency, to "just in time" consumption logistics, i.e. based on the principle of careful preventive planning and programming, based on the determination of actual needs, which provides what is needed when needed, while minimizing the storage of stocks

[3126] Modernization programs in the field of materials The lines of action along which the Ministry of Defence is moving to modernize the materials of our Armed Forces can be summarized as follows: • significant strengthening of C3I capabilities which will have to be more effective, available in real time and with a broader geographical coverage, both at a strategic and tactical level; • greater mobility to be achieved through an increased air and sea transport capacity of men and equipment, strengthening dedicated air and sea military transport, resorting, if necessary, also to the commercial sector; • greater tactical mobility on the ground and increased precision firepower; • multidimensional protection of forces

[3127] This presupposes both an increased air defense capability and more flexible and timely tactical air support as a means of deterrence, pressure, support and protection of forces deployed in theaters beyond the border

[3128] Modernization program in the Command, Control, Communications and Information (C3I) sector The characteristics to which these systems must respond can be summarized as follows: • interoperability, i.e. the ability to exchange services at joint and multinational (Combined) level; • flexibility, i.e. the ability to rapidly reconfigure in relation to the evolution of the operational situation, including the transportability aspect. • In this framework, the Ministry of Defence is in the process of developing a set of systems capable of responding to joint strategic needs, characterized by full integrability with specific FA systems. These are: • The SICRAL satellite communications system, • The Joint Digital Network (RNI), • The Defence Command and Control system (C4I Defence), • The Defence telematics network (DIFENET). All the aforementioned systems integrate, at different levels and within the limits of the specific operational needs for which they were designed, joint forces' needs

[3129] SICRAL and RNI are concerned with the transport of information

[3130] the first with a predominantly strategic connotation (out of area operations, mobile users), the second with a predominantly infrastructural connotation (connections between command centers located throughout the country

[3131] The two systems are perfectly integrated with each other, to the point that one can be considered an extension of the other, thus achieving interoperability at the joint level

[3132] Furthermore, the two systems can accept/provide services from/to similar systems of allied countries, thus responding to the principle of multinational interoperability

[3133] C4I Defence and DIFENET belong to the applications sector and, respectively, carry out the fusion of data coming from the Command and Control systems of the individual Armed Forces

[3134] in addition to operational web and email services), and the Defence sector INTRANET, in compliance, among other things, with specific legal provisions

[3135] Both systems obviously see SICRAL and RNI as the preferred transport systems

[3136] With the progressive entry into service of the above-mentioned systems, the Ministry of Defence will have an effective tool for exercising Command and Control in the various operational situations envisaged

[3137] However, just as in the civilian sector, communications requirements in the military sector are increasing exponentially over time, and on the applications front, new software simultaneously chases and stimulates hardware innovation

[3138] Recent international events, as well as the practical experiences gained over the last decade, demonstrate that military operations are increasingly moving towards typologies different from those of classic conflict

[3139] “Unconventional” conflicts, the fight against international terrorism, peacekeeping and peace-enforcing actions, civilian evacuations, disaster relief, etc. have assumed, and will likely assume, an increasingly important role in the future

[3140] Added to this is an ever-increasing sensitivity among Western public opinion towards the costs associated with military operations

[3141] The two facts outlined above have a considerable impact on C3I systems: • on the one hand, the commander in the field needs an increasingly advanced and up-to-date awareness of the operational situation, in order to be able to promptly plan targeted, low-risk and "surgical" actions; • on the other, a widespread diffusion of Command and Control tools is necessary, since the action carried out by even the most basic tactical grouping (naval unit, patrol, aircraft) is susceptible to provoking reactions and consequences that, going beyond the simple tactical context in which they developed, can take on strategic and political significance

[3142] The Commander of the near future will therefore need increasingly sophisticated automated Command and Control systems and, above all, increasingly widespread among the forces under his control

[3143] To manage tomorrow's operations, there will be an increasingly greater need to exchange information (operational, intelligence, logistical, medical, media, personnel well-being, etc.) with command centers that will very often be located in remote areas from the operations area

[3144] The second requirement that future communications systems will have to meet will be to provide operational users with a large amount of information in close to real-time and with a human/machine interface that is as user-friendly as possible

[3145] The use of INTERNET technologies, combined with broadband transmission systems, can be a response to this requirement

[3146] Furthermore, the ever-increasing amount of information to be transmitted, together with the need for global coverage, suggests the opportunity to complement typically military systems with dual and/or commercial systems, capable of ensuring the satisfaction of non-strictly operational needs or of covering particular geographical areas outside the footprint of military satellites

[3147] The Ministry of Defense is already moving along these lines and, in programmatic terms, financial resources have already been allocated to begin preparatory studies for the modernization of transport systems (SICRAL and RNI

[3149] The main features of these systems are briefly described below

[3150] SICRAL System It is a satellite communications system intended to provide transmission support for joint operations and exercises

[3151] It is based on: a satellite segment in geostationary orbit, operating in three frequency bands; a military Management and Control Centre located near Rome, responsible for both satellite control and the configuration and implementation of the communications networks that can be implemented; an initial allocation of 107 user terminals of various types (fixed, transportable, naval, avionics, vehicular, “manpack”

[3152] The system enables the creation of high-capacity traffic flows capable of covering military needs throughout the satellite's visibility area, which extends from the eastern coast of the American continent to beyond India

[3153] SICRAL was built almost entirely using Italian technology by a consortium of companies (Alenia Spazio, Telespazio and FiatAvio), supported by Marconi Mobile for the construction of the user terminals

[3154] The satellite was launched on 7 February 2001 from the Kourou testing range (European Ariane consortium) and the first operational connections were established in April

[3155] The satellite's operational life is estimated at 10 years

[3156] The overall cost of the undertaking was approximately 465 million euros (€900 billion

[3157] The SICRAL project, the first of its kind in Italy, represents a milestone in the military communications sector

[3158] It is indeed evident that since 7 February 2001 the availability of satellite communications has become an essential requirement for Defence, a prerequisite for the correct exercise of Command and Control of national forces

[3159] This means that study activities aimed at ensuring the continuity of the service even after 2011 have already begun

[3160] Obviously, operational experience in the field, emerging communications needs, and foreseeable technological developments over the next decade will constitute a fundamental element of these studies. Inter-force digital network This is a radio link communications system intended to meet the infrastructure needs of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Carabinieri throughout the country

[3161] It consists of: • a central network control centre which allows the efficiency of the entire network to be monitored and its reconfigurability in the event of failures

[3162] • a series of nodal centres located throughout the country

[3163] • an interconnection (gateway) to the SICRAL system, which ensures the flow of communications to/from the satellite

[3164] The inter-force digital network was created by the Marte consortium (MARCONI-TELETTRA), exploiting and expanding the infrastructure of a previous analogue network

[3165] It allows a bidirectional flow of 34 Mbps

[3166] Work is currently underway to provide the Interforce Digital Network with greater flexibility of use through the creation of alternative routes (meshing) and integration with fibre optic lines

[3167] The project is expected to be completed by 2004, with an overall cost of approximately 155 million euros (300 billion

[3174] The Defence Telematics Network (DIFENET) The need for a telematics network that would allow the connection between the computers and networks of the Defence Administration regardless of their geographical location and the operating system of the various IT systems was already deeply felt by the Armed Forces

[3175] This became urgent when the issue of connecting the Defence Administration to the Single Public Administration Network (RUPA) had to be addressed in compliance with the relevant legal provisions

[3176] RUPA is the most important cross-sector project pursued by AIPA for the creation of a telematics network in which all Public Administrations are integrated with each other through the services offered (email, file transfer, access to news, virtual terminal and INTERNET

[3177] This network requires that each Administration must “access” it with its own “domain,” understood as the set of hardware (computers, networks, etc.) and software (applications and data) resources belonging to the same organization

[3178] In summary, DIFENET performs the following functions

[3179] • represents the reference basis for the implementation of the interoperability of telematic networks in the AD field and for establishing the Defence INTRANET; • is intended to support the traffic of unclassified administrative data, initially excluding the possibility of processing classified data or data connected to the conduct of operations

[3180] However, it is designed to form the backbone for future developments towards a national geographic network to be used also for operational uses and classified information

[3181] • it is structured, from the point of view of network architecture, in such a way that each network user entity retains responsibility for the design, implementation and management of its own information systems, while adhering, however, to the technical rules indicated in the DIFENET document; • through a “DIFENET Management Centre” (CGD), the management, administration and configuration control of the network is ensured, as well as making interoperability services possible between the various network user entities

[3182] DIFENET, in the configuration outlined above, will be operational by 2003 with a spending commitment of approximately 3 million Euro (6 millions

[3183] Modernization programs in the land equipment sector In the field of modernization of weapons systems, for several years now the Army has oriented its strategic choices towards the objective of international cooperation

[3185] • maintaining maximum interoperability with the systems of allied armies

[3310] International Cooperation Policy in the Field of Material Transfer. As mentioned above, another aspect that increasingly characterizes the Italian Armed Forces is that of multinationality

[3311] This is an increasingly evident peculiarity of the international scenario, where on the one hand the generalized decrease in defense resources and on the other the growing spirit of cooperation even between formerly adversarial countries is leading them to pool their forces

[3312] As is known, the Italian Armed Forces are undergoing a significant downsizing, moving from a mixed force of 250,000 units to a professional model of 190,000 units by December

[3313] This downsizing, combined with a more elaborate political push for technological renewal initiated by the Ministry of Defense, has made available a large quantity of resources and materials that were in excess of what was needed

[3314] In line with this renewed approach, the availability of materials and resources (although largely technologically outdated) and their transfer have constituted and constitute a valid and concrete instrument of foreign policy, particularly towards those member countries of the Partnership for Peace (PfP

[3315] In this context, an intense activity has developed, supported by the tendency to establish “Agreements” regarding cooperation with various Nations, providing the excess material free of charge, as shown in the following table

[3316] Operational Policy Any choice made on the technological and operational levels of the use of forces has a direct and immediate impact on the operational sector, understood as the activities necessary to maintain, guarantee, ascertain and restore the efficiency, suitability for use of materials and the right level of reliability, effectiveness and safety based on the original operational requirement

[3317] As is known, this activity requires increasing costs as they are linked to the technology of the systems themselves, which are increasingly sophisticated

[3318] This requires pursuing a policy oriented, already in the research phase, towards systems suitable for containing operational needs, within acceptable limits and in any case pre-established in the phase of defining the military technical-operational requirements

[3319] in other words, it is necessary to consider the "Life Cycle Cost" (LCC) of each system from the early stages of the study, by carrying out accurate cost analyses (LCA

[3320] In this framework, there are many initiatives that can be adopted, each of which requires dedicated in-depth analysis, such as: directing the planned interventions towards the civil industry

[3322] Regardless of the working hypotheses illustrated above, the organizational structures that currently characterize the sector are reported below

[3323] Land Segment The Army, in relation to the operational environment in which it operates, has configured logistics into two Areas

[3324] responsible for the logistical support of combat units in operations

[3325] Its Command, Management and Executive bodies are all capable of operating without fixed infrastructure and can be deployed outside the national territory

[3326] Furthermore, they are able to operate in non-permissive, high-conflict environments

[3327] SUPPORT AREA

[3328] responsible for providing direct support to all FA units/entities when in garrison

[3329] Ensures the procurement and availability of materials required by the Membership Area for operations

[3330] Ensures the continuous availability of resources through the management of FA stocks

[3331] Its Command, Management and Executive bodies are not projectable and can only operate in fixed installations

[3332] Since the mid-1980s, the FA has moved from a logistics organization "by subject matter" to one "by function

[3333] In summary, before 1980, operators in the sector operated and were divided according to the type of material they worked with (small arms, artillery, engineering, police, etc.). Following the restructuring, the organizational architecture was based on the function the operators performed, regardless of the type of material

[3334] Today we find specialized personnel and entire operational units that deal with supplies, others that are dedicated to maintenance and still others responsible for transport, etc

[3335] Two of the main logistics functions, “Supplies” and “Maintenance”, are illustrated below

[3336] The analysis will be divided according to the operating environment in which they operate

[3337] in garrison and in operations

[3338] Supplies to Garrisoned Units The supply of garrisoned Units is ensured by the Support Area

[3339] Through careful planning of user needs, it delivers the requested materials to the permanent headquarters, either cyclically or on an ad hoc basis

[3340] To carry out this task, the Support Area uses warehouses/depots located throughout the country, employing a transport system dedicated to this task

[3341] Supplies to units in operations In operations the units are supplied by a department called the Adherence Support Group (GSA

[3342] This department, with variable composition, is calibrated for the specific mission

[3343] In low-conflict operations, it is possible to outsource some services in order to recover specialized logistics structures

[3344] Accumulations of supplies to combat units must be avoided, so as not to limit their mobility

[3345] Maintenance activities of the Units in garrison, maintenance activities vary depending on the family to which the material belongs (commercial vehicles, tactical vehicles, combat vehicles, weapon systems, etc.) and depending on the capabilities required for repairs

[3346] it can be carried out at the user of the material, at specialized FA workshops, at specialized civil companies and finally at the companies manufacturing the material

[3347] Users are usually responsible for scheduled maintenance and checks

[3348] Furthermore, depending on the resources available (specialized personnel, spare parts and equipment), they can also carry out repairs of a certain complexity

[3349] Newly introduced materials usually come with a warranty service for the first few years of their life

[3350] Maintenance activities of Units in operations In operations, Units must preserve their mobility, especially in high intensity operations and in non-permissive environments

[3351] Therefore, the types of interventions that users can carry out, unlike what happens at headquarters, tend towards a lower level, transferring the most expensive interventions to the GSA. Naval Segment In the Navy, the tasks relating to logistics functions are institutionally divided between the Inspectorate of the MM Commissariat and Administrative Coordination (MARISPECOMMI) for the sectors of food, clothing, barracks, fuels/lubricants and vehicles and the Inspectorate for Naval Logistics Support and Lighthouses (NAVISPELOG) for the sectors of vessel maintenance, management of spare parts/materials, ammunition and lighthouses and maritime signals

[3352] MARISPECOMMI is also responsible for the procurement of goods and services in the catering, cleaning, and labor sectors

[3353] Functions performed by the Navy Commissioner's Inspectorate (MARISPECOMMI) The Navy Commissioner's Inspectorate carries out administrative coordination activities with respect to all MM bodies and also involves the FA Administration Directorates

[3354] By virtue of its new regulations, the Inspectorate has acquired the right to coordinate, within the FA, the provisions issued by Segredifesa on administrative matters

[3355] The Inspectorate provides consulting and interpretation services on administrative and logistical matters to the central and peripheral bodies of the Ministry of the Interior. Pursuant to Presidential Decree 451/90, it also carries out technical oversight of the functionally dependent Ministry of the Interior Commissioners' Offices and, most recently, of the service canteens, pursuant to Article 2 of the Ministerial Decree of August 1st. Finally, it conducts research into improvements and innovations in commissioner station equipment, conducting experiments and submitting proposals to the relevant Technical Directorates-General, and maintaining and updating the relevant technical regulations

[3356] Food The procurement of food supplies required by the FA is carried out in a centralized or decentralized manner, for an annual budget of approximately 60 billion for a force of approximately 40,000 units

[3357] The resulting logistics activities are carried out locally by the Directorates and Sections of the Military Maritime Commissariat (Maricommi), which evaluate requests and initiate the procurement procedures necessary to restore the logistics cycle and, at the central level, with centralized or decentralized purchasing planning by the competent DG or the MM Commissariat Inspectorate

[3358] As part of the sector's new policy, the regulatory instrument for increasing the value of rations and for the transition to cash rations is being defined

[3359] The competent DG is studying the outsourcing of the service through procurement from large-scale retailers, with the maintenance of naval "transit warehouses" for the MM at the La Spezia, Taranto and Augusta offices

[3360] Clothing The procurement of clothing for MM needs is implemented in a centralized or decentralized manner, for a total annual budget of approximately 45 billion

[3361] Of these, 12 billion are earmarked to finance the tailoring contract for various types of ordinary and special clothing, based on the strength programs indicated by the SM

[3362] Logistics activities are carried out locally by Maricommi, which examines requests, initiates procurement procedures, and updates inventory levels in real time. At the central level, purchasing plans are developed by the Inspectorate in consultation with the SM and subsequently delegated to the relevant DG or to Maricommi

[3363] The new policy indicated by the DG envisages the suppression of military tailoring shops in order to achieve a single clothing contract for the Armed Forces in the medium/long term

[3364] A contract is expected to be finalized that will gradually transition from "packaging with fabrics and accessories paid for by the CEO" to "supply of clothing with fabrics and accessories paid for by the company." This contract should be finalized and fully implemented by the beginning of

[3365] The "personalized dressing" project is still in its infancy, and a study on it has been initiated by the DG itself

[3366] The acquisition of barracks materials is implemented on the basis of the FA's actual needs, keeping stocks to a minimum in order to avoid unnecessary redundancies in warehouses

[3367] Central purchases are made on the basis of the centralized plan prepared for the DG on the basis of the needs reported by the peripheral High Commands (of the territorial organization of the MM) and of the information provided by the Maricommi (warehouse situations and average annual consumption

[3368] Spare parts and decentralized purchases are donated to the Maricommi responsible for the territory

[3436] Bureaucratic procedures

[3437] These include both spare parts for the aircraft and all the ground equipment necessary for their support and maintenance

[3438] The management of the materials mentioned is carried out following the classic logistical functions of acquisition, conservation, distribution and disposal

[3439] Throughout the aircraft's operational life, there is also a need to organize the repair of materials rendered inefficient due to unforeseen failures or the scheduled overhaul of complex devices

[3440] Such interventions can be carried out at Armed Forces entities or at external industry

[3441] Such activities are fully subject to the State Accounting laws

[3442] Current regulations are particularly strict regarding the management of state-owned materials

[3443] At any moment it must be possible to know the state and physical position of each material

[3444] Furthermore, a complete and detailed accounting report of the material in the possession of the various entities of the Armed Forces must be provided annually

[3445] The regulations date back to historical periods that did not foresee the dynamic management required to maintain the efficiency of complex weapons systems made up of thousands of parts

[3446] It should also be noted that the regulations, in order to enforce strict compliance, identify specific legal entities that have personal responsibility for the condition of the materials

[3447] To meet both operational needs and strict compliance with regulations, the Armed Forces has established a widespread organization consisting of depots and warehouses, whose managers coincide with the legal entities required by the aforementioned accounting laws

[3448] The reality described above, in its concrete daily unfolding, leads to an inevitable contradiction between the urgencies dictated by flight activity and the slavish paperbased bureaucracy required for each individual movement of parts

[3449] In fact, the transfer of materials from the operational department to the base warehouses, from there to the depots, and every further step must be carefully documented and approved

[3450] Particularly complex is the so called transfer of ownership (i.e., the physical/accounting possession of the material) between the Armed Forces and the potential repair industry, as well as the internal transfer of the repaired material subjected to acceptance and compliance procedures required by the repair contract, always based on paper documentation

[3451] Experience shows that this system presents clear signs of inadequacy and inefficiency, often compensated for by the goodwill and quality of the staff involved

[3452] Furthermore, this reality also effectively prevents tax relief formulas for the Administration in managing efficiency

[3453] Without delving further into the details of the issue, it's enough to mention the recent experience with the C130J aircraft. For this aircraft, the Italian Air Force requested five years of turnkey logistics support from the manufacturing industry

[3454] That is, the company would have had to contractually ensure the efficiency of the machines without involving the Armed Forces except for pre-flight operations

[3455] In reality, the necessary application of the laws forces the administration to carry out the procedures for receiving materials and sending the faulty parts for repair according to the usual procedures, which cannot be overcome by contractual provisions

[3456] That is, the spare parts must be taken care of by the Administration and only subsequently passed on to the company that carries out the work on the aircraft

[3457] This causes delays of several days, nullifying the spirit of the contract, which intended to give the company full responsibility for the aircraft's recovery time

[3458] The shipping and repair process, which requires extremely complex procedures to ensure the traceability of individual parts as required by regulations, is even worse

[3459] In fact, the concept of exchanging materials, whereby a device sent for repair remains the property of the Armed Forces, which must receive the same part back, is not accepted by the regulations

[3460] In conclusion, all regulations regarding line efficiency materials should be reformed to allow for movement based on actual operational needs and protecting the Administration's interests based on the level of efficiency achieved

[3461] Materials management should certainly ignore the traceability of individual devices, allowing for the replacement of faulty equipment with an efficient one without presuming any alteration to the state's assets

[3462] That is, it is absolutely necessary to develop regulations based on the result that must be achieved (high efficiency of aircraft) rather than on the detailed control of the parts

[3463] It should be noted that the current situation, in addition to constituting an unacceptable waste of the Administration's human resources, also prevents the application of advanced outsourcing concepts to these activities

[3465] Logistics support is developed through a constant balancing of needs and possibilities in order to operate in terms of efficiency, effectiveness, adherence and cost-effectiveness

[3466] This line of action is pursued by the General Command of the Force through

[3467] • a cyclical planning and programming activity

[3468] • the optimization of available resources

[3469] • the simplification and rationalization of procedures and inventory management

[3470] • constant study and research activity

[3471] • achieving maximum adherence of support to the needs of the Departments by increasing, where possible, home services and outsourcing some executive activities, with the aim of freeing up personnel for more specifically operational activities

[3472] In short, the Carabinieri, like other military organizations, has moved from "just in case" logistics—based on the analysis of potential needs, resulting in costly and unused accumulations of materials to deal with any type of emergency—to "just in time" logistics, which, based on careful planning and preventive programming, founded on the determination of actual needs, provides what is needed when it is needed, minimizing stockpiles

[3514] Spare Parts The almost complete "outsourcing" of the maintenance of the Armed Forces' commercial vehicle fleet has allowed us to almost eliminate spare parts stocks for this type of vehicle - with the exception of consumables (batteries, covers, windshield wipers, etc.) - for which the minimum level of autonomy has been maintained, by virtue of their ready availability on the market

[3515] However, spare parts are maintained for combat, tactical and tactical-logistic vehicles that are not of commercial origin, taking into account the time required by the industry for their production

[3516] Even though the need for these resources has decreased compared to the past, a quantitative and qualitative shortage must still be lamented

[3517] On the other hand, the Army is faced with an "abundance" of spare parts for older-generation combat vehicles, a consequence of the reduction in the number of vehicles and their gradual replacement with new-generation systems

[3518] This situation is, however, finding a partial solution through the sale, to countries with which cooperation agreements are in place, of quotas of the aforementioned old-generation weapons systems, complete with an initial supply of spare parts

[3519] With regard to the definition of ammunition stocks, a complete review of the calculation criteria is underway within NATO

[3520] In particular, for war ammunition, and more specifically for those with a caliber greater than 20 mm

[3521] defined as “battle-decisive ammunition”), the calculation to quantify the stocks is no longer linked to the well-known parameters “fire day” or “combat life” and does not take into account any time factor

[3522] This ammunition, in fact, is calculated according to the "objective-oriented" methodology, which, using a mathematical model, allows the stockpiles to be calculated in terms of the number of shots required to destroy the targets envisaged in the different planning situations, of which the "most expensive" one is taken as a reference for the constitution of the stockpiles themselves

[3523] The results of this process, currently being refined, will need to be verified for their financial feasibility and adequate storage possibilities

[3524] The fact remains, however, that the current situation is deficient

[3525] As regards training ammunition, however, stocks are calculated taking into account that the quantities to be acquired must not exceed the maximum numerical values that can be consumed during the validity period of the ammunition itself or, in the case of long durations, the technical life of the weapon system that uses it

[3526] These calculations also take into account the “supplements” that come to training supplies from war ammunition approaching the end of its technical life, within the framework of correct rotation

[3527] In this regard, it should be noted that the release for consumption of war ammunition that would otherwise be out of use is undoubtedly one of the most sensitive issues for the purposes of economical management of stocks, also to avoid subsequent costly disposals

[3528] However, even in this sector, especially for some types of ammunition, the situation is deficient

[3573] And it is precisely with regard to the problems related to strategic transport that, given the extremely high cost of the aircraft, two options are being evaluated: direct acquisition or participation in the creation of a pool of aircraft within the Alliance for common use

[3574] Military air transport, although adequately sized, will still not be sufficient to meet all the needs of the Defense

[3575] Even in this field, it will therefore be necessary to provide for the use and participation of civil carriers, with the same legislative/regulatory issues mentioned when dealing with sea transport

[3593] General Aspects: The issue of infrastructure in the Armed Forces has always been of great importance, due to its direct impact on personnel management. This concerns both young men called up for military service, who expect to find barracks conditions not entirely dissimilar to those of civilian life, and career military personnel, subject to frequent changes of station, for whom the availability of service accommodation is a prerequisite for complete and easy mobility

[3594] These are therefore objectives that, in addition to being fundamental to the organizational efficiency of the military instrument, have a positive impact on the well-being and morale of personnel

[3595] Considering that the Armed Forces' infrastructures

[3596] used by the military are often the result of the legacy received from the Risorgimento and that only a minimal part of them date back to the post-war period, it must be admitted that they are not able to provide adequate services and decent environments

[3597] It also follows that their level is not entirely in line with the new and modern needs of the Armed Forces

[3598] as well as not being adequate for the constantly evolving regulations on plant safety and accident prevention at work

[3599] Over the last thirty years, despite the limited financial resources available, much has been achieved, but this still appears insufficient to upgrade and make the entire Armed Forces infrastructure fleet effective and efficient

[3600] In this context, in 1999 the Ministry of Defence continued its work of renovating and modernizing infrastructure, especially those intended to house volunteers, by adapting housing standards and developing a project for the construction of housing using the "Project Financing" system

[3601] To this end, the Ministry of Defense is making every effort to implement a program of progressive rationalization, through the decommissioning, or exchange, of all infrastructure no longer suited to the changing needs of the Armed Forces

[3602] Among the interventions that the Ministry of Defence has deemed to be a priority, those pertaining to the sphere of well-being and services are highlighted below: Publications of the Peace Studies Centre www.studiperlapace.it ____________ • Canteens and refectories

[3603] almost all barracks are now equipped with self-service facilities and suitable and welcoming rooms for eating meals; • Heating systems

[3604] We are continuing to modernize the obsolete and outdated diesel-powered plants, replacing them with modern, methane-powered plants to ensure cost-effective and efficient management

[3605] • Conference rooms

[3606] the existing structures have been adapted and organised to meet the changing needs of young men called to arms

[3607] Compliance

[3608] It cannot yet be said that the required safety standards have been achieved, even though the problem is particularly felt by peripheral commands and the Ministry of Defence is dedicating significant financial commitment to it

[3609] The following table summarizes the costs incurred by the Ministry of Defense in the aforementioned sectors. The program for the construction of housing with the "Project Financing" system. Currently, officers and non-commissioned officers are entitled to state-owned housing, a total of approximately 100,000 potential users

[3610] There are currently approximately 18,800 available accommodations

[3611] A comparison of the aforementioned data shows an "expectancy" value for housing equal to 1/5 (ratio of housing units/potential users

[3612] In essence, accommodation is available for one in five people (the aforementioned value becomes insignificant if we take into account that among the 18,000 accommodations there are some that are dilapidated, occupied by retired staff or located in areas where departments have been closed

[3613] Furthermore, by 2005, the Armed Forces will have a completely professional connotation and the Defence Model envisaged, based on current data, foresees the total availability of approximately 190,000 units, of which over half will be made up of volunteers (on extended service or in Permanent Active Service

[3614] Volunteer staff in SP, obviously, will have to have the same right to access state-owned housing that is now reserved for U.S. and S.U

[3615] Essentially, starting in 2005, the number of potential users of state-owned housing will increase significantly

[3616] The current financial perspectives of the Ministry of Defense do not allow for the launch of a program of acquisition, or construction, of housing, not even to maintain the aforementioned "expectations" of housing

[3617] Article 16 of Law 266 of 18 July 1999 (Regulatory Annex to the Budget Law) provides a regulatory instrument that allows for multiple intervention options that could not only eliminate one of the main obstacles to personnel transfers, but also meet the expectations of all staff

[3618] To this end, the Chiefs of Staff Committee examined the (Home System) Project (a program for the construction of housing using a Project Financing method), which envisages the following implementation path

[3619] the Ministry of Defense identifies the needs by specifying the number of housing units to be built in each location, making the land available

[3620] following a specific tender, the implementation of the programme is entrusted to a management body which, with its own funds, provides for the construction of the housing according to the housing standards indicated by the Ministry of Defence

[3621] Ownership of the properties remains with the managing body, which also assumes the cost of maintenance

[3622] • the managing body grants the use of the accommodation to military personnel, based on the indications of the AD, at an “acceptable” and convenient rent compared to the market

[3623] • the monthly fee can allow military personnel to “buy out” of the accommodation

[3624] • the AD takes on the burden of paying rent for accommodations that remain temporarily empty

[3625] The project, examined with the General Staff and the General Command of the Carabinieri, with the qualified collaboration of a consultancy firm (Advisor), concluded with a feasibility study of the Program and with the Draft of a Legislative Decree, as a regulatory vehicle for the problem

[3626] Furthermore, with a view to "testing" personnel satisfaction, a rapid sample survey was also developed, from which positive feedback has already been received from the Army and Navy, highlighting a willingness to join the Program that ranges from 70% to 90%

[3627] The aforementioned Draft Legislative Decree, on which there are still some reservations, is made up of seven articles: • Scope of application and purposes; • Characteristics of the Program; • Criteria for granting accommodation; • Management of the Program; • Obligations of the Manager; • Procedures for selecting the Manager; • Financing of the Program

[3628] Essentially, each user is allowed to choose between the pure rental or the option to buy formula, with the possibility of switching from one to the other at any time

[3629] In this sense, a financial option has been envisaged that would allow an individual to acquire ownership of the property within twenty years

[3630] It also provides that the Ministry of Defence contributes to the Program with the transfer of "Real Estate", as provided for by law

[3631] It has been assessed that the contribution to the Program of the aforementioned "Real Estate" contributes significantly to the reduction of costs which, together with the use of all possible opportunities to reduce tax burdens, can reach the level of 30%

[3632] The managing body is expected to be able to provide housing not only in "blocks" (i.e., entire buildings), but also in "small clusters" (i.e., within residential complexes for residential purposes), thus avoiding the feared "ghettoization

[3633] Some detailed organizational aspects are referred to Ministerial Regulations

Following the approval of Law No. 380 of 20 October 1999, which established the Women's Volunteer Service, the Defense General Staff developed the following ad hoc infrastructure policy in coordination with the Armed Forces

[3635] Considering that the legislative provision provided for recruitment scheduled according to the following implementation times

[3636] • firstly, the Officers (1st level); • secondly, the Non-Commissioned Officers (2nd level

[3637] • finally, for Volunteers (3rd level), the Ministry of Defense established that any infrastructural construction and/or adjustments should initially concern the training institutes for the cadres (Academies and Schools) and subsequently the training units and those employing the Volunteers. The foregoing, and the limited financial resources, led the Armed Forces to adopt an approach to the infrastructural problem based essentially on the use of existing facilities

[3638] Essentially, it was believed that the same infrastructure intended for male recruitment could be used, resorting to "physical separation" only for activities where it was essential to guarantee "privacy" (dormitories/bedrooms, toilets and changing rooms, appropriately equipped with suitable sanitary facilities and furnishings

[3639] Army infrastructure “Policy” The typological solution identified, therefore, is that of the 2-4 person living cell which also ensures the availability, within its own area, of “dedicated” toilet facilities

[3640] In this regard, it was deemed appropriate to outline the following criteria to be followed within the AF: • define minimum standards, excluding excessively costly "digressions"; • identify housing solutions proportionate to the influx of female personnel to training institutes, such as the Modena Military Academy (30 – 40 units) and the Marshal Student School (70 – 100 units), consequently evaluating the possibility of their timely implementation

[3641] • use existing infrastructure by assigning "female soldiers", where possible, separate barracks or, alternatively, reserved dormitory floors, creating, where necessary, "dedicated" accesses

[3642] The aforementioned criteria have the advantage of allowing for good integration of female personnel into the departments, since, except for limited "additional supplies" for toilets, the dormitories to be allocated to women should have the same characteristics as those already in use by men

[3643] In fact, it is believed that, from the very beginning of the female service, any form of "privilege" for "female soldiers" should be avoided, as this could constitute a cause for possible friction with the male component, with consequent negative effects on the esprit de corps of the units

[3644] Furthermore, there is the belief that these same women must have the certainty of being treated impartially, that is, as “soldiers”

[3645] This is to make them feel “integrated” in all aspects of military life

[3646] In this context, therefore, the possibility of reserving the top or first floor of a three-story building for women (a solution adopted by the US Army) could guarantee good functionality

[3647] This housing “separation” is also used by the Israelis who, if the infrastructure has sufficient reception capacity, prefer to allocate isolated barracks for women, located on the ground floor, identical to those used by men

[3714] NATO resources concern the set of: • “Manpower” necessary for the management of these programmes

[3715] Italy participates in the various programs with a share in terms of finances and personnel that places it fourth among the nations

[3716] In the 1990s, in order to optimize the allocation of shared military financial resources, member countries strengthened NATO's management structure by promoting the development of purpose-built structures and establishing a High-Level Resources Commission

[3717] the Senior Resource Board (SRB), responsible for the global management of NATO's military resources

[3718] Despite the breadth of the problem, the NATO Resources sector has so far been considered atypical, limiting knowledge of it to a few "insiders

[3719] On the contrary, resource issues require the adoption of national positions that often go beyond technical-military aspects to directly impact political decisions

[3720] And precisely because of the breadth of the subject matter—which involves various branches (military policy, operations, logistics, financial planning, infrastructure, telecommunications, and command and control systems)—staff action is difficult and laborious, requiring close coordination between numerous organizational elements of the AD, whose structure is not designed for unitary program management

[3721] Therefore, in order to optimize the use of resources, NATO conducted a profound restructuring of its organizations and modified its procedures in the 1990s, achieving close integration between the NSIP, the MC and “Manpower”

[3722] Furthermore, the importance of joint funding and cooperation in resource logistics was reaffirmed in the new strategic concept approved at the Washington summit in April

[3723] These difficulties, moreover, are reflected in the work carried out in the numerous Allied forums dealing with resources, where it is essential that the visibility of the decisions taken by Italy meet criteria of absolute consistency

[3724] Solid preparation is a prerequisite for competing with similar allied organizations that have a high level of specialization and considerable experience

[3725] However, individual professional skills must be supported by an efficient and harmonious structure where staff can operate at their best

[3726] At the national level, the entire sector is headed by the Defence General Staff, which plays a leading role in relation to the 14 Defence bodies involved in the programmes in question

[3727] As regards NATO programmes in Italy, the two main projects currently in an advanced stage are worth mentioning

[3728] AFSOUTH 2000 in Lago Patria and JOINT COMMAND SOUTH in Verona

[3729] AFSOUTH Command Publications Peace Studies Center www.studiperlapace.it AFSOUTH is currently located in Bagnoli, in properties rented by the Banco di Napoli Foundation

[3730] The project to relocate and build the new AFSOUTH headquarters was decided and planned by the Atlantic Alliance for an estimated cost of approximately 300 billion lire

[3731] The choice of the Lago Patria site (Giugliano - Naples) was made based on the operational requirements established by NATO and the availability of state-owned land, through a complex feasibility study

[3732] The Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between NATO and Italy has been signed, and the project is now being implemented

[3733] To carry out the tasks associated with this intervention, the Defence General Staff has established its own local office called PA-2000 which, included in the Joint Project Coordination Office, constitutes the natural interface between Italy and NATO

[3734] Italy, as the Host Nation, is responsible not only for the implementation of the project, within the timeframe established by the Atlantic Alliance, but also for numerous other tasks such as expropriations, urbanization works, etc. The new Project was presented, with fully satisfactory results, to the Local Authorities during two Service Conferences and to the President of the Campania Region

[3735] The construction, particularly complex as it is divided into two components, Civil Works and Telecommunications, includes a main building and other support buildings, such as the Motor Pool and Community Center

[3736] Additionally, the relocation of the HF antenna park from Lago Patria to Licola and the redevelopment of the Nisida infrastructure complex, which hosts NAVSOUTH, are planned

[3737] Joint Command South in Verona is currently divided into five locations

[3738] The relocation was started in 1994, with the idea of renovating the "Passalacqua" barracks in Verona

[3739] At the end of 1999, after obtaining NATO funding of approximately 60 billion lire, the Defence General Staff began a calm dialogue with the Mayor of Verona to identify alternative solutions, given that the nearby University had insistently requested that the barracks be included in its infrastructure assets

[3740] A Declaration of Intent has been signed with the Municipality, which provides for an exchange between Passalacqua and a 30-hectare site on the southern outskirts of the city, called "La Genovesa," which will also be able to house the Land Operations Forces Command

[3741] We will now have to proceed by convening a Services Conference and presenting the cost estimates to NATO

[3742] Infrastructural issues of the Carabinieri 10.6.1 Introduction The buildings, systems and structures constitute the logisticalinfrastructural complex necessary to satisfy the needs of the various organizational lines into which the Corps is divided, configuring themselves, due to the effects they have on the operations and efficiency of the Departments, as an essential component of the command organization

[3743] The sector's policy aims to find optimal conditions for maintaining, rationalizing, and enhancing structures to make them functional and responsive to actual needs, developing housing standards based on optimizing the cost/effectiveness ratio

[3744] The achievement of these strategies is conditioned by the diversified ownership regime of the approximately 5,000 barracks in use throughout the country, of which 143, equal to 2.9%, belong to the Military State Property, 865, equal to 17.4%, to the Civil State Property, and 3,986, equal to 79.8%, are privately owned and leased by the Ministry of the Interior

[3745] The properties belonging to the military state, although old and in need of functional and architectural adaptations, are now incorporated into urban expansion, proving particularly suitable for ensuring the necessary "proximity" to citizens

[3746] In recent decades, significant initiatives have increased the real estate holdings of the civil state, thanks to targeted legislative funding, which has made it possible to build modern facilities that meet the changing needs of the Commands, even though many now require necessary adjustments required by recent environmental, accident prevention, and safety regulations for facilities

[3747] State military barracks
