[3797] General information The competitions provided by the Armed Forces are subject to their priority institutional commitments

[3798] They consist of the use of personnel, resources and materials in tasks that are the same or similar to those normally carried out within the Military Organization

[3799] The role of the Armed Forces is to be considered complementary to that played by the Ministries and civilian organizations institutionally responsible for the various sectors of intervention

[3800] The type of commitments in the competitive tender sector is regulated by specific legislative provisions and directives of the Ministry of Defence and the Defence and Air Force, which define procedures, operating methods, dependencies and limits of the commitment

[3854] Safeguarding free institutions

[3855] In addition to its international commitments, since 1945 the Army has also been involved in various interventions at home, in conjunction with the Public Security Authorities, to safeguard public order and safety in certain areas of the country characterised by events that could have harmful consequences for the community

[3856] These commitments, which fall within the institutional activities envisaged by Law 382/1978 "Norms of Principle on Military Discipline" which, among the tasks established for the Army, Navy, and Air Force, also includes that of "contributing to the safeguarding of free institutions," have been implemented at a rapid pace since July 1992, constituting a demanding test for all units of the Armed Forces

[3857] Since that date, in fact, the national political authorities have decided to increasingly engage the Army, in conjunction with the Police Forces, to contribute to the protection of internal security, as a suitable tool to strengthen the State's presence in particularly critical areas of the nation

[3858] The interventions were primarily aimed at fighting organized crime, following the intensification of criminal activity in some regions, and at controlling illegal immigration at Italy's borders

[3859] This deployment involved the direct participation of military units in the preventive and repressive actions of the Police Forces and required the adoption of specific measures on both an institutional and organizational level

[3860] Article 13 of the Law of 1 April

[3861] the Prefect has at his disposal the Police Force and any other forces placed at his disposal under the laws in force and coordinates their activities

[3862] Among these, the Government's decision to grant the Armed Forces (FA) military personnel the title of "Public Security Officer" stands out for its exceptional nature, clearly differentiating the recent operations from all those conducted previously. This decision allows them to "proceed with the identification and immediate on-site searches of persons and means of transport, pursuant to Article 4 of Law 152/75, also for the purpose of preventing or impeding behavior that could endanger the safety of persons or the security of infrastructure or monitored locations, excluding judicial police duties

[3863] This legal status has given greater effectiveness to the actions of Army units, which have been able to operate fully autonomously with the typical methods of the Police Forces, maintaining their own Command and Control structures unchanged

[3864] Recently, two legislative provisions have further "regularized" this form of intervention: Law 331/2000, where art. 1, paragraph 5, states that "the Armed Forces contribute to the protection of free institutions and carry out specific tasks in circumstances of public disasters and in other cases of extraordinary necessity and urgency

[3865] • Law of 26 March 2001 no. 128 (so-called “security package”), which institutionalized the intervention of the Armed Forces

[3868] These programs, with a maximum duration of six months (renewable), are adopted after consulting the National Committee for Public Order and Security, in which the Chief of Staff of the relevant Armed Forces is called to participate, and define the maximum numerical commitment of military personnel that can be used in each province and the related employment directives

[3869] In this context, the military, in order to prevent or impede behavior that may endanger the safety of people or the security of the structures they monitor, can proceed with the identification and detention of people or vehicles on site for the time strictly necessary to allow the intervention of Police Force Agents (under no circumstances may the military act as Police Agents

[3870] Article 4 of Law No. 152/1975, "Provisions for the Protection of Public Order," provides that "in exceptional cases of necessity and urgency, which do not allow for a timely judicial action, officers and agents of the judicial police and the public force during police operations may proceed, in addition to identification, to an immediate on-site search, for the sole purpose of ascertaining the possible possession of weapons, explosives, and burglary tools, of persons whose behavior or presence, in relation to specific and concrete circumstances of place and time, does not appear justifiable

[3903] The Meteomont Service, created within the Alpine Troops in the winter of 1972/73, in collaboration with the Italian Air Force, to guarantee Alpine units a framework of maximum safety during mountain activities, especially in winter, has assumed increasingly greater importance at a national level

[3904] Today, Meteomont fits into the broader concept of prevention, safety, and rescue for all those who live in the mountain environment or frequent it for work and/or tourism

[3905] The Service is currently based on the following constituent bodies: • the Alpine Troops Command in Bolzano, with management, organizational, coordination and control functions; • 6 Meteomont Sector Centers (Turin with the sub-centers of L'Aquila, Aosta, Bolzano, Bressanone, Belluno and Udine) covering the entire Alpine arc and Abruzzo, responsible for organizing and implementing the service in their respective areas of competence

[3906] or a Meteorivometric Monitoring Network currently made up of 48 automatic and 57 manual stations

[3907] for the acquisition of daily and periodic observations and measurements

[3908] The network's territorial distribution was defined, in agreement with regional and provincial authorities, to ensure widespread coverage of the areas subject to snow monitoring and integration with civilian networks

[3909] or Extraordinary detection units, for the collection of meteorological information in areas not covered by the detection network

[3910] For the Data Collection Center at the Italian Air Force Meteorological Center in Milan-Linate, for the collection, compilation, and distribution of meteorological information, based on data provided by the Italian Air Force Meteorological Service

[3911] “Meteomont” pursues its objectives through the development of multiple activities, which are interrelated and integrated with each other

[3912] In particular: the forecasting activity, carried out through the issuing of a daily weather forecast and snow assessment bulletin

[3913] teaching, management and control activities in the field of safety and rescue in winter mountains and on ski slopes

[3914] training activities, such as: qualification course for meteorological observers for the benefit of the personnel of the Alpine Troops and the State Forestry Corps

[3915] Ski slope rescue course for Alpine Troops and State Forestry Corps personnel

[3916] • research, studies, and experiences relating to the environment and phenomena associated with snow and avalanches; • participation of managers in conferences and seminars, in Italy and abroad, of interest in the specific sector

[3917] • Production and updating of Military Avalanche Cartography and special cartography (elevation, slope, and aspect maps); • Collaboration and participation in the activities carried out by the bodies responsible for Civil Protection, the environment, and regional and provincial services

[3918] • meteorological support at home and abroad for units engaged in training/operational activities

[3919] With regard to this last aspect, the Alpine Troops Command has long established effective cooperation with numerous civilian bodies interested in the issues in question and among these the following have a position of particular interest

The validity of the safety and prevention system implemented by the Meteomont Service has been confirmed in recent years, particularly in the civilian world, with the launch of numerous collaborations with public and private bodies and various information bodies including RAI, RAI-CCISS and numerous periodicals (Airone, Rivista della Montagna, etc

[3931] The maintenance and development of the aforementioned collaborations, the scientific and technological progress in the field of meteorological and snow analysis and the progressive transition from a conscript army to a voluntary army, with consequent reduced availability and high cost of human resources, today require a substantial updating and strengthening of the systems for acquiring, transmitting, archiving and processing meteorological and snow data that constitute the "Meteomont system", according to new criteria, such as: • transition from the current data reception and transmission system, via radio/wire, to more efficient and economical systems (e.g. satellite and digital); • the replacement of the fixed manual detection network with new automatic stations, providing for a 50% strengthening of the current automatic network, equal to 24 stations, with the consequent substantial reduction in personnel employed of approximately 60%

[3932] Conclusions: Summary of the competitions provided by the Army. In relation to the ongoing evolution of the Armed Forces and the ongoing international missions, the criteria followed for granting competitions – while ensuring maximum availability within the limits of available personnel and material resources – will increasingly tend to favor the use of highly specialized units (engineers and helicopters) that are not normally available in the civilian sector. Navy. The functions performed by the Navy within the framework of the relationship between the Armed Forces and the country derive from the needs of public safety, environmental protection, protection of economic activities at sea, and public utility, with the use of the potential of military structures

[3933] Among these functions, those with a marked operational connotation concern general surveillance and control at sea, the control of illegal immigration flows (through devices in the waters of the lower Adriatic and the Strait of Otranto, the Northern Ionian Sea, and the Strait of Sicily), the surveillance of economic activities and the protection of freedom of fishing (through the surveillance and protection of national fishing vessels operating in the critical areas of the Strait of Sicily and the Adriatic Sea), search and rescue at sea (intervening with its own "life-saving units at sea," especially in complex operations on the high seas, also with the use of offshore patrol vessels equipped for maritime rescue services), the protection and control of underwater archaeological heritage (through the use of specialized means to support activities to safeguard the maritime environmental heritage and archaeological research), and the protection of the marine environment and the fight against marine pollution

[3934] As part of its general maritime policing activities, the Navy carries out control activities on merchant vessels, including visits and inspections of documentation and cargo

[3976] Politics and programs On the stimulus of these events

[3977] The Defence General Staff has initiated the development of a Defence environmental policy, a joint work programme and a dedicated management system which are structured around the following key points: • compliance with national laws and compliance with NATO standards; • pollution prevention; • nature conservation; • management of hazardous materials; • establishment of a Joint Working Group for environmental protection; • determination of the organisation. • environmental cleanup and recovery

[3978] However, developing such a program requires financial and personnel resources that are not immediately available

[3979] Furthermore, the Defence General Staff has planned a series of actions, with the intention of implementing them together with activities within NATO and within the Bilateral Cooperation with the United States of America: establishment of an Accident Prevention and Environment Office; development of an Environmental Policy of the Ministry of Defence; definition of a Joint Environmental Directive; personnel training and education

[3980] Establishment of the Accident Prevention and Environment Office The first step was the creation of a Regulatory and Environmental Section, which was initially established to address all environmental impact issues related to military infrastructure

[3981] As activities progressed, the Section became the coordination point for all aspects of environmental protection within the Defence sector

[3982] In confirmation of the importance attributed to environmental protection issues, the Defence General Staff felt the need to elevate the Environment Section to Office level by including the treatment of accident prevention matters, which are similar in some respects

[3983] The Office is now the point of reference for national and NATO environmental planning, for cooperation with other ministries and local authorities and with the US Department of Defense on environmental issues

[3984] The Joint Working Group However, the development of an environmental policy and programs for Defense requires the contribution of all the Armed Forces' Member States and the technical-administrative bodies, not only for reasons of joint standardization but also and above all to acquire and integrate the experiences gained in each Armed Force

[3985] It is for this reason that an Inter-Force Working Group was established, composed of representatives from the following sectors: technical-operational sectors of each Armed Force; technical-administrative sectors of the Ministry of Defence; technical-specialist sectors, when deemed necessary

[3986] In dealing with every aspect relating to environmental protection, the Group has established four working subgroups to deal with specific topics

[3987] The Subgroup for the protection from electromagnetic pollution to address the burning problem of non-ionizing radiation

[3988] Also in anticipation of the future approval of a framework law on the matter, the Subgroup has already produced a first draft of the "Inter-Force Regulation for Protection from Non-Ionizing Radiation", which will be further improved to include the provisions of the Legislative Decree

[3989] The Subgroup for Noise Protection is drafting an implementing regulation for the framework law on noise pollution (L. 447/95), relating to the noise produced by military aircraft

[3990] By virtue of the experience gained by the Air Force with the MILNOISE project and with the construction of a mobile noise detection vehicle (total project cost one billion), the Subgroup is providing assistance to local authorities for the purposes of noise mapping required by the aforementioned law

[3991] The Subgroup for the Development of Environmental Protection in Military Installations has produced, in cooperation with the USA, a questionnaire for the preliminary investigation of all the activities carried out in military bases for the purpose of identifying any contaminated sites and preventing pollution

[3992] This questionnaire is currently being distributed to all peripheral Defense agencies to assist in identifying contaminated sites, pursuant to Article 17 of Ministerial Decree on the Environment No

[3993] For the quality improvement activity, a pilot installation has been identified for each Armed Force where the collection of information on environmental problems and the experimentation of possible solutions can be started: • The Subgroup for information, education and environmental training of personnel which is developing, in cooperation with the USA, programs for raising awareness, specialization and cultural elevation in the field of environmental protection of military personnel at all levels

[3994] The Subgroup for Hazardous Materials recently established to address one of the most sensitive sectors of environmental protection

[3995] The “Guidelines” of the Ministry of Defence had their first definition with the approval of the relevant “Guidelines” by the Chiefs of Staff Committee on 9 December

[3996] These guidelines were subsequently developed into a more comprehensive document which is currently being approved by the Minister of Defence

[3997] The Joint Environmental Directive With this document, the Defence General Staff intends to provide a comprehensive framework of international, EU, national, behavioral, informational, and guideline standards to facilitate the conduct of military activities in compliance with national environmental protection laws and NATO standards

[3998] The Directive aims to

[3999] • provide a unified and inter-force framework for environmental protection

[4017] Contribution to NATO environmental protection With regard to NATO standardization, it is worth pointing out that Italian foreign policy provides for participation in multinational forces, including in out-of-area operations, which implies training and exercises in Italy and abroad

[4018] These activities cannot ignore the laws in force in the host countries

[4019] By 1998, the need to standardize doctrine for joint environmental protection during military operations was agreed upon by most NATO countries

[4020] Therefore, within the Joint Service Board (JSB) of the NATO Standardization Agency (NSA), a Working Group on Environmental Protection was established, the Environmental Protection Working Group (EPWG), which was tasked with developing STANAG 7141-EP, the basic environmental doctrine document, and any other more specific STANAGs. The EPWG, currently composed of representatives from twelve nations, has already met twice at NATO Headquarters in Brussels

[4021] the Presidency of the group was entrusted to Italy

[4022] The ratification draft will be submitted to member countries for final approval by the end of 2001, constituting the first real step towards a common military environmental policy

[4023] The Italian presidency was particularly appreciated for achieving the objectives set and was reconfirmed unanimously

[4024] Environmental protection has long since become a fundamental parameter in both the planning and conduct of military operations and is expressed in the most varied scenarios

[4025] from simple national exercises to complex multinational out-of-area operations

[4026] This standardization will facilitate NATO Commanders in planning and conducting military operations and training

[4027] The environmental issue is therefore vast and complex, with a large number of topics that will require the EPWG to undertake long and arduous work and to work closely with other national and NATO groups operating in different sectors

[4028] It is expected that the EPWG's activities will significantly develop in the future to enable the Alliance to keep pace with the increasingly precautionary environmental protection measures enacted by member countries

Aircraft noise containment The aforementioned MILNOISE project on aircraft noise, developed by the Pratica di Mare Experimental Flight Centre, is part of a broader strategy aimed at containing noise pollution caused by the Italian Air Force's training flight activities

[4064] Also in order to keep the noise produced by military aircraft during training activities within acceptable limits, the Italian Air Force has imposed limitations on very low-altitude flights (VLA) within the national territory

[4065] These limitations have, in effect, reduced the available areas and raised the minimum altitudes, severely hampering BBQ activity. [4091] The Operational Programme “Security for the Development of Southern Italy” 2000-2006, with a view to strengthening the technologies used by the Armed Forces

[4092] to the qualification, training and updating of personnel, to a full and effective involvement of civil society, sees the Force committed to the implementation, among others, of the "Environment" project (Measure I. 3.) for which it is responsible

[4093] The project's primary objective is to strengthen territorial control through the use of advanced technologies that enhance the prevention and fight against environmental threats

[4094] This is to enhance the organizational structure of the Carabinieri Environmental Protection Command, which, by establishing specialized regional sections, aims to deepen local knowledge of issues of interest and provide more timely and effective support for the prevention and repression activities carried out by the territorial force

[4095] The “Environment Project” concerns, first and foremost, the creation of a “Database” (the so-called “Flag Project”) managed by the Carabinieri Environmental Protection Command and also accessible to other Police Forces, the State Forestry Corps, the National and Regional Agencies for Environmental Protection, and finally, the Regions, with a view to fully coordinating environmental protection activities

[4096] The project will also allow for improved monitoring of risk areas thanks to

[4097] the acquisition of constantly updated information using advanced technology equipment designed to detect sources of pollution or sources of environmental risk, as well as to take images from land platforms and in the air

[4098] multimedia data processing, integrated with thematic cartography and geographic mapping (satellite and aerial), to the full advantage of the analysis and planning of targeted operational interventions

[4099] Special telephonic alert systems for environmental protection will also be activated at the Carabinieri stations in the territories included in the so-called “Objective 1”

[4100] The General Command of the Carabinieri also contributes to: • the NATO Committee for Challenges to Modern Society (NATO – CCMS) project on illegal activities related to radioactive materials by reporting, through the Carabinieri Environmental Protection Command, any information of interest that may emerge from the work of the “Environmental Crimes Project” within the G-8; • the “National Radioactive Fallout Detection Network”, established by Law No. 421/1996, to strengthen measures to prevent the dangers of pollution from radioactive substances, through a program of adaptation and replacement of the control and monitoring systems and equipment used by the National Fire Brigade, as some telemetry sites are located at the Corps' headquarters. [4113] Military journalism

[4114] Pursuant to Presidential Decree no. 556 of 25 October 1999, "Implementing Regulation of Article 10 of Law no. 25 of 18 February 1997, concerning the powers of military leaders," the Minister of Defense is responsible for issuing directives on communication, public information, and promotional activities for the Armed Forces

[4115] In turn, the Chief of Staff of Defence handles the public relations of the Defence General Staff and coordinates all delegated public relations, i.e. those within the specific remit of the Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces

[4116] It also issues directives regarding historical documentation and maintains relations with the information bodies, in coordination with the competent offices of the Ministry

[4117] Military journalism must: • reach outside its own sphere to stimulate the conscious participation of citizens in military activities in the country

[4118] • turn internal attention to the Executives with particular emphasis on the youngest through various cultural projects aimed at: o promoting interdisciplinary training paths

[4119] or stimulate and encourage intellectual growth and the comparison of ideas

[4120] o identify and develop pedagogical themes and the inspiring principles of ethics, life, and the State; o foster the process of osmosis of ideas and experiences between the Armed Forces and between the military and civilian worlds; o strengthen awareness that the Armed Forces are a great reservoir of technical, scientific, human, and cultural resources at the service of the Nation and act as a catalyst for intellectual synergies

[4121] Publicity in the joint force area The relationship with an informed public opinion minimizes the risk of misunderstanding in strategic choices regarding security and defense

[4122] From this perspective, the adoption of the Internet has satisfied the need to conform to modern communication systems in addition to the still valid “printed paper”

[4123] The use of your own “Official Website” – www.difesa.it – allows you to present to the outside world the image of the Defense in general, of the General Secretariat of Defense and of the individual Armed Forces - www.sgd.difesa.it; www.esercito.difesa.it; www.marina.difesa.it; www.aeronautica.difesa.it; www.carabinieri.it

[4124] as well as providing citizens with a rapid and effective interface with the military world

[4125] As regards joint-force publications, the following publications are published: “INFORMAZIONI DELLA DIFESA”, a periodical published by the Defence General Staff

[4126] GIORNALE DI MEDICINA MILITARE", a periodical published by the General Directorate of Military Health; - "BONUS MILES CHRISTI", a periodical published by the Military Ordinariate; - "BOLLETTINO SEGNALETICO DI DOCUMENTAZIONE", published by the Secretary General of Defense/National Director of Armaments. 12.1.4 Publicity in the Armed Forces Area The Armed Forces' communication and information activities are carried out not only through programs designed for nonadvertising institutional communication, but also through billboards, promotional distributions, the organization of events (sporting, cultural, etc.), participation in specialized exhibitions, fairs, and conferences, collaboration in the production of films for television and cinema, and the organization of conferences (including at schools

[4127] Within military journalism, a prominent place is occupied by the Historical Offices which, in addition to dealing with the acquisition and preservation of documentation relating to the life of the Armed Forces, also play an important role in the dissemination of military history, through editorial productions

[4128] Below is a list of periodical publications divided by Armed Force

[4129] Army • “MILITARY MAGAZINE”, periodical published by the Army Publications Center; • “BULLETIN OF THE ARCHIVES OF THE HISTORICAL OFFICE”, periodical published by the Historical Office of the Army General Staff

[4130] Navy • “RIVISTA MARITTIMA”, periodical published by the Navy General Staff

[4131] • “NOTIZIARIO DELLA MARINA”, periodical published by the Naval General Staff

[4132] ARCHIVE BULLETIN OF THE HISTORICAL OFFICE", periodical published by the Historical Office of the Navy

[4133] Aeronautics • “RIVISTA AERONAUTICA”, periodical published by the Air Force General Staff

[4134] • “FLIGHT SAFETY”, periodical published by the Flight Safety Inspectorate

[4135] “RIVISTA DI METEOROLOGIA AERONAUTICA”, periodical published by the General Office for Meteorology

[4136] Carabinieri • “IL CARABINIERE”, a periodical published by the Carabinieri Publishing House; • “RASSEGNA DELL'ARMA DEI CARABINIERI”, a periodical published by the Carabinieri Officers' School; • “SERVICE FOR STOLEN WORKS OF ART”, a bulletin published by the General Command of the Carabinieri; • “OPERATIVE ACTIVITIES OF THE CARABINIERI”, a publication published by the General Command of the Carabinieri

[4137] Introduction The transition from compulsory conscription to volunteering, and therefore to an Armed Forces made up of professionals, has required a significant increase in communication and propaganda activities in particular

[4138] Added to this is the increasingly massive strategic position that the media are acquiring within military operations

[4139] Communication, as is well known, is a strategic resource both with respect to the operations themselves and with respect to the consensus they must receive from public opinion

[4140] In the age of real-time television news and visual technologies connected to the information world, it is risky to launch any kind of military initiative without ensuring its media recognition, one that not only allows it to gain consensus but also allows it to manage events in real time

[4141] The Italian Armed Forces find themselves having to deal with a tradition of prejudicial distrust toward the military institution and the military function itself

[4142] But, at the same time, the new tasks, ranging from immigration control to peacekeeping missions, have brought about profound changes and given the military world a strong visibility

[4143] The Armed Forces' new commitments create the conditions for a different perspective, even on the part of the press, which is particularly interested in military missions abroad

[4144] This is why the military must review their way of communicating, acquiring the tools necessary to professionally manage the "mission" that international needs and the nation require of them

[4145] Likewise, an increasingly high level of professionalism is essential at the national level as well and is indeed required by those laws that have recently revolutionized the way we understand institutional communication

[4146] The current communications structure of the Armed Forces In defining the new organizational structure of the Defense, ample space was dedicated to the creation of a Public Information and Recruitment Promotion Network designed to maintain the image of the Armed Forces and promote recruitment

[4147] The Network's nationwide deployment is implemented within the pre-existing organizational structure, in which each Agency, Section, or Office reports directly to the immediately superior Command Body

[4148] Each territorial Public Information structure, while acting according to the directives issued by the respective General Staff, or by the immediately superior Command (in any case always subject to prior approval by the central bodies), enjoys a certain autonomy within the territory under its jurisdiction

[4149] In fact, in addition to promotional activities for recruitment, it also manages relationships with public information bodies at the local level

[4150] The territorial press officer is responsible for communicating directly with journalists and therefore providing the responses they expect in real time. The Public Information Service of the Ministry of Defense, formerly called the Press Office of the Minister of Defense (circular dated October 14, 1950, signed by the Minister of Defense pro-tempore, the Hon. Randolfo Pacciardi), has assumed, with the new structure of the Cabinet of the Minister of Defense, the role of an office that directly collaborates with the Minister himself, as it is responsible for Defense communications policy

[4151] The Head of the Press Office of the Minister's Office is the Head of the Public Information Service of the Ministry of Defense and, as such, issues provisions in the public information sector and guides the public information activities of the central and peripheral bodies

[4152] The Press Office, divided into five Sections and a Secretariat, carries out various tasks

[4153] First, it promptly informs the Minister and the Chief of Staff of news reported by national and foreign media

[4154] prepares the daily press review

[4155] prepares and coordinates news of military interest for the “Televideo” and “Internet” services, regulating the methods and times of publication

[4156] prepares and disseminates press releases, news and statements regarding the Minister

[4157] Ensures information dissemination regarding the Minister's activities at national, international, and NATO levels; directs and coordinates, in accordance with the Minister's directives, the Ministry's public information activities, also making use of the central and peripheral public information bodies of the Armed Forces

[4158] Furthermore, it coordinates the entire editorial activity of the Defense by monitoring and authorizing, on behalf of the Minister, the publication of articles in military magazines

[4159] prepares documentary files on the occasion of the Minister's interventions in Italy or abroad

[4160] Organizes - subject to the Minister's approval - press conferences, seminars, and conventions; examines and authorizes requests for collaboration and the provision of personnel and resources from radio and television stations and film studios; coordinates, subject to the Minister's approval, initiatives aimed at increasing interest in the issues and activities of the Armed Forces throughout the country

[4161] Finally, it submits to the Minister for approval the national initiatives for promotional activities in favor of enlistments

[4162] requests for interviews with the Chiefs of Staff and the heads of the Armed Forces and all initiatives proposed by the General Staffs in the field of Public Information

[4163] Very often, news disseminated by public information organizations takes on political significance, involving the competence and responsibility of the Head of the Ministry

[4164] Hence the need for coordination capable of shifting the information process from the center to the periphery and vice versa, according to a process in which the Authority is constantly informed of all communication activities and, if necessary, issues the required authorizations

[4165] For this to happen, the Central and Peripheral Public Information Bodies in the Defense sector must comply with specific directives and carry out the required tasks

[4166] The Central Bodies deal with news regarding the activities of the Chiefs of Staff, the Secretary General/DNA and the Armed Forces as a whole

[4167] they disseminate press releases, denials or clarifications, subject to authorization from the Minister

[4168] They participate in national and international exhibition activities and collaborate with institutions, institutes and organizations for the development of statistical, historical, sociological and scientific studies regarding the Armed Forces

[4169] The Peripheral Bodies (Press Officers of High Commands and other Bodies), on the other hand, deal with news published by the local press of political and/or military interest at the national level, and/or which strictly concern the technicalmilitary activity of the Peripheral Commands and Bodies

[4170] Public Information for the Armed Forces is managed by the Public Information Office of the Defence General Staff (UPI), which, among other things, oversees operational public information and produces the magazine "Informazioni della Difesa." The following Armed Forces components report to the UPI, and therefore to the Chief of the Defence General Staff: the Public Information Agency (API) for the Army, the External Relations Office for Documentation of Promotional Activities (REDAP) for the Navy, the Public Information Office for the Air Force, and the Public Information Office for the Carabinieri

[4171] The Public Information of the General Secretariat of Defence/DNA is the responsibility of the Public Information Service of the Secretary General/DNA

[4172] The information and communication activities of Public Administrations The performance of information and communication activities by Public Administrations was taken into consideration by the legislator with Legislative Decree no. 29 of 3 February

[4173] The ordinary legislator, also with the aim of implementing the principles of transparency and effectiveness of administrative action, subsequently intervened with Law No. 150 of 7 June 2000, "Regulation of the information and communication activities of Public Administrations," published in the Official Journal No. 136 of 13 June

[4174] Law 150 establishes the rules that the Public Administration must follow in the preparation and communication of information to citizens, both by identifying forms, tools, communication products and training methods, and by regulating the structures of the offices responsible for communication activities

[4175] The law, also having to address the requirements that public sector personnel must possess to perform information and communication functions, has delegated this task to a regulatory source

[4176] Article 5, in fact, provides for the adoption of a regulation to identify the qualifications for personnel to be used for information and communication activities and to regulate training interventions for those personnel already carrying out these activities

[4177] The law aims to ensure that press office and public relations staff acquire a high level of professionalism while allowing the Public Administration to have adequate internal human resources for communications tasks

[4178] The framework of the Implementing Regulation is therefore divided into two areas

[4179] the standard discipline (24 months after the entry into force of the regulation), which concerns the qualifications that will be required for personnel to be used for information and communication activities

[4180] the transitional provisions, which concern the training activities prescribed for those who, although already carrying out institutional communication activities and therefore having a certain amount of experience in the sector, nevertheless lack the adequately updated knowledge tools to fulfill their role by developing new communication techniques

[4181] Article 9 of Law 150/2000 states that Press Offices are staffed by personnel registered in the National Register of Journalists

[4182] Registration in the Register of Journalists is required for the Head of the Press Office and for those who assist him in carrying out his institutional functions

[4183] The debate over whether or not certain tasks should be performed by journalists long predates the law

[4184] It is widely believed that a journalist is better suited to the role of press officer, for two main reasons: • membership in a professional association gives them greater bargaining power and autonomy, especially in dealings with senior management within their administration, who more often than not have no experience in institutional communications; • practicing the same profession, albeit in different fields, offers the two sides—that of service information and that of market information—common ground, including technical and cultural, which facilitates the relationship

[4185] Furthermore, it allows you to identify and implement targeted "communication strategies" to address contingent problems or long-term events

[4186] Finally, the journalistic specificity of the press officer's job presupposes a knowledge of the world of information

[4187] especially the market one

[4188] And this knowledge is not based only on daily viewing of agencies and newspapers or television news, but also requires the ability to perceive the trends of journalism, that is, the editorial policies that underlie the "information product

[4189] The approval of Law 150/2000 and the issuance of the resulting Implementing Regulation therefore require a timely adaptation of the Ministry of Defense's Public Information structures

[4190] Currently, in fact, with a few exceptions, in the Defence press offices only a very limited number of officers possess the requirements established by law and the personnel to be employed in the press offices are taken from other functions/specializations and "transferred" without receiving any prior training

[4191] The problem of lack of training also concerns the figures of the editors responsible for the Armed Forces magazines

[4192] The anomaly was remedied, in agreement with the National Order of Journalists, by resorting to registration in a Special List of Editors-in-Chief not registered with the Order itself, which, however, has repeatedly recommended regularizing the position”

[4193] For the sake of completeness, it seems appropriate to mention the different levels of preparation of PI personnel in two European countries

[4194] In Germany, IP is delegated to the PAOs (Public Affairs Officers, there are 28 throughout the country) who are the territorial spokespersons (Military Districts, HQs, Military Regions and Schools

[4195] To be designated PAO, Officers must have full command of the English language and have attended a specific six-week course at the Academy for Information and Communication (AIK) and 4 weeks of practice in newspapers, TV and radio

[4196] In France, the Ministry of Defense has given Public Information a leading role by establishing, on July 27, 1998, the DICoD (Delegation for the Information and Communication of the Defense department) with the specific task of strengthening the link between public opinion and the Armed Forces, of promoting the image of the latter, of coordinating and disseminating information and communications relating to the Ministry of Defense, of representing the Ministry of Defense in relations with the media

[4197] Before being employed in the IP, military personnel must have attended a theoretical-practical course at a journalism school, passed the exams and completed a period of internship in newspapers, TV and radio

[4198] In the immediate future, France plans to open an institute for the education and training of all its personnel in the field of IP, with particular attention to personnel (military and journalists) who will then be employed in theaters of operation

[4199] Sporting activities in the Armed Forces. General information

[4200] Physical preparation is the basic element of military training

[4201] Consequently, sporting activity must be a constant in maintaining the fighter's physical fitness

[4202] This objective must be pursued gradually but continuously, starting from the initial phase of military training, continuing with maintenance activities for the majority of military personnel and with greater intensity for those members who perform high-level competitive activity

[4203] In this context, gymnastic activity in the Armed Forces has been divided into two categories

[4204] the mass one, which has a competitive conclusion in the military field, and the conservative one, reserved for a few elements of specific interest, which has the aim of “preserving” the prominent athletes for the national sporting heritage for the so-called “excellence” competitions

[4205] Mass physical activity develops gradually, from the moment of incorporation, according to diversified programs prepared by the General Staffs of each Armed Force

[4206] It initially involves all military personnel who, through competitions in units of increasingly higher level, are selected to finally participate in the Interforce Military Championships, in which thousands of young people compete annually in various sporting disciplines

[4207] Below is a list of the main joint competitions held during the year

[4208] TABLE 12.2.3 Conservative activity for competitive sport Athletes deemed by CONI to be of "clear national interest", who perform military service, are brought together at the Interforce Sports Centres and/or the CAGSE (Army Sports and Gymnastics Training Centre) where intense sporting activity is practiced in the various sectors of interest using qualified technicians and appropriate equipment

[4209] This is also valid, in this phase of transition to the professional Armed Forces, for soldiers still performing their military service

[4210] Naturally, this "conservative" activity allows us to select the most talented young people for participation in military competitive activities planned at national and international level

[4211] On the international level, competitive activity is mainly expressed through participation in: military world championships organised by the International Military Sports Council (CISM), which includes 122 countries and of which Italy has been a member since 1949; regional events in the European and Mediterranean area

[4248] Combatant and Armed Forces Associations The free associative phenomenon among ex-military personnel is the one that more evidently and more spontaneously than any other possible cultural, promotional and propagandistic activity, reveals the deep popular roots of the Italian Armed Forces, their entirely democratic nature, their interpenetration with the civic and family traditions of Italians

[4249] The activities carried out by the Associations, according to the statutory provisions, aim to morally support the Armed Forces and to strengthen the bonds of solidarity between serving and retired personnel, through the holding of national, regional and provincial gatherings which involve, with growing interest, the civilian population

[4250] Furthermore, in agreement with local administrations and with the support of the Ministry, they promote ceremonies and events to celebrate key moments and dates in the history of the country

[4251] Further activity is significantly increasing in the area of interventions in cases of public disasters and in voluntary participation in public order services in front of schools

[4252] Most of the Associations (listed in the table) have recently been gathered together in the Permanent National Council of Armed Forces Associations (ASSOARMA), in order to consolidate this immense moral heritage. LIST OF COMBAT AND ARMS ASSOCIATIONS 12.4 Military Museums

[4253] Military museums are those entrusted to the management of personnel of the Armed Forces

[4254] Military museums collect centuries-old testimonies of a world that has characterized the evolution of the Armed Forces from their origins to the present day

[4255] The main purpose of museums is to collect and preserve memorabilia that contribute to highlighting and illustrating the history of an Armed Force and its Corps within the context of Italian history

[4256] It is worth highlighting that, following the recent reorganization of the Armed Forces, intended to distinguish the operational component from the territorial one, the Italian Army has provided for a new organization for Weapon/Corps Museums which no longer depend on the territorially closest Operational Command (Regiment), but on a Regional Territorial Command

[4257] A few exceptions have been made, when the Military Museum stands on the site of the Operational Command

[4258] There are also relationships between the Armed Forces Associations and the Military Museums

[4259] In particular, it is highlighted that, within the scope of the Museums' specific objectives, the staff of said Associations promote (at said facilities) knowledge of Military History, as well as the Association's specific functions

[4260] Shrine of the Flags at the Vittoriano

[4261] The Shrine of the Flags at the Vittoriano is located in Rome in Piazza Venezia

[4262] The monumental area collects and preserves the war flags of disbanded departments, of decommissioned naval units, as well as the flags of military institutes and units belonging to the disbanded state armed forces

[4263] The complex also includes the Shrine of the Unknown Soldier, where the unidentified remains of a soldier who fell during the First World War were buried during a solemn ceremony on November 4, 1921. Army Museums

[4288] General Commissioner for Honours to the Fallen in War

[4289] Historical notes and institutional duties A law enacted in 1951 (no. 204, dated 9 January 1951) entrusted a General Commissioner for Honours to the Fallen in War, reporting directly to the Minister of Defence, with the task of providing for the "census, research, temporary placement and subsequent definitive placement of the remains of military, militarized and civilian personnel who died as a consequence of the war from 10 June 1940 to 15 April

[4290] This provision replaced the previous ones issued in 1919, 1931 and 1935 respectively

[4291] The aforementioned law was followed by the regulations and provisions for war cemeteries (law of 20 February 1981, no. 31) and the law of 2 March 1985, no. 60 which expanded the powers of the General Commissioner

[4292] In particular, the General Commissioner's Office provides for

[4293] census of the burials of Italian war dead, research and definitive placement of their remains in burial grounds in Italy and abroad

[4294] • dissemination of information on the Fallen, burial places, possibility of transferring the mortal remains

[4295] arrangement, maintenance and custody of the military shrines and cemeteries of the State property in Italy

[4358] Summary of possible evolutionary lines in defense The analysis of the restructuring process of the Armed Forces cannot conclude without some considerations aimed at identifying the factors that influence the further evolution of the military structure

[4359] The first consideration, undoubtedly positive, is that the "reduction" effort prescribed by the December 1995 financial law has been completed in its general outline

[4360] The second consideration, also positive, is that the chain of command found its proper definition with the law on the reform of the top management of February 1997 and with its Implementing Regulation of October

[4361] The third consideration, also positive, is that compulsory conscription has been suspended, meaning that the Armed Forces, within four or five years, will be made up entirely of professional soldiers, for a total of 190,000 men and women

[4362] This is thanks to the law of November 2000 and the subsequent Legislative Decree of May 2001. The fourth consideration, of a completely different nature, as it is not linked to regulatory considerations but rather to the evolution of the international security framework, requires an in-depth analysis of the "state of the art," that is, a verification of what has been done and whether what has been done responds to the nation's new security needs

[4363] The overall total for the Army, given the turnover requirements that are bordering on acceptability, would be 9-10 Brigades and, since the Army plays a major role in the development of such operations, it must be recognized that it would be desirable to increase the availability of ground forces up to the current 12-13 Brigades

[4364] To achieve this, given the financial and personnel impossibility of achieving this goal, all that remains is to review the structure of the 112,000 men and women made available by current legislation, reducing or eliminating intermediate structures whose functions can be reabsorbed by the Armed Forces General Staffs and studying a different command architecture, to be further explored through "benchmarking" operations between the General Staffs and with the General Command of the Carabinieri

[4365] A similar analysis would be appropriate regarding the size of the Brigades (Light Brigades or Heavy Brigades?) and the creation of a joint Special Forces unit

[4366] At the same time, the Defence General Staff, which has rightly assumed the preeminent role in the joint conception of the military instrument, should take on all those functions that are divided, but also repeated and overlapping, between the Armed Forces General Staffs and some General Directorates

[4367] specifically, this refers to healthcare, police stations, supplies, infrastructure, transport and recruitment

[4368] Furthermore, given that the need for territorial control has increased, it would be appropriate to focus efforts solely on choices arising from national security and commitments to the UN, NATO, and the EU, avoiding the dispersal of human and financial resources in other international structures

[4369] Finally, it is necessary to ensure that the aforementioned commitments correspond to the support of adequate financial resources and logistical structures to maintain the efficiency of the means, provide the necessary equipment and training, and renew and modernize the materials and weapons systems worn out by so much use

[4370] Furthermore, in the inevitable review of all activities deriving from agreements outside of those of a fundamental nature (i.e., NATO and the EU), the willingness to take into consideration any cooperation needs, especially bilateral ones, dictated by contingent situations or training needs, may remain firm

[4371] In light of these considerations, it seems necessary to reopen the discussion of restructuring the Ministry of Defense to achieve, through an internal reorganization of structures and resources, a higher level of operational efficiency commensurate with the needs of national and international security

[4372] In short, it is within the structures of the Armed Forces that solutions can and must be found to save resources, personnel, and infrastructure

[4373] The renovation is not complete and efforts must continue to seek better architecture

[4431] Summary of possible evolutionary lines on personnel Personnel problems are many and have been addressed mainly in terms of the functionality of the tool, sometimes neglecting the human aspect which in any case affects functionality as it can cause disorientation and demotivation

[4433] This specifically concerns: reducing transition times for the end of military service; finding the most effective ways to ensure volunteers' entry into the workforce; implementing economic measures to facilitate the exodus of redundant personnel and improving emoluments for those who remain; reinstating command periods as an essential testing ground for promotions; revising the composition of promotion committees to ensure impartiality; enforcing, without exception, age limits for each rank; promoting the new law on military representation; and redundancy in the bodies responsible for personnel management in general and the volunteer recruitment system

[4471] On the other hand, continuous commitment is natural, necessary and indispensable to achieve results "in the medal zone

[4472] Therefore, Carabinieri, Financiers, State Police Agents and Forestry Corps are always at the top of the rankings of athletes in uniform

[4473] The transition to a professional Armed Forces could offer greater potential for results for the Army, Navy, and Air Force over time, but at the same time, precisely because of the significant reduction in these numbers, it will be necessary to approach preparation for competitive activity with a joint vision

[4474] Consequently, Sports Centers will have to acquire the "multi-arm" characteristic by bringing together athletes who practice the same sporting discipline regardless of the Armed Forces they belong to

[4475] It is also considered appropriate to focus attention on the phenomenon of “athletes” in uniform, who only engage in sporting activities without setting foot in the barracks or undergoing any operational training

[4476] A standardization effort in this sector could lead to a proper reconciliation of sporting ethics with military ethics

[4477] With the reduction in military personnel due to the professionalization of the Armed Forces, the entire sector is currently being studied by the Defence General Staff to find a solution that will allow the publicity and full maintenance of the museum activity, both in terms of the conservation of the assets contained therein and to guarantee attendance by the public

[4478] The possibility of establishing a single military museum in Rome, following the example of what has been achieved in Paris, London and Brussels, is also being studied

[4479] The initiative should be seen as part of the historical-commemorative path advocated by the Head of State from 2001 to 2011, the year in which the 150th anniversary of the constitution of the Italian State will be celebrated
